rows.key_quote: Merger-announcement call that also covered both companies' Q3 results. Array reported Q3 revenue of $330 million (including one month of AWM; $321 million excluding), adjusted gross margin of 22.8% including a 330 bps charge for a 45X rebate reserve, and adjusted EBITDA of $32 million (10% margin), with a record $2.6 billion order book up 42% YoY and book-to-bill of 1.6x. Shoals reported record revenue of $195.3 million, up 44% YoY, gross margin of 31.9% (up 160 bps QoQ), adjusted EBITDA of about $40 million (20.4% margin), and $186 million of new orders, with results above its guided range. The deal is stock-for-stock (1.6931 Array shares per Shoals share, Shoals holders owning about 65%), targets $100 million of annual synergies by year three, includes $161.3 million of preferred redemption within 90 days, and carries a preliminary 2027 outlook of $2.2-2.4 billion revenue and $410-480 million adjusted EBITDA against a $3.4 billion backlog.

H1 FY2027 operating income was JPY 2.2 trillion on sales of JPY 26.96 trillion, with net income of JPY 2.24 trillion; OI rose year-on-year as cost reduction, price revisions, value-chain profits and tariff mitigation offset Middle East disruption and material costs. Toyota revised full-year operating income guidance up JPY 500 billion to JPY 3.9 trillion, with revenue forecast at JPY 53.5 trillion on FX assumptions of JPY 157/USD and EUR 182. Consolidated vehicle sales fell 25,000 units YoY (but rose 26,000 ex-Hino), while Toyota/Lexus unit sales fell to 96% of the prior year on weak China demand and the Middle East, and the electrified ratio reached 55.6%. Shareholder returns were expanded: interim dividend of JPY 50 (up JPY 5), FY dividend of JPY 100, buyback authorization raised JPY 300 billion to JPY 1.3 trillion, and an additional 1 billion treasury shares cancelled.

Westlake reported Q3 2026 sales of $3.0 billion and EBITDA of $408 million, up from $313 million a year ago but down sharply from $679 million sequentially. PEM EBITDA rose $125 million YoY to $215 million on an 11% margin, but fell roughly $201 million sequentially as PVC and polyethylene prices retreated from Q2 conflict-driven highs, and HIP EBITDA fell $20 million YoY to $195 million with margin down to 18% from 20%. Q4 HIP guidance is $900 million-$1 billion revenue at a ~13% EBITDA margin, reflecting a typical 4-5 point seasonal decline, while 2026 capex guidance was trimmed $50 million to $850 million. Management flagged a challenging 2027 for housing, ~6% global polyethylene capacity additions in 2027, and European energy costs still rising (German power above EUR 200/MWh).

Qnity reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.6 billion, representing a 22% year-over-year increase and 9% sequential growth. Adjusted EPS rose 55% year-over-year to $1.46, while adjusted gross margin expanded 270 bps to 47.8%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by $200 million and adjusted EPS by $0.50 at the midpoint.

Zimmer Biomet reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $2.063 billion, up 3.1% reported and 3.7% constant currency (4.7% ex-China distributor consolidation), with hips +7%, S.E.T. +7.1%, and technology/data +13% offsetting knees down 2.6%. Adjusted EPS was $1.90, flat year-over-year, as adjusted gross margin fell 90 bps to 71.7% and adjusted operating margin fell 140 bps to 25.1% on U.S. sales force investment; GAAP EPS was $1.00 versus $1.16. Management raised full-year organic constant currency growth guidance to 3.0%-3.5% from 2.25%-3.25% and adjusted EPS to $8.50-$8.60 from $8.47-$8.59, with full-year adjusted gross margin now around 72%, 100 bps above prior expectations. Free cash flow was $372 million, up about 34% year-over-year, and the company remains on track for roughly $1 billion of 2026 share repurchases.

Zillow reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $724 million, up 7% YoY, with rentals up 26% to $220 million but for-sale flat at $489 million (residential down 4%). Adjusted EBITDA was $182 million at a 25% margin, up 70 bps YoY, and diluted adjusted EPS was $0.55 versus $0.44 a year ago. For Q4, guidance calls for total revenue of $635-665 million (roughly flat YoY) and EBITDA of $100-135 million (about 18% margin), with the assumption that purchase mortgage industry volumes decline 10%-15%, sharply worse than the prior mid-single-digit decline expectation. Management said it is planning for macro conditions to stay difficult into 2027 and that the mortgage funnel will take time to rebuild.

CLEAR reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $292.9 million, up 27.8% year-over-year, bookings of $323.5 million (+24.4%), adjusted EBITDA of $103.9 million at a 35.5% margin (roughly five points of expansion), and operating income of $82.9 million. Active CLEAR+ members grew 14.5% to 8.5 million and total CLEAR members via CLEAR1 grew 30.7% to 46.7 million, with CLEAR1 bookings near 3x the prior-year quarter. Q4 guidance is revenue of $299-$302 million and bookings of $335-$340 million, excluding potential large CLEAR1 contracts, while full-year free cash flow guidance rose from at least $480 million to at least $490 million. Q3 free cash flow was negative $103.8 million, reflecting the roughly $315 million settlement of accrued partnership liabilities that management says will not recur.

For the third quarter of 2026, revenue was $5.2 million, an increase from $3.7 million in the prior year period driven by license revenue. R&D expenses rose to $35.5 million and SG&A increased to $23.9 million due to recruitment and launch preparation costs. The FDA accepted the BLA for AMT-130 with a PDUFA date of May 1, 2027, and the MHRA validated the MAA in the UK.

Ralliant reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $620 million, a 17% increase year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $0.93 representing a 64% normalized growth. The company delivered on all metrics above the high end of its guidance ranges and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.34 billion-$2.36 billion, an increase of $75 million at the midpoint compared to prior expectations. Management highlighted broad-based demand acceleration across defense, utilities, and industrial markets, supported by a backlog exceeding $1.5 billion in defense and strong organic growth in Test and Measurement.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $55 million, flat versus the prior year quarter, with adjusted revenue (excluding outsourced claims service) rising to $54 million from $52 million. Pre-tax income was about $30 million, EPS $0.25, and Adjusted EBITDA margin exceeded 51%, which management said were within guidance. Managed Premium grew to roughly $1.4 billion from $1.2 billion a year ago and ARR rose to $206 million from $192 million sequentially, while Q4 pre-tax income guidance of $26-29 million was framed as seasonal and Q4 Managed Premium guided to about $1.34 billion, below the Q3 level. Shareholders' equity rose 17% from prior year end to $298 million, and the company repurchased over 1.1 million shares for about $17 million year to date while remaining debt-free.

Red Violet reported a record Q3 FY2026 with revenue of $27.8 million (up 20% YoY) and adjusted net income of $7.3 million (up 23%). The company highlighted strong cash flow generation of $12.7 million and a trailing 12-month revenue surpassing $100 million for the first time. Management noted broad-based growth across all verticals, including accelerated growth in background screening and insurance, while acknowledging softness in IDI's real estate business that is expected to persist until market conditions improve.

Xperi reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $114 million, up 2% YoY, with GAAP net loss of $5.2 million (-$0.11 per share) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.24; adjusted EBITDA was $23 million (20% of revenue), essentially flat versus 21% a year ago, and operating cash flow was $4 million with free cash flow a $3 million use. Media platform revenue more than doubled to $17 million on advertising and related revenue up ~280% to $15 million, while connected car fell 14% to $30 million and consumer electronics fell 28% to $14 million. Annual revenue guidance was narrowed to $450-462 million (midpoint up $1 million), adjusted EBITDA margin was raised two points to 19-21%, and operating cash flow guidance rose $5 million to $20-30 million; management also cut its media platform growth expectation to ~60% and now sees year-end ARPU of $8-10, about 90% of the prior goal at the midpoint. CFO Robert Andersen announced a planned 2027 retirement, and management said it is evaluating buybacks under its existing authorization.

XPEL reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $137.8 million, up 9.9% YoY, with gross margin of 44.6% (up 280 bps YoY and 50 bps QoQ), operating margin 15.3%, EPS of $0.59 and adjusted EPS of $0.62. EBITDA grew 28.3% to $25.3 million and adjusted EBITDA margin reached 18.9%, with SG&A of $40.4 million up 13.3% (about 4% ex-China). Q4 revenue guidance is $125-$127 million, implying sequential decline, reflecting decelerating U.S. aftermarket, a worsening dealership channel, Middle East weakness, and China now on a like-for-like basis, with no formal FY2027 guidance beyond a reiterated medium-term low-double-digit growth ambition. Management flagged the dealership/regulatory impact as likely troughing in Q4 while calling out slowing consumer demand in the U.S. aftermarket.

Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue was $1.0B, down 1% YoY, below expectations due to discontinuing account payout for a large Saudi partner; adjusted operating margin fell to 18% from 20% on mix and higher agent signing bonuses, though it improved sequentially on Beyond Efficiency cost actions. Adjusted EPS of $0.42 beat expectations on expense timing, faster cost savings, and a lower 9% tax rate. Full-year guidance puts organic revenue down 2% to 1% (flat to +1% including Intermex if it closes) and adjusted EPS at $1.28-$1.38, an improvement of $0.03 versus original guidance, but Q4 Branded Digital revenue and transactions will step down as the Saudi payout business is exited. Operating cash flow YTD fell 21% to $321M and buybacks remain paused.

Essential reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $0.36, up 9% from $0.33, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.38 excluding about $0.02 of merger-related costs. EPS gains came from $0.06 of regulatory recoveries and surcharges (roughly 65% water) plus $0.01 from higher water volumes, partly offset by $0.02 each from higher D&A and interest/lower AFUDC; O&M fell 0.6% (~$0.9M) despite $4.9M of merger expenses. Management did not reaffirm long-term EPS guidance, citing the pending American Water merger expected to close by end of Q1 2027, though it maintained a five-year capital plan of at least $8.7 billion and a 2026 record $1.7 billion capex target. In Pennsylvania, an ALJ context about $105 million of the $163.2 million gas rate request, with a final order expected in December.

MercadoLibre reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue and financial income up 41% YoY FX-neutral, with Brazil GMV +36% and items per buyer +16%. Income from operations was $676 million at a 6.3% margin, down 40 bps QoQ, driven by ~60 bps of shipping headwind (20% fulfillment capacity expansion, lower free-shipping threshold, energy costs, temps) and 40 bps higher S&M (11.6% of revenue) from Brazil affiliate investment. Fintech grew strongly (MAU +29%, AUM +67%, credit book +62%) with 15-90 NPLs stable at 7%; advertising grew 58% and acquiring 42%. Management framed the margin compression as deliberate investment, gave no explicit forward guidance, and said it does not target a specific short-term margin; some shipping cost is expected to partially return in Q4 while energy pressure remains.

Pattern reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $886 million, up 38% year-over-year (approx. 42% adjusted for timing shifts), and Adjusted EBITDA of $57 million, a 40% increase. Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to approximately $3.5 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to roughly $220 million, citing strong Net Revenue Retention (NRR) of 127% and record new brand partnerships. The company highlighted significant growth in non-Amazon revenue (+86%) and international revenue (+56%), while maintaining a net cash position with no debt.

Q3 FY2026 revenue came in at EUR 24.2M, below the guided EUR 29-31M range, up 1% QoQ but down 32% YoY, while gross margin of 36.5% missed the 38-40% guide on DC product mix. Adjusted EBITDA loss of EUR 5.3M improved 32% QoQ and 24% YoY and landed within the guided range, and opex fell 34% YoY. Backlog rose to EUR 16.9M from EUR 12M, which management cites as visibility for a reacceleration once supply constraints ease. Q4 guidance is EUR 29-31M revenue, 36-38% gross margin, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of EUR 5.5-3.5M, with no raise versus prior periods. Cash fell to EUR 10.4M from EUR 25.1M at June 30, partly on restructuring payments.

Remitly reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $510 million, up 22% year-over-year and $4 million above the midpoint of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $121 million at a record 24% margin. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $1.989 billion and $1.991 billion (22% growth) and provided an early look at 2027 revenue growth in the high teens, citing strong cohort stability and AI-driven efficiency as key drivers.

Eco Wave Power reported Q3 2026 net loss of $529,000, down ~47% from $996,000 a year earlier, with operating loss narrowing ~25% to $666,000 and net financial income of $137,000 versus a $108,000 expense in Q3 2025. Nine-month net loss fell ~24% to ~$2.2 million, R&D dropped ~48% to $310,000, and cash plus short-term deposits totaled ~$7.68 million (~$7.43 million excluding restricted). No revenue, EPS, or formal financial guidance was disclosed; the company is pre-commercial and framed priorities around cost discipline plus project milestones in India (first BPCL purchase order for site assessment), Portugal (1 MW Porto concession, construction targeted for 2027), and the U.S. The quarter's substantive change was commercial progression from MOUs to a paid assessment order and an early licensing discussion for a potential up-to-60 MW Port of Los Angeles project.

Wayfair reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue growth of 9.7% YoY, with U.S. revenue up 11.4% and international down 2.3%. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.9% ($236 million) and net income was $62 million, a $160 million improvement YoY, while gross margin was 29.6% as advertising fell to 9.9% of revenue. Q4 guidance calls for high single-digit revenue growth and Adjusted EBITDA margin of 6%-7%, with gross margin targeted at the lower end of 29.5%-30.5%. Management emphasized U.S. share gains now in the double digits and compounding order growth, but noted the category remains flat and macro conditions unchanged.

Bristow reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue up ~$26 million and Adjusted EBITDA up ~$10 million sequentially, with the BSM acquisition (closed July) contributing $16.9 million of government services revenue and $9.2 million of other services revenue. Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint was reaffirmed at ~$310 million (~25% YoY growth), while segment ranges were revised: OES adjusted operating income guidance raised to $240-$250 million on 27% segment margins, and government services revenue set to $470-$490 million with adjusted operating income cut to $35-$45 million. The core negative is that aircraft availability penalties from OEM supply chain delays continue to depress government services margins and are now expected to stabilize only by the end of Q1 2027. Capital returns continued with $25 million of buybacks (550,000 shares at $45.64) and a $0.125 dividend.

Vishay reported record quarterly revenue of $979 million, above the $945-975 million guidance range, up 6.6% sequentially (adjusted) and 24% year-over-year on 20% volume and 4% ASP growth. Gross margin was 25.5%, up over 200 bps sequentially, and operating margin rose to 9.4% from 5.8% in Q2, with EPS of $0.37 versus $0.19 in Q2. Q4 guidance is $990 million +/- $15 million and gross margin of 26.0% +/- 50 bps, which management said exceeds its goal of exiting the year at 24% quarterly gross margin by 200 bps. Backlog reached $2.2 billion (6.6 months) with book-to-bill of 1.29, and full-year free cash flow is now expected near break-even given a planned reduction of the receivables securitization program.

Viridian reported $24.7 million in first-quarter Lumvoa net product revenue with more than 100 patients on therapy as of September 30, a launch management characterized as exceeding expectations. The company ended Q3 with just over $955 million in cash and reiterated its target of broad payer coverage six to nine months from launch, disclosing it had policies in place covering 30% of lives as of quarter-end, with a permanent J-code effective January 1, 2027. Management declined to give Q4 revenue or patient guidance but said it expects growth into the fourth quarter and does not see the demand as a bolus. On the pipeline, the elegrobart BLA remains on track for Q1 2027, with VRDN-008 first-in-human data and a VRDN-292 Phase I start expected later this quarter.

VPG reported adjusted Q3 FY2026 revenue of $87.4 million (GAAP $85.1 million after $2.3 million of tariff refunds passed to customers), up 4% sequentially and 10% year-over-year, the highest level in three years. Adjusted gross margin improved to 39.3% from 38.6% in Q2, while adjusted EPS of $0.14 was dampened by a 48% adjusted tax rate that cut roughly $0.03 per share versus the prior run rate. Orders of $103 million produced a 1.17 consolidated book-to-bill (Sensors 1.35, a second consecutive record), and management guided Q4 revenue to $84–91 million while introducing a 2027 outlook of 10%–12% growth, above the three-year plan's annual target. Humanoid robotics remains small at ~$200,000 of bookings and $300,000 of sales as the initial customer pushed its production ramp to Q4.

A clinical-stage biotech quarter with no product revenue; Q3 FY2026 R&D expense was $80 million versus $151 million a year ago (prior year included a one-time $75 million VIR-5525 milestone), and SG&A was $24 million versus $22 million. Cash and investments ended at $901 million, excluding the $90 million Gilead upfront received in October, with runway projected into the second half of 2028. The Gilead preclinical collaboration brought $65 million upfront plus a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium, up to $45 million in near-term preclinical milestones, up to $1.74 billion in later milestones, and tiered high-single to low-double-digit royalties, with the Sanofi 20% pass-through having expired. No financial guidance was given; key catalysts are ECLIPSE 1 top-line data this quarter and ECLIPSE 2/3 in Q1 2027, while the VIR-5818 data update slipped from this year after FDA feedback on the monotherapy arm.

Q3 net sales rose 7% YoY to $2.45B, but adjusted net sales growth excluding commodity pass-through and FX was only ~1%, against a ~2% decline in global auto production. Adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to $275M with margin up 40 bps to 11.2%, while net income fell to $102M from $109M on higher interest expense and free cash flow dipped to $170M from $179M. Full-year adjusted net sales growth guidance was unchanged at ~2% and EBITDA midpoint held at $990M, with the sales midpoint raised solely on higher copper pass-throughs; free cash flow guidance midpoint rose $50M to $300M. Regional weakness in EMEA (adjusted sales -8%) was offset by Asia-Pacific 9% adjusted growth and Americas 1%.

Vermilion reported Q3 fund flows from operations of CAD 237 million on E&D capex of CAD 146 million, generating over CAD 90 million of free cash flow, while paying CAD 21 million in dividends and repurchasing CAD 20 million of shares. Full-year 2026 production is guided to 122,400 BOE/d on CAD 620 million of capex, above the original midpoint of guidance despite Australia downtime and Canadian gas deferrals, with Q4 production expected at 121,000 BOE/d and European gas near 100 MMcf/d as turnarounds complete. The newly released 2027 budget sets E&D capital of CAD 675-725 million for 122,000-126,000 BOE/d (~2% absolute, 5% per-share growth), and the 2027 base dividend rises 4% to CAD 0.56 per share. Negatives include the Montney 28,000 BOE/d target slipping to early 2029 from mid-2028 on third-party processing timing and a flat European gas outlook for 2027 versus 2026.

Third quarter net revenues increased to $944 million from $931 million in the prior year, driven by pricing actions that offset volume declines and commodity inflation. Adjusted EPS was $0.39 compared to $0.42 last year, resulting in a sequential miss on earnings while revenue beat expectations. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for net revenues of +1% to +3% and adjusted EBITDA of $660 million-$675 million without revision.

Vertex reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $213.3 million, up 11% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $64.8 million (up ~50% YoY, ~$8M above the high end) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 30.4%. ARR rose 11.7% to $724.3 million, cloud revenue growth accelerated to over 20%, and non-GAAP gross margin expanded 370 bps to 77.6%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $828.9-$830.9 million (midpoint up $2.4 million) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $217.9-$219.9 million (midpoint up $10.9 million), though it flagged a discrete payroll OEM loss expected to reduce Q4 GRR and NRR by about one point.

Weyco reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $77 million, up 5% YoY, with wholesale up 6% to $64 million and retail up 3% to $7.2 million; Florsheim Australia fell 3% (down 10% in local currency). GAAP diluted EPS was $1.19 versus $0.69, with consolidated gross margin of 49.7% including $3.3 million of tariff refunds recognized in cost of sales, and operating earnings rose to $13.7 million from $8.1 million. No numeric guidance was issued, but management flagged near-term gross margin uncertainty from tariffs and supply-chain inflation, and said it does not want to raise wholesale prices given a stretched consumer. The board declared a regular $0.28 quarterly dividend plus a $2.00 special dividend, and inventory is being rebuilt toward roughly $70 million by year-end from $60 million.

Q3 revenue rose 7% YoY to $724 million, with rentals up 26% to $220 million and multifamily up 35%, while for-sale revenue was flat at $489 million (residential down 4% to $419 million, mortgages up 32% to $70 million). EBITDA was $182 million at a 25% margin, up 70 bps YoY, and diluted adjusted EPS was $0.55 versus $0.44 a year ago. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $635-665 million, roughly flat YoY, with for-sale and residential revenue each down 9-15% as the company cut its industry purchase origination assumption to a 10-15% decline from prior mid-single digits. Full-year 2026 revenue growth is guided to about 10-11% with flat EBITDA margins.

Riot Platforms reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $181 million (up 1% YoY) and GAAP net income of $4 million ($0.01/share), driven by a $172 million gain on Bitcoin fair value which offset lower mining revenue due to a 38% price decline. The company announced the signing of its largest lease in history, a 15-year triple-net deal for 910 MW at Corsicana with Frontier AI Lab, alongside progress on Rockdale and AMD expansions. Management raised full-year NOI expectations to exceed $2.2 billion annually upon full deployment, citing strong liquidity ($950 million) and no equity raises in 2026.

Avnet reported record Q1 FY2027 sales of $10.7 billion, up 82% YoY (71% excluding the extra week), and record adjusted EPS of $3.63, both well above the high end of guidance. Adjusted operating margin expanded more than 200 bps YoY to 4.7%, the fifth consecutive quarter of expansion, with EC at 4.8% and Farnell back to a double-digit 10.1% operating margin. Q2 guidance of $11.1-11.4 billion in sales and $3.90-4.10 in adjusted EPS implies about 12% sequential growth on a comparable basis, well above typical seasonality, but the guide assumes flat-ish memory pricing versus the ~one-third of Q1 growth that came from memory pricing. Working capital absorbed $842 million of operating cash, driving a $950 million debt increase and gross leverage at 3.1x.

PFG reported Q1 FY27 net sales growth of 5.5% with all three segments contributing, total cases up 4.2% and organic independent restaurant case growth of 5.5%. Gross profit rose 8.5% with 33 bps of gross margin expansion, adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to $528 million (upper end of guidance), adjusted EPS rose 11.9% to $1.32, and net income rose 38.4% to $129.5 million. Full-year guidance was reiterated at $72.5-$73 billion in sales and $2.125-$2.225 billion in adjusted EBITDA, with Q2 guided to $17.0-$17.2 billion in sales and $490-$510 million in adjusted EBITDA; Foodservice inflation is now expected at the bottom of the low single-digit range versus prior expectations. Headwinds include persistent elevated fuel (roughly $16 million net Q1 impact, similar expected in Q2), non-recurring prior-year candy inventory gains and margin pressure in Specialty, and Convenience growth normalizing to low single digits as it laps Love's and RaceTrac, with a back-half step-up tied to Jersey Mike's onboarding in February.

News Corp reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $2.3 billion, up 6% year-over-year, and total segment EBITDA of $403 million, up 19%, with margins expanding 180 bps to 17.7%. EPS were $0.29 versus $0.20 and adjusted EPS $0.28 versus $0.22, marking a 14th consecutive quarter of EBITDA growth. Dow Jones revenue rose 8% to $630 million (EBITDA +11% to $160 million, margin 25.4%), Digital Real Estate revenue rose 10% to $529 million (EBITDA +34% to $212 million), and Book Publishing revenue rose 9% to $582 million with EBITDA up 29%. News Media revenue fell 1% to $540 million with EBITDA down $12 million to $18 million, and management gave a qualitative outlook (continued Dow Jones margin expansion, Realtor.com revenue growth, higher Book Publishing costs, similar News Media trends) without formal numeric guidance; October REA listings were down 13% year-over-year.

News Corp reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $2.3 billion, up 6% YoY, with total segment EBITDA up 19% to $403 million and margins expanding 180 bps to 17.7%. EPS were $0.29 versus $0.20 a year ago, and adjusted EPS $0.28 versus $0.22, marking a 14th consecutive quarter of YoY EBITDA growth. Growth engines Dow Jones (revenue +8%, EBITDA +11%), Digital Real Estate (revenue +10%, EBITDA +34%), and Book Publishing (revenue +9%, EBITDA +29%) collectively grew segment EBITDA 24%, offsetting News Media revenue down 1% and EBITDA down $12 million to $18 million. Guidance was qualitative rather than a raised numeric range: continued Dow Jones revenue growth and margin expansion, continued Realtor.com revenue growth, and broadly similar News Media trends, with October REA listings down 13% YoY.

Power Integrations reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $125.5 million, up 6% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS rising 28% to $0.46. The company beat its gross margin outlook and reduced inventory by over $7 million, though channel stock rose to 11.8 weeks due to soft consumer demand and supply constraints in high-power segments. Management raised the quarterly dividend to $0.22 per share starting Q1 2027 and provided a Q4 revenue guidance range of $118-$126 million.

MSGE reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $217.1M, up 37% year-over-year, and adjusted operating income of $34.3M, up $27.2M from the prior-year quarter, driven by a record number of Garden concerts including 16 Harry Styles residency nights and higher per-concert revenue. Management said its FY2027 bookings financial outlook is stronger than what it communicated in August, expects record Christmas Spectacular revenue on 231 shows (vs 215) and over 1.2M guests, and reiterated expectations for robust full-year revenue and AOI growth with significant underlying free cash flow. The company repurchased ~314,000 Class A shares for $25M in the quarter, and noted concert pacing is up in the December quarter at the Garden but down in the back half on timing. Suite license renewal rate exceeded 95% and concert F&B/merch per caps rose double digits year-over-year.

Kennametal reported Q1 FY2027 sales up 54% organically with EPS of $3.48 versus $0.34 adjusted a year ago, but the bulk of the gain was a $3.14 price/raw timing benefit from tungsten rather than underlying operations. Sales and EPS came in above the midpoint of the prior outlook, Metal Cutting delivered a fourth straight quarter of mid-single-digit volume growth, while Infrastructure volumes fell low double digits on price sensitivity, China mining safety-related slowdowns, and limited product substitution. FY2027 sales guidance was maintained at $3.33-3.45 billion, but adjusted EPS was updated to $5-$6 and, with tungsten at ~$2,700, price/cost headwinds now extend into Q4 with an expected low double-digit exit EBITDA margin versus the prior mid-teens expectation. Free operating cash flow was -$212 million versus -$5 million a year ago as inventory values tripled on tungsten costs, and buybacks remain paused.

Jack Henry reported Q1 FY2027 record non-GAAP revenue of $682 million, up 7% year-over-year, exceeding the outlook from August commentary, with non-GAAP operating margin of 28% expanding 102 bps and GAAP EPS of $2.28 up 16%. Management raised full-year non-GAAP revenue growth guidance to 6.6%-7.4% (up from a prior range via a higher bottom end and slight top-end adjustment) and now guides GAAP EPS of $7.47-$7.51, or 7%-8% growth, while reiterating 20-40 bps of margin expansion and 85%-100% free cash flow conversion. Offsets include a deliberate deconversion revenue assumption of $30 million and described first-half margin headwinds from normalized self-insured medical costs plus planned AI, cyber, and EC2030 data center investments; management also flagged lower non-GAAP revenue growth in the second half. The company cited nine competitive core wins (versus four a year ago), 367 Gladiator sales (triple prior year), 93% recurring revenue, and $83 million free cash flow up 19%.

PROCEPT BioRobotics reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $98.3 million (18% YoY growth) and completed 13,400 U.S. procedures (22% YoY growth). The company remained on track to meet its full-year 2026 guidance of $390-$410 million revenue and 54,000-56,000 procedures, with Q4 expected to be EBITDA positive. Gross margin expanded to 66% from 65% in the prior year.

Gold.com reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $3.265 billion, down 11% YoY, but up 51% to $3.15 billion excluding a $1.38 billion decrease in forward sales; gross profit rose 23% to $89.6 million as gross margin expanded to 2.74% from 1.98%, and net income turned to $1.6 million, or $0.05 per share, from a $0.9 million loss. Adjusted pre-tax income jumped 172% to $13.2 million and EBITDA rose 22% to $17.4 million. Volumes declined sequentially (gold ounces down 11%, silver down 9% QoQ), and management described the quarter as the slowest market they had seen in a long time, with buybacks as a percentage of new sales dropping significantly. No explicit forward guidance was provided, but premiums were noted as stable to slightly rising and M&A pipeline described as strong.

Core net sales declined 1.7% year-over-year to $989 million all-in, while core adjusted operating margin decreased 210 basis points to 14.3%. Management updated the full-year outlook to reflect a more measured retailer inventory position ahead of the cough and cold season and continued softness in Europe, resulting in lower guidance for both core and all-in net sales compared to prior expectations.

Primoris reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of just under $2 billion, a decrease of $226 million (10.4%) year-over-year, driven by lower renewables activity and regulatory delays in the Energy segment. Gross profit declined to $204.7 million with a gross margin contraction to 10.5% from 10.8% in the prior quarter. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance to adjusted EPS of $2.10-$2.25, reflecting lower revenue contribution in Q4 and higher effective tax rates.

Coty reported Q1 FY2027 net revenue of $1.56 billion, down 1.6% like-for-like, which was ahead of guidance for a low-to-mid-single-digit decline and ahead of consensus. Adjusted EBITDA was $274 million, down 7% year-on-year, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.6% and adjusted gross margin of 63.3%, both down 120 bps; gross margin came in below the prior expectation of a 50-100 bps decline on higher freight and excess/obsolescence costs. Adjusted EPS ex-swap was $0.15, flat year-on-year and above the $0.11-$0.13 guide, and free cash flow rose $73 million year-on-year to $85 million with net debt down ~$300 million to ~$2.6 billion (~3.1x). Q2 guidance calls for low-single-digit like-for-like revenue decline, high-single-digit EBITDA decline, and EPS of $0.16-$0.18, with FY2027 still framed as a transition year and no full-year framework until the strategic review concludes by end of calendar 2026.

Coherent reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $2.37 billion, up 16% sequentially and 56% year-over-year pro forma, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.09 up 80% year-over-year. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 184 bps year-over-year to 40.6% and operating margin reached 23.2%, while data center revenue grew 85% year-over-year and communications 84%. Q2 guidance of $2.55-$2.75 billion revenue and $2.28-$2.48 EPS implies further sequential acceleration, and management raised its gross margin target to above 45% before the end of calendar 2028, 300 bps above its prior long-term target. The company also disclosed a new ~$20 billion five-year PhotonLink LTA and reiterated a path to a $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of FY2027 and a $4 billion quarter in FY2028.

Net revenue fell 8% YoY to $86.5 million, with product revenue down 26% to $27.3 million on 12 units shipped, driven by China geopolitical headwinds; service revenue grew 4% to $59.2 million. Gross margin rose to 30.1% from 28.8% on a 35.1% service margin (up 410 bps vs FY26 trailing), while adjusted operating loss was $1.1 million excluding a $35.4 million non-cash goodwill impairment, and Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $2.5 million from a $4.1 million loss. Product gross orders were $19.8 million for a 0.7 book-to-bill, below the 1.2 level management calls healthy, and backlog was roughly $272 million. Management gave no formal guidance, citing focus on commercial execution and product volume conversion.

Postal Realty Trust reported Q3 FY2026 AFFO per share of $0.36, which was in line with the prior quarter but represented a three-penny increase year-over-year. Management raised full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to a midpoint of $1.43 per share (range $1.42-$1.44), driven by higher acquisition volume and improved borrowing costs. The company acquired $82 million in postal properties during the quarter, bringing pro forma net debt to run rate Adjusted EBITDA down to 3.5x.

Amcor reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $6.1 billion, up 7% on 1% organic volume growth and pass-through of $316 million in higher resin costs in Global Flexible Packaging; adjusted EBITDA of $883 million was flat ex-divestitures and currency, adjusted EPS of $0.95 was flat year over year in constant currency and at the midpoint of the outlook range. The company lowered its transition-period adjusted EPS guidance to $1.70-$1.80 from $1.80-$1.90, citing late-September acceleration in energy and distribution costs and the timing of pass-through, now sizing the gross hit at $100 million-plus with roughly half offset and recovery expected by end of the December quarter. The board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.66 per share and management still expects double-digit adjusted EPS growth in 2027, positive volumes, and leverage near 3x by year-end 2027, against a $500 million Middle East working capital drag not recovered until end-2027. Volumes were up 1% organically (fourth consecutive sequential improvement), with 3% growth in focus categories and all regions positive, while Rigid Packaging EBIT fell 3% reported and non-core volumes declined low-to-mid single digits.

Pursuit reported record Q3 revenue of $251.5 million, up 4.4% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA growing 7% to $125.5 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance at the midpoint of $133 million (range $130-$136 million), citing strong performance despite weather headwinds and the sale of the Flyover business. The company highlighted margin expansion driven by yield optimization and a fixed cost base, alongside record results from its newly acquired Eagle Wing Tours.

FY2026 net sales rose 1% to $3.29 billion, in line with guidance, with adjusted gross margin up 80 bps to 32.4% and adjusted EPS up 18% to $4.48, exceeding guidance; free cash flow was $278 million and leverage fell 0.21 turns to 3.89x. Q4 sales fell 11% to $303 million as retailers pulled back purchasing after earlier load-in. FY2027 guidance is 2%-4% sales growth (1%-2% from Black Kow), EPS of $4.70-$4.90, roughly $275 million of free cash flow, and gross margin expansion at the low end of the 50-100 bp midterm range, against roughly $100 million of commodity headwinds. Management said the plan holds up even with flat-to-slightly-down top line, but flagged low-single-digit retail inventory and commodity headwinds.

Qualcomm reported fiscal Q4 non-GAAP revenue of $10.4 billion and EPS of $2.17, with QCT revenue of $9 billion at the high end of guidance and QTL revenue of $1.3 billion at a 70% EBT margin. QCT automotive posted its first $2 billion quarter with 89% year-over-year growth, while handset revenue of $5.1 billion reflected memory-driven smartphone market weakness and the Apple ramp-down. December-quarter guidance of $10.4-11.2 billion revenue and $2.15-2.35 EPS implies QCT handset revenue down mid-single digits sequentially, offset by Data Center revenue above $650 million as custom silicon shipments to two hyperscalers begin. The most important changes versus the prior period were the completed QTL renewals with Apple, Huawei, and Transsion at an unchanged revenue run rate, the $8 billion annualized auto exit run rate versus $7 billion expected last quarter, and a reiteration of the $5 billion FY2027 Data Center target.

FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose to $625.7 million with Adjusted EPS up 75% to $4.04, but Q4 Adjusted EBITDA fell 3.1% year-over-year ($5 million decline); excluding an $18.2 million prior-year incentive accrual benefit, Q4 Adjusted EBITDA rose $13 million (8.7%) and margins expanded ~60 bps. FY2027 guidance sets Adjusted EBITDA at $645 million (low end) and adjusted free cash flow at $290 million, embedding $60 million of favorable price/cost, $10 million from incremental Envaplast, offset by $20 million transportation inflation, an $11 million volume headwind from low-single-digit Metal declines, and $30 million of inflation partially offset by $15 million of structural savings. Full-year adjusted free cash flow was $279.3 million, pressured in Q4 by higher resin-driven inventory and cash taxes, while the company repurchased $225 million of shares (~6% of shares outstanding) and cut leverage to 1.2x from 3.5x. The structural cost-out target was raised to $150 million by end of FY2027, up from the original $100 million commitment already met.

FICO closed FY2026 with Q4 revenue of $657M, up 27% YoY, non-GAAP EPS of $11.10 up 43%, and a non-GAAP operating margin of 61% versus 54% a year ago; full-year revenue rose 27% to $2.535B, with free cash flow of $1.034B (+40%) and $3.028B of buybacks (about 10% of shares). Q4 scores revenue grew 33% to $414M on a 72% jump in mortgage originations revenue despite high-single-digit volume declines, and software revenue rose 19% to $243M with platform ARR up 72%. Against these results, management declined to provide FY2027 guidance, citing the in-progress shift to bespoke mortgage pricing and mortgage market uncertainty, and said it will no longer disclose pricing details on a go-forward basis. GAAP results included a $65M antitrust settlement accrual and a $27M restructuring charge.

Fiscal 2026 revenue was $261.5 million, down 2% year-over-year but within the guidance revised last quarter, and adjusted EBITDA was $28.9 million (11.0% margin) versus $28.8 million, within both original and narrowed ranges. Q4 revenue fell 2% to $70 million while adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $12.8 million and margin expanded to 18.3% from 16.4%, helped by a $7.7 million full-year decline in operating SG&A. FY2027 guidance is revenue of $263-273 million constant currency (about 1.5%-5% growth, ~3% at midpoint after a ~$2 million China licensee transition drag) and adjusted EBITDA of $29-34 million (~9% growth at midpoint). Leading indicators were stronger than reported revenue, with consolidated subscription and committed-services invoiced amounts up 9%, Enterprise up 18%, and North America deferred revenue up 17%, though Education invoicing fell 10% and Q4 North America invoicing was flat.

Prudential reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted operating income of $1.3 billion ($3.77/share), missing the prior year's $1.4 billion ($4.05/share) due to a $140 million impact from the Prudential of Japan sales suspension and PRT runoff, though U.S. businesses showed solid underlying momentum. Management reiterated full-year 2026 effective tax rate guidance of 20%-21% (down from prior 21%-22%) following the restatement of emerging markets into divested entities. The company confirmed net proceeds of approximately $3.1 billion from the sale of Brazil and Mexico businesses, with closing expected in H2 next year.

PSBD reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $11.6 million ($0.38 per share), missing the prior year's $13.6 million due to lower base rates and portfolio paydowns, while NAV per share declined slightly from $13.21 to $13.34 after a volatile quarter with rate hikes in September. Management maintained a cautious outlook on deal activity citing elevated interest rate volatility and geopolitical uncertainty, though they affirmed confidence in the sustainability of the base dividend and prioritized share repurchases.

Emerson reported Q4 underlying sales up 7% with software and systems up 14%, adjusted segment EBITA margin expanding 160 bps to 29.1%, and adjusted EPS up 15% to $1.86, all above expectations. Full-year adjusted EPS rose 10% to $6.59 on 4% underlying sales growth, free cash flow up 9% to $3.5 billion, and $1 billion of buybacks. FY2027 guidance calls for ~5% underlying sales growth, 29% adjusted segment EBITA margin, and adjusted EPS of $7.25 (up 10%), plus a 7% dividend increase. Orders grew 14% and backlog rose 11% to $8.2 billion, though Europe and China remain weak and management built caution on those regions into the guide.

Cencora reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $88.4 billion (+6% YoY), adjusted gross profit of $3.6 billion (+23%) and adjusted EPS of $4.66 (+21%), with adjusted gross margin up 57 bps to 4.04%. Full-year adjusted operating income rose 14% and adjusted EPS reached $17.97 (+12%), with adjusted free cash flow of $3.8 billion ahead of guidance. FY2027 guidance calls for EPS of $19.40-$19.75 (+8-10%; 10-12% excluding the MWI/Covetrus merger), revenue growth of 3-5% and operating income growth of 4-6%, the last reduced by an approximate 5-point drag from businesses in Other. The company introduced two new reporting segments, raised its dividend 10% and plans $1.25 billion of buybacks in FY2027.

Ashland reported Q4 FY2026 sales of $498 million, up 4% YoY on 3% volume and 2% pricing, with adjusted EBITDA of $121 million (+2%) and adjusted EPS of $1.12 versus $1.08. Life Sciences (sales +4%, EBITDA +16%, margin 35.6%) and Personal Care (sales +8%, EBITDA +14%, margin 30.1%) delivered record margins, while Specialty Additives EBITDA fell to $20 million from $29 million on lower Hopewell productivity. FY2027 guidance is sales of $1.905-1.975 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $405-435 million, and FCF conversion above 40%, incorporating $7-10 million of FX EBITDA headwind and a ~$5 million Hopewell carryover in Q1. Operating cash flow rose to $90 million from $40 million and net leverage stood at 2.3x.

Adient closed fiscal 2026 with Q4 sales of $3.7 billion, up 1% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $229 million at a 6.1% margin, both roughly flat, while adjusted EPS was $0.52. Full-year revenue was about $15.2 billion (up 4%, up 2% ex-FX), adjusted EBITDA $884 million essentially flat, adjusted EPS $1.87 and free cash flow $222 million versus prior guidance of $120-130 million, helped by roughly $60 million of pulled-forward cash and $35 million of IEEPA refunds. For fiscal 2027 management guided revenue down to roughly $14.8-15.0 billion on a ~1% global production decline, adjusted EBITDA of $900-925 million, and free cash flow of more than $100 million, citing continued mix compression in the Americas and China. The board added $400 million to the buyback authorization, and management flagged a $30-70 million Americas tariff pull plus fuel surcharge and labor cost recovery embedded in the guide.

Sturm, Ruger & Company reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $148 million, a 17% year-over-year increase from $127 million in the prior year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $14 million (10% margin) compared to $3 million last year, driven by product mix and manufacturing efficiencies. Management raised full-year capital expenditure guidance expectations to approximately $30 million while declaring a quarterly dividend of $0.18 per share.

Veeco reported Q3 revenue of $209 million, within guidance, non-GAAP operating income of $25 million and diluted EPS of $0.36; gross margin of 39% came in below expectations due to higher supply chain costs, product mix, and timing of an LSA system under U.S. export review. Q4 guidance of $230-260 million implies sequential growth, with gross margin guided to 43-44%, and full-year revenue guidance was updated to $790-820 million with EPS of $1.32-1.52. Management cited strong AI-driven order momentum across advanced packaging, silicon photonics, and annealing, guiding 2027 growth toward the high end of a 20-40% WFE range and a path to exceed $1 billion in 2027 revenue, while flagging industry-wide component constraints.

Insulet reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $842 million, up 19.2% year-over-year on a reported basis and 19.6% on a constant currency basis. Adjusted gross margin expanded 200 basis points to 74.2%, while adjusted operating margin increased 490 basis points to 22%. Management narrowed full-year 2026 revenue guidance to the top end of the prior range and provided an updated, more conservative perspective for 2027 growth.

Q3 production was in line at 433 MBOE/d and oil came in within guidance at 230 MBbl/d, though roughly 2% below the midpoint due to Permian downtime and Uinta takeaway constraints that cost about 4,000 bbl/d. SM generated $1.3 billion of adjusted EBITDAX and $1.1 billion of operating cash flow, with $397 million of adjusted free cash flow, $747 million of capex and $133 million returned to stockholders. Synergy capture was raised to roughly $400 million actioned versus the original $200 million target, and net debt fell to $6.0 billion from $7.4 billion at the end of Q1. Full-year capital was narrowed to about $2.75 billion at the prior midpoint, but full-year cash taxes are now seen at $100-120 million versus roughly $50 million at $85 oil, and the Uinta rail constraint persists into early 2027.

Trimble reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $967M, up 7% (over 9% organic tracked for the full year), and EPS of $0.86, in line and above the midpoint of guidance. Record ARR of $2.564B rose 10%, but the full-year ARR outlook was cut to approximately 10% from a prior 12%-14% on Field Systems positioning-services weakness (South America ag) and softer Transporeon ARR. Full-year revenue midpoint was held at $3.925B and EPS midpoint raised slightly to $3.66 (about 17% growth), while AECO operating margin target was lifted 100 bps to 36%. Management also flagged a roughly $90M 2027 revenue and operating income headwind from a calendar shift in term-license renewals, and noted a cost-reduction program.

Call was dominated by the announced stock-for-stock merger of Shoals and ARRAY, with Shoals shareholders receiving 1.6931 ARRAY shares and owning ~65% of the combined company, expected to close in Q1 2027. Shoals Q3 revenue was a record $195.3M, up 44% YoY, with gross margin of 31.9% (up 160 bps QoQ), Adjusted EBITDA of ~$40M at 20.4% of revenue, ~$186M in new orders and ~1.0 book-to-bill; management said results were well above the guided range but Q4 guidance was not detailed on the call. ARRAY Q3 revenue was $330M including one month of AWM ($321M ex-AWM), Adjusted gross margin 22.8% including a 330 bps 45X rebate reserve charge, Adjusted EBITDA $32M at 10% margin, and a record $2.6B order book up 42% YoY with 1.6x book-to-bill. Combined preliminary 2027 outlook is $2.2-2.4B revenue and $410-480M Adjusted EBITDA including $100M+ year-three synergies, with pro forma 2026 net debt/EBITDA of 2.6x declining below 2x in 2027.

Trinity reported Q3 FY2026 total investment income of $98 million, up 30% year-over-year, and NII of $50 million, or $0.52 per share, covering the $0.51 distribution at 103%. NAV per share rose $0.14 to $13.61 and total net assets grew 5% sequentially and 33% year-over-year to a record $1.3 billion, with ROE of 15.5%. Platform AUM reached $3.4 billion, up 31% year-over-year, with $614 million funded in the quarter, $880 million of new commitments, and $1.4 billion of unfunded commitments. No explicit forward guidance was given beyond the $0.17 monthly dividend through Q4; management described the pipeline as the largest in company history.

Sprott reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $22 million, up 67% YoY from $13.2 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $46 million, up 44% YoY from $31.9 million, driven by average AUM of $58.8 billion (up 39% YoY). AUM ended at $57.3 billion, up 3% QoQ but down 4% YoY from $59.6 billion, with $200 million in net redemptions including $421 million of outflows from the Physical Silver Trust partly offset by $380 million of inflows into the Physical Gold Trust and $200 million of net sales in critical materials. The board raised the quarterly dividend 25%, the third consecutive year of double-digit growth, and year-to-date buybacks approach 1% of shares outstanding with over $200 million in cash and no debt. Guidance was not provided, but management cited accelerating free cash flow from operating leverage and variable compensation.

Trex reported Q3 net sales up 26% to approximately $360 million, with roughly $30 million (~11 points) from initial distribution load-in and the balance from underlying demand estimated at ~15% growth versus ~6% category growth. Adjusted gross margin fell to 36.9% from the prior year on labor inefficiencies, higher depreciation, and over $4 million of incremental inbound freight; adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to ~$100 million (27.7% margin). The company raised full-year guidance to net sales of ~$1.296-$1.306 billion (up 11% at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $355-$360 million, and guided Q4 sales to $175-$185 million including $5 million of load-in. Free cash flow was ~$135 million, with $83 million of revolver paydown and $55 million of buybacks in the quarter ($97 million repurchased through October 31 against a $150 million second-half target).

Tutor Perini reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.7 billion, up 22% YoY, with record operating income of $125 million (up 213%) and adjusted EPS of $1.83, up 59%. GAAP EPS was $0.39, up 457%, weighed down by a $51 million debt-extinguishment loss and a $34 million pension settlement charge. Management raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.90-$6.10 from $5.15-$5.45 and reiterated expectations for double-digit revenue and earnings growth in 2027, supported by a near-record $20.4 billion backlog and a book-to-burn of 1.3x.

Timken reported Q3 FY2026 total sales of $1.21B, up 4.7% YoY (organic +2.8%), adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.5% vs 17.4% last year, and adjusted EPS of $1.65, up 20% YoY (including a ~$12M/$0.13 tariff refund benefit). Industrial Motion sales rose 12.4% (organic +7.3%) while Engineered Bearings grew only 0.7% (organic +0.5%) on a double-digit China wind decline. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $6.35-$6.50 (20% growth at the midpoint), total revenue guidance held at ~+5.5% and organic at +3.5%, with EBITDA margin nudged to mid-18%. Management also gave an early 2027 view of mid-single-digit organic growth, cited a sequentially and YoY up mid-single-digit backlog, and noted the belts divestiture may see 200+ bps to Industrial Motion margins in 2027.

TKO reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $1.36 billion, up 21%, and Adjusted EBITDA of $556 million (+54%) at a 41% margin, up ~870 bps year-over-year. UFC revenue rose 60% to $519M on a favorable event mix and the Skydance media step-up, while WWE revenue fell 1% to $399M on three fewer PLEs, and IMG revenue grew 16% with World Cup Adjusted EBITDA of ~$45M. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second consecutive quarter to $5.79-$5.83B revenue and $2.295-$2.315B Adjusted EBITDA, up $10M and $15M at the midpoint versus August guidance. The outlook assumes scheduled Middle East events proceed, and management noted a contingency impact if they cannot be staged.

Combined Q3 FY2026 revenue was $298.7 million, up 257% year-over-year and 90% sequentially, including a first full quarter of Renesas TPD at $86.3 million (+67% YoY); core SiTime was $212.4 million (+154%), with CED at $127.3 million (+202%). Non-GAAP gross margin was 70.7% (up 11.9 pts YoY, 3.6 pts QoQ), operating margin 43% (up 25 pts), and EPS $4.01 (+360%), with non-GAAP net income up over 5x to $130.3 million. Q4 guidance is $331-341 million revenue at ~70% gross margin with roughly flat opex, implying EPS of about $4.76 at the midpoint; management also announced a 3-for-1 stock split effective December 7, 2026. Offsets include continued wafer supply constraints through 2027, a $6.6 million use of operating cash in Q3 on working capital, and DSO up 10 days to 61.

Consolidated revenue was KRW 4,497.3 billion, up 3.2% QoQ and 13.1% YoY, with operating income of KRW 552.3 billion, marking three consecutive quarters above KRW 500 billion and cumulative first-three-quarter operating income of KRW 1,655.9 billion. Mobile service revenue grew QoQ on flagship handset launches and higher-value subscriber acquisition, and ARPU rose. Third-quarter DPS was KRW 830; management guided to maintaining at least the current dividend level but deferred a new shareholder-return policy (including any treasury share cancellation) to no later than the Q1 2027 DPS determination. AIDC progress included Ulsan construction permits, talks with three to four global potential tenants, and a target for phased data center opening from 2H 2029.

Teknova reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue up 22% YoY (second straight record quarter), with Clinical Solutions up 86% to $3.2M and Lab Essentials up 9% to $9.0M. Gross margin expanded to 38.0% from 30.7%, net loss narrowed to $3.5M (-$0.06/sh) from $4.3M (-$0.08/sh), and adjusted EBITDA improved to -$1.0M from -$1.6M. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $46-48M, implying ~16% growth at the midpoint, while gross margin guidance stayed in the mid-to-upper 30s. The company also completed a $46M equity raise ($43M net) in mid-October and reiterated an expected first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter before the end of 2027.

SLRC reported Q3 FY2026 NII of $0.33 per share, matching the prior quarter and covering the $0.31 distribution, on gross investment income of $49.3 million versus $48.8 million in Q2. NAV per share fell to $17.83 from $18.00, a roughly 90 bps sequential decline (down 2.1% YoY) driven by a fair-value write-down on the OmniGuide non-accrual. Net realized and unrealized losses widened to $10.2 million from $9.5 million, leaving net increase in net assets from operations at $7.6 million versus $8.3 million. Originations set a record at $575 million (95% specialty finance) against $429 million of repayments; management gave no explicit EPS or NII guidance but struck a cautious credit-cycle tone, projecting defaults and liability-management exercises to rise over the next year.

Triple Flag reported Q3 FY2026 results with 25,000 GEOs, revenue of $107 million up 14% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $94 million up 22%, and operating cash flow per share of $0.45 up 15% from $0.39. Management said it remains on track to deliver in the top half of its increased 100,000-110,000 GEO guidance range and reiterated the 2030 outlook of 150,000-160,000 GEOs (~50% growth), with a 2031 view to come in February. It repurchased $20 million of shares in the quarter (on top of $20 million in Q2), repaid $50 million on its revolver to $185 million drawn with over $1.1 billion of available liquidity, and expects to repay the facility during 2027. No hard guidance raise occurred on this call; the increased range was referenced as prior context.

Q3 revenue was $88.2M, up 7.4% YoY, with gross margin 78.2% (down 120 bps) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.5M (4% of revenue), all in line with guidance. Q4 guidance was cut to $77-79M, a 2% YoY decline at the midpoint, with adjusted EBITDA of negative 2% to negative 4% of revenue, citing competitive peer-to-peer spend and a more promotional holiday; this marks a second consecutive guide-down. Management also gave preliminary 2027 framing of low single-digit revenue growth and flat adjusted EBITDA margins versus 2026. Price paid per item fell from $21 to $18 beginning in June and has held there, pressuring revenue despite record GMV (up 20%), record 1.8M active buyers (up 16%), and 17% order growth.

trivago reported Q3 2026 total revenue of EUR 192.5 million, up 16% year-over-year and its seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with net income of EUR 5.4 million and Adjusted EBITDA of EUR 18.7 million (the highest since mid-2023, and ahead of internal expectations). Management confirmed full-year 2026 guidance of mid-teens revenue growth and Adjusted EBITDA of around EUR 30 million, and introduced a 2027 outlook of double-digit revenue growth and around EUR 45 million Adjusted EBITDA, targeting a 10% margin by 2028. Americas and developed Europe each grew referral revenue 15%, while Rest of World fell 10% on FX and Middle East impact; watching and marketing rose EUR 17.3 million, with Americas ROAS declining to 129% from 135.4%.

Q3 revenue fell 7% YoY to $462.3M, while ex-TAC gross profit rose 7% to $188.8M and adjusted EBITDA grew 16% to $56M (29.7% margin). Scaled advertisers declined 4% and average revenue per scaled advertiser fell 5%. Management lowered full-year ex-TAC guidance to $754-763M (~6% growth) and issued a Q4 revenue guide of $477-493M, citing declining impressions per page view from AI-driven consumer behavior shifts and a slower-than-expected Next Engage rollout. Q3 repurchases totaled $30.3M (7M shares at $4.37), with a new $200M buyback authorization.

TrueBlue reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $521 million, up 21% and above the high end of guidance, with net income of $9 million versus a $2 million loss a year ago and adjusted EBITDA of $21 million versus $11 million. All three segments grew and expanded margins, led by PeopleReady up 34% on energy work that doubled; gross margin fell to 20.5% from 22.7% on revenue mix, while SG&A was cut 3%. Q4 guidance calls for revenue growth of 20%-24% with steady sequential gross margin, implying ~22% growth at the midpoint. Working capital rose $35 million on stronger revenue, with management expecting a return to free-cash-flow positive as it normalizes.

Q3 revenue of $314.7M grew 5.4% YoY and beat the $302M top end of guidance by $12.7M, a record quarter; adjusted EBITDA was $59.1M at 18.8% margin, ~10 bps above guidance. Full-year revenue guidance was raised for the second consecutive quarter to $1.249-1.251B (5.6% growth at midpoint) and adjusted FCF raised for the third straight quarter to $115-125M, with Q4 revenue guided to $319-321M (2.3% growth) and 19.5% margins. Adjusted EPS fell to $0.34 from $0.42 a year ago, and Trust & Safety declined 15.8%. Largest client fell to 17% of revenue from 27% on automation, while the rest of the business grew ~20% and AI Services rose 27.7%. Management flagged that 2027 investment step-up will pressure near-term margins.

SmartRent reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $42 million, up 15% year over year, with core revenue up 24% to $41 million. Gross margin expanded 1,500 basis points to 41%, and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.1 million, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Q4 guidance calls for total revenue growth of 15%-20%, core revenue growth of 20%-25%, and adjusted EBITDA growth of roughly 450%-650%. The main blemish was a sequential decline in SaaS ARR driven by attrition in Smart Operations, though management expects that pressure to persist for a couple more quarters.

Talos reported Q3 FY2026 total production of ~92,000 BOE/d (oil ~69,000 bpd), both exceeding guidance, with adjusted EBITDA ~$406M and adjusted free cash flow ~$186M on premium oil realizations ~$1.60/bbl above WTI. The company raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 68,000-70,000 bpd oil and 92.5-94.5 BOE/d (~8% oil increase at midpoint vs. original guidance), funding the $420M Gulf of America bolt-on while keeping leverage at 0.6x and the revolver undrawn. Total capital and P&A spend is unchanged from the original plan, with capex guidance lowered at the midpoint and P&A raised. Daenerys appraisal remains ongoing with a 2027 sidetrack and no development decision yet.

Net sales rose 21.2% YoY to $1.98B, with domestic up 19.4% to $1.31B and international up 25.2% to $663M; adjusted EPS was $2.34 versus $1.50 a year ago and adjusted EBITDA grew about 46%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 560 bps to 55.9%, though management said excluding the IEEPA tariff refund gross margin would have been down roughly 100 bps. Guidance was raised, with the company flagging that the refund benefit, partly reinvested (~$45M to factory partners, plus media, R&D and AI spend), is being balanced against margin expansion, and international growth is expected to re-accelerate in Q4 versus Q3.

Southwest Gas reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS from continuing operations of $0.20 versus $0.06 a year ago, with year-to-date adjusted EPS of $2.69, up 18%, driven by California rate relief, customer growth, and flat O&M. Management reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.17-$4.32 (centering around the midpoint) and the 12%-14% long-term EPS growth target; no guidance was raised. Final orders in California (~$32M) and Nevada (~$48M) deliver ~$80M of incremental annual revenue, while Arizona remains pending with staff context $53-58M versus the company's updated $91.3M request. The quarter benefited from roughly $0.12 of non-recurring items (D&A true-up and state tax benefit) that management said were not fully in plan.

Snap reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.72 billion, up 14% year-over-year and within the prior guidance range of $1.70-$1.74 billion, with gross margin of 62% (up ~7 points), net income of $56 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $383 million (22% margin). Advertising revenue grew just 4% as upper-funnel brand advertising declined, while other revenue grew 84% and paid subscribers surpassed 30 million. Q4 revenue guidance is $1.950-$1.985 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $490-$525 million, and full-year infrastructure cost guidance was narrowed to $1.65-$1.66 billion from $1.65-$1.70 billion. Management also announced a shift to global MAU and MAU-based ARPU as primary metrics beginning Q1 2027.

Smith & Nephew reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.55 billion, up 3.4% underlying and 3.4% reported with no FX impact, an acceleration from Q2, but cut full-year guidance to approximately 3% revenue growth (trading profit to about $1.25 billion, FCF about $750 million) citing no expected material improvement in U.S. knees and hips. Sports Medicine & ENT grew 7.9% with joint repair up 11.2%, wound declined 0.2% on an 8.8% bioactives fall, and orthopedics returned to growth at 2.5% while U.S. knees and hips stayed weak. Management disclosed that discussions with J&J over DePuy Synthes had ended, while a broader strategic review of orthopedics remains active. The guidance cut follows prior reductions and comes before the LANDMARK cemented launch in Q2 2027 and CORI Hip in Q1 2027.

Adjusted EPS of $2.31 beat the midpoint of guidance by $0.76, but $0.67 of that came from net IEEPA tariff refunds rather than operations; above-the-line operating performance was 'largely in line' with expectations. Adjusted gross margin of 39.4% included about 430 bps of tariff benefit, with the remaining ~350 bps of YoY improvement driven by productivity and mix. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised and tightened to $5.95-$6.25 (midpoint +$0.60, 31% YoY growth), of which $0.55 is incremental net tariff refunds; revenue and organic outlooks were unchanged (~flat total, low-single-digit organic). Free cash flow guidance rose $400M at the midpoint to $1B-$1.2B, and a new $1B buyback authorization followed $250M repurchased in the quarter.

Silvaco reported Q3 FY2026 bookings of $19.3 million, above the midpoint of guidance, but revenue of $16.3 million came in slightly below the guided midpoint due to IP milestone timing pushes into Q4. GAAP gross margin was 84% (Non-GAAP 85.3%), down sequentially on the revenue shortfall but up roughly six points year-over-year, with GAAP OpEx down 6% sequentially to $18 million and a GAAP net loss of $4.6 million (14-cent loss per share). Q4 guidance calls for record revenue of $22 million at the midpoint, up 35% sequentially and 21% year-over-year, with FY2026 revenue growth of 17% and mid-to-high teens growth expected again in 2027. TCAD bookings hit a Q3 record $10.3 million (+89% YoY) on a new tier 1 FTCO customer, and IP bookings grew 193% year-over-year.

Q3 net sales were ~$1.05B, up 8% YoY and above the top end of guidance, with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.50 and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.80. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $265M and margin expanded 109 bps to 25.3%, led by Electronic & Specialty Materials sales up 13% (electronic materials +31%) and refrigerants +8%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for a second consecutive quarter to net sales of $4.195-$4.22B and adjusted EBITDA of $1.05-$1.06B, while Q4 guidance implies sequential moderation. Nuclear sales grew only 4% on ~$30M of product loan returns, and Building Solutions & Intermediates declined 5% on construction softness.

Suncor reported record Q3 2026 adjusted funds from operations of CAD 6.7 billion and record free funds flow of CAD 5.2 billion. Upstream production averaged 853,000 bbl/d (second-highest Q3 ever, down from last year's record due to Syncrude's 47-day coker turnaround), refining throughput was 488,000 bbl/d at 95% utilization, and product sales hit a record 677,000 bbl/d. Management raised monthly buybacks from CAD 500 million to CAD 750 million, declared a 10% dividend increase, and reaffirmed its 2026 Investor Day targets of CAD 2 billion incremental free funds flow and a further $5/bbl WTI break-even reduction through 2028 despite the CAD 1.2 billion sale of East Coast offshore assets.

TORM reported Q3 2026 TCE earnings of $353M versus $236M a year ago, EBITDA of $274M versus $152M, and net profit of $199M versus $78M, with EPS of $1.94 versus $0.79. Average TCE rate rose to roughly $40,100/day from $31,000/day, and the board declared an interim dividend of $1.35 per share versus $0.62 a year ago. Management raised the low end of full-year TCE guidance by $50M to $1.75B-$1.9B and the low end of EBITDA guidance by $50M to $1.35B-$1.5B, citing strong Q4 coverage including LR2 spot days booked at roughly $185,000/day. Earnings moderated from an exceptionally strong Q2, and management framed the newbuild expansion as fleet renewal required by about half the LR2 fleet turning 20 within a few years.

TSLX reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $0.44/share (10.7% annualized ROE) and net income of $0.36/share (8.9% ROE), with NAV per share of $16.19 versus $16.24 at June 30. NII exceeded the $0.42 base dividend for 105% coverage, supporting a $0.42 base plus $0.01 supplemental dividend, and NII has risen sequentially each quarter of the year. Full-year NII ROE guidance was reaffirmed at 10%-10.5% assuming turnover stays below 20%, though Q4 repayment-driven fee income will determine where in that range results land. Portfolio yield rose ~20 bps to 11.4%, but M&A-driven origination was subdued and watch-list (risk-rated 3) loans rose to ~5% of the portfolio from ~2%.

Root reported Q3 2026 revenue of $381M versus $388M a year ago, with gross written premium down 8% to $358M and gross earned premium down 5% to $356M. Net income swung to $14M from a $5M loss a year ago, adjusted EBITDA was $34M roughly flat, and the net combined ratio improved 4.9 points to 97.2%. Policies in force rose 4% YoY to 484,000 but were broadly flat sequentially, and management guided year-end PIF broadly in line with Q3 while citing an intensified competitive environment that it expects to persist, with Q4 accident-period loss ratio trending toward the top of the 60%-65% target range on seasonality. Partnership new writings grew 19% YoY and were 52% of new writings; $36M of the $75M buyback authorization has been used through Q3.

Q3 2026 after-tax adjusted operating EPS of $2.20 included $0.33 of favorable notable items versus $2.81 a year ago (which included $0.75 of notable items); core premium grew 4.7%. Results fell short of earnings expectations as group disability's benefit ratio, excluding notable items, rose to 70.6% from 61.3% on higher LTD submissions (~5 points) and STD/PFML pressure (~2 points), while UK group income protection benefits also worsened and international adjusted operating income was only $0.2 million. Full-year 2026 adjusted operating EPS guidance is now $8.30-$8.50, incorporating the annual assumption review, with Q4 assumed similar to Q3; the $3.8 billion LTC reinsurance with Fortitude Re closed and YTD capital return exceeded $1 billion. Management characterized the LTD increase as behavioral-health-focused claim submissions, not yet a sustained trend, and is repricing and taking other actions.

Veracyte reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $151.8 million, up approximately 15% year-over-year, with Afirma tests up 19% and Decipher Prostate up 12%. Non-GAAP gross margin rose 90 bps to 73.7% and adjusted EBITDA was $41.2 million (27.2% of revenue), above the 25% long-term target. Despite the solid quarter, management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $590-593 million from $590-596 million and lowered incremental Decipher annual volume growth expectations to 12,000-15,000 tests, citing normalization after two years of outsized guideline-driven growth and distraction from digital pathology competitors. The preliminary 2027 outlook calls for approximately 10% volume growth but only mid-single-digit revenue growth and roughly 22% adjusted EBITDA, as prior-period collections drop off and lower-ASP products (Prosigna, bladder) mix in.

Adjusted net income per share came in at $0.25, with fee-related revenue of $89 million (up 17% YoY), FRE of $43 million (up 19% YoY) and a 48% FRE margin (47% YTD, flat YoY). Fee-paying AUM reached $35.2 billion, up 2.4% sequentially and 21% YoY (11% excluding Stellus), on $1.3 billion of gross fundraising and deployment in the quarter. Management reiterated the full-year core fee rate of ~103 bps (implying a step-up in Q4 after a soft 99 bps in Q3), $6-8 million of catch-up fees, flat full-year FRE margin, and a mid-twos year-end leverage target; no specific EPS or FRE guidance was given versus prior periods in the text. The main soft spot was a 1 bp sequential decline in the core fee rate to 99 bps on fundraising and tax-credit seasonality, which management attributes to timing rather than demand.

Q3 FY2026 contract sales rose 29% YoY to $565 million at the high end of guidance, with VPG up 30% to $4,822 and adjusted EBITDA up 27% to $216 million; development profit nearly doubled to $142 million on a 31% margin. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint guidance to $820 million and contract sales midpoint to $2.13 billion, absorbing an estimated $16 million in Hurricane Lowell lost profits ($11 million in Q4) not in prior guidance. Marketing and sales costs fell 600 bps to 48% of contract sales and leverage dropped to 3.6x from 4.2x at the start of the year. Q4 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $218-238 million and contract sales of $599-619 million.

Management described Q3 as a "great quarter" with $33.4 billion of volume and roughly "a couple hundred million dollars" of Adjusted EBITDA, with expenses down about $58-59 million quarter-over-quarter, though no formal revenue, EPS or margin lines were given in this Q&A-only call. Guidance was soft-to-flat: Q4 volume is explicitly seen as lower ("not going to be $40B, $50B, $60B") with gain-on-sale steady in the 115-130 bps range, while a $2.1 billion 2027 expense target was affirmed versus a $2.3 billion Q3 run rate. The most important changes are the Oaktree capital injection and rights offering (addressing dilution and liquidity) and large MSR sales ($135-140 billion in 2026) used to deleverage, with leverage targeted below 1.5 by year-end. Tone was combative on competitor claims (Rocket) and confident on cost and capital, but cautious on the mortgage market backdrop.

Rapid7 reported Q3 FY2026 ARR of $820M, $8M above guidance, with non-GAAP operating income of $46.2M (21.7% margin) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.60, ahead of guided profitability. Total revenue of $212.4M declined ~3% YoY, and total ARR fell ~2% YoY as core platform ARR ($85M of mix) grew ~1% while non-core (~15% of ARR) declined ~19%. Q4 guidance calls for ARR of ~$812M (down from $820M), revenue of $208-210M (~4% YoY decline), and full-year revenue of $841-843M (~2% decline); full-year free cash flow is reaffirmed at ~$130M and 2026 exit margin at ~20%. 2027 guidance and formal color were deferred to the next call.

Royalty Pharma reported Q3 FY2026 portfolio receipts of $890 million, up 9% YoY, with royalty receipts also up 9% and up 12% year-to-date. Portfolio cash flow (Adjusted EBITDA less net interest) was $673 million at a ~76% margin, and ROIC was 14.3% with ROIE at 20.2%. Management raised full-year 2026 portfolio receipts guidance to $3.5-3.55 billion from $3.4-3.5 billion, the third consecutive quarterly raise, lifting royalty receipts growth to ~10-11% from 7-10%. The quarter included a $150 million non-cash impairment on pelacarsen, though the investment was structured to return 1.1x.

United Therapeutics reported record total revenue of $833 million and record Tyvaso revenue of $504 million in Q3 2026, with management attributing growth to consistent monthly execution, higher dosing (roughly one in three new Tyvaso DPI patients reaching higher doses, twice the prior rate), and no material inventory or seasonal effect. Management did not provide explicit numeric guidance for revenue or EPS on the call, and stated the sales force expansion had limited Q3 revenue impact with benefit expected in Q4 and 2027. Offsetting the commercial strength, the soft mist inhaler NDA filing slipped from year-end 2026 to 2027 after FDA feedback required additional data, the triple oral pill faces an unclear path after FDA said bioequivalence data was insufficient, and the ralinepag API supplier carries an OAI compliance status. The company also disclosed a settlement removing PH-ILD from the YUTREPIA label and an opportunistic buyout of Arena's ralinepag royalty economics.

USANA guided FY2026 net sales to approaching $900 million and adjusted EBITDA to approximately $77 million, down from a prior $80.5 million outlook, citing softer Rise sales and deliberate Hiya investment partly offset by stronger core profitability. Core nutrition is now guided to roughly $740 million, about $10 million below the most recent outlook, with active customers down 8% year-over-year and Greater China driving most of the sequential decline. Hiya was the bright spot, with active monthly subscribers up 18% sequentially (~29,500 net adds) and its net sales outlook raised to $130 million, while Rise Wellness had its outlook lowered again on lumpy club orders. Cash from operations was $45 million YTD versus $26 million last year, free cash flow $36 million, and the company ended with $179 million in cash and no debt.

Sunrun reported Q3 FY2026 Cash Generation of $6 million ($56 million excluding $50 million of safe-harbor equipment investment) and added over 24,000 customers, with direct volumes up 17% QoQ and 9% YoY while affiliate volume fell 67% YoY. The company cut full-year Cash Generation guidance to approximately $200 million from a prior $200-$375 million and revised Aggregate Subscriber Value to about $4.6 billion versus prior $4.6-$4.9 billion, citing modestly lower direct sales pacing and sustained higher interest rates. Offsets included record 75% storage attachment and Upfront Net Subscriber Value rising to over $3,700 per subscriber from $2,000 in Q2. Management reiterated 2027 volume growth but flagged elevated ITC insurance costs and new California property tax, deferring 2027 guidance to the Q4 call.

First commercial quarter following the August 26 FDA approval of RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer: net product revenue of $197.6 million across roughly five weeks, with more than 5,000 unique patients treated on a commercial basis. Management attributed early demand partly to finite dynamics — completed EAP-to-commercial transitions and a backlog cohort of patients who had exhausted options — and cautioned it is too early to read a normalized trajectory, while noting 2026 GAAP opex guidance of $2.1–2.2 billion is reiterated and 2027 opex will rise from the current run rate. R&D was $417.1 million versus $262.5 million and SG&A $153.3 million versus $52.8 million a year ago, with a net loss of $407.5 million and $3.7 billion in cash plus a $250 million post-quarter Royalty Pharma debt tranche. A positive CHMP opinion on October 15 and NCCN category 1 preferred listing were the key regulatory and guideline developments.

Q3 net sales were $383 million, up 2% sequentially and 8% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $52 million versus $40 million in Q2 and $42 million a year ago. The GAAP loss from continuing operations was $229 million, driven by $221 million of non-cash impairments primarily at Témiscaming; excluding impairments the loss was $8 million versus $20 million in Q2. HPC adjusted EBITDA rose $16 million sequentially to $73 million on 23% margins (from 19%) as CS pricing reached $2,227/ton versus $825 for commodity cellulose, but Paperboard & HYPP remained negative at $9 million and Témiscaming was economically idled October 3 after the 50% U.S. paperboard tariff, with $2-3 million per month of carrying costs. The strategic review conclusion slipped from Q4 to Q1 2027, and management still targets positive free cash flow for 2026 with CS volumes exiting the year near a 100,000 ton/quarter run rate but full-year CS volumes below prior year.
