Sinclair reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $893 million, up 16% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $213 million, up 113%, driven by political advertising of $136 million (up 55% vs. Q3 2022) plus 1% distribution growth; core advertising declined 4% on political crowd-out and cost-pressured consumer categories. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: political now ~$455 million vs. prior at least $375 million (and initial at least $333 million), consolidated adjusted EBITDA to $825-835 million (up $85 million at the midpoint) and total revenue to $3.53-3.6 billion, while core advertising and distribution ranges were narrowed within prior ranges. STG net leverage fell to 5.1x from 5.2x last quarter and 6.0x a year ago, and Ventures standalone separation was taken off the table though a broadcast spin-merge remains a stated priority. Management flagged 2027 as a tougher comp year without Olympics/World Cup or political revenue and with MLB labor uncertainty, alongside a large MVPD renewal slate.

UroGen reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $89M versus $27.5M a year ago, with ZUSDURI net product revenue of $68M, up 35% sequentially from roughly $50M in Q2, and JELMYTO at $21M versus $22M in Q2, including a $1.5M one-time unfavorable gross-to-net true-up. Net loss narrowed to $1.5M (-$0.03 per share) from a $33.3M loss (-$0.69) a year ago, with $90.5M in cash and securities and $117M in receivables. Management trimmed full-year JELMYTO guidance to approximately $90M on the true-up and competitive clinical-trial enrollment headwinds, kept opex guidance at $260-270M but flagged spending toward the upper end, did not issue ZUSDURI guidance, and expects Q4 profitability and positive cash flow with continued quarter-over-quarter ZUSDURI growth. Unique prescribers rose to 662 from 452 and repeat prescribers to 331 from 204, while UGN-103 received a June 14, 2027 PDUFA date.

Socket Mobile reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $3.4 million, up 9% YoY and 12% QoQ, with gross margin improving to 48.6% from 47.7% a year ago and 46.4% in Q2. Operating loss narrowed to $644 thousand from $1.06 million a year ago and $1.2 million last quarter, and Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $262 thousand; loss per share was $0.09 versus $0.16 in Q2 and $0.15 in Q3 2025. No explicit revenue or EPS guidance was given; management reiterated cost management, stabilizing revenue, and enterprise expansion priorities. The largest change versus prior periods is the voluntary Nasdaq-to-OTCID listing transition, disclosed after a stockholders' equity deficiency notice, alongside a $425 thousand 10% bridge loan from Chairman Charlie Bass and $575 thousand of convertible notes repaid.

Revenue rose 5.7% to $462 million, but essentially all growth came from the ~$30 million Keystone contribution; adjusted EBITDA fell 18.6% to $95 million and margin contracted to 20.6% from 26.7%. EPS was $0.22 versus $0.31. Full-year 2026 guidance was cut to adjusted EBITDA margin down approximately 250-300 bps year-over-year, versus prior expectations, citing mortgage rates, inflation, job site labor shortages, the Roanoke outage (about 60,000 tons of lost cement production), and soft Florida demand. Management pointed to 2027 price increases effective January 1 ($12/ton cement, $15/cu yd ready-mix) and Project Cornerstone cost savings (~$20 million realized in 2026, >$50 million run-rate targeted by 2029).

Q3 sales were $172.4M, up 11.6% (organic up 11.1%), with gross margin expanding to 29.4% from 27.7%, adjusted operating margin of 17.5%, and adjusted EPS of $2.88. MedTech grew 12.5% and YTD sales rose 10.3% to $500.6M. Management reiterated the 6%-9% organic and 12%-18% total growth framework, flagged Q4 as seasonally softer, and said AJR transfers to the Dominican Republic remain behind schedule with completion now expected in 2027. SG&A rose $4.1M YoY, including ~$1.9M in back-office and management investments and ~$800K of equity comp with duplicate CEO costs.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $64.5 million, up 19% YoY, with ACV of $44.7 million (17% growth, 24% excluding contribution ACV) and software revenue of $38.2 million, of which hosted revenue grew 49% to $17.2 million. Drug discovery revenue rose to $24.2 million from $13 million, driven by a Structure Therapeutics amylin milestone, while total operating expenses fell 13% to $64 million and net loss widened to $38 million from $33 million on mark-to-market losses in public equity holdings. Full-year 2026 drug discovery revenue guidance was raised to $75 million-$85 million from $65 million-$75 million, and ACV guidance is now $222 million-$232 million (12%-17% growth), with OpEx still expected below 2025. Software gross margin slipped to 75% from 77%, reflecting the hosted licensing transition that management said reduces reported revenue by roughly $2 million-$3 million per 1% of hosted mix.

Seadrill reported Q3 2026 revenue of $428 million, down $21 million QoQ on fewer operating days, with Adjusted EBITDA of $121 million (30% margin excluding reimbursables) and $179 million of Free Cash Flow. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.56-$1.58 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $440-$460 million, the third consecutive quarterly raise, while narrowing CapEx to $210-$230 million. Since the August call the company added roughly $800 million of total contract value, and drillship availability for 2027 fell from 30% to under 15%. Positives were partly offset by a soft U.S. Gulf with near-term schedule gaps and an oversupplied region, deferred Petrobras tendering until 1H 2027, and a Q4 repair and maintenance cost step-up.

UFG reported a 94.6% Q3 combined ratio, record nine-month earnings, 14% ROE, and $1.34 per diluted share in net and adjusted operating income. Net written premium grew 13%, but average renewal rate change moderated to 2% with property rates under the most pressure and casual/umbrella in upper single digits. The underlying loss ratio of 57.3% rose slightly YoY and the expense ratio of 34.9% was roughly flat, with management flagging more modest future margin improvement. Prior-year reserve development was neutral and the catastrophe loss ratio of 2.4% was above last year's 1.3% but below historical averages; no formal guidance was issued.

Uber reported a fifth consecutive quarter of 20%+ gross bookings growth, 215 million MAPCs, 35% non-GAAP EPS growth, and record trailing 12-month free cash flow of $10.4 billion, with Delivery gross bookings up 23% and grocery/retail at a $15 billion run rate growing 40%. However, Mobility came in below expectations as driver supply failed to keep pace with demand in several international markets, driven by elevated fuel costs and immigration dynamics. Q4 gross bookings growth guidance was held steady at 18%-22%, with Q4 non-GAAP EPS growth guided to about 37% year-over-year at the midpoint. Management flagged targeted supply investments that will pressure mobility take rate, while noting supply hours improved in October and reaffirming AV targets of ~700 driverless vehicles by year-end and 2,000+ by end of 2027.

Q3 GAAP revenue was $326.1 million, down 5.8% QoQ and 4.1% YoY, in line with the $310-340 million guidance midpoint. Non-GAAP gross margin of 34.7% included a ~$36 million IEEPA tariff benefit; excluding it, margin was ~23.6%, near the 22-26% guided midpoint, and non-GAAP EPS was $0.29 with $7.8 million of free cash flow, the fifth straight positive quarter. Q4 revenue guidance of $245-275 million is about $50 million below the Investor Day 2026 target at the midpoint, driven by $35 million of proactive channel inventory reduction, $10 million from de-emphasized markets, and $5 million of FX, with Q4 non-GAAP gross margin guided to 17-21%. Management also flagged a 10%+ sequential revenue decline in Q1 2027 and guided only to roughly flat revenue and adjusted EBITDA break-even for the full year 2027.

Sezzle reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue up 42.6% YoY to $166.5 million, with net income up 79.3% to $47.8 million and adjusted net income up 89.9% to $47.7 million. TTV grew 34.9% to a record $1.4 billion, and revenue less transaction costs rose 10.5 points to 64.7% of revenue, at the top of the 55%-65% target range. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for the fourth time, lifting revenue growth to approximately 42.5% from 35% and adjusted EPS to $5.45-$5.50 from $5.25, and introduced preliminary 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.20. Active subscribers reached 955,000, up 68.1% YoY, while marketing spend fell to $15.9 million from $19.4 million in Q2.

Q3 revenue of $24.0M came in within the $24-26M guide but fell 21.5% YoY and 5.4% QoQ; GAAP net income of $0.4M and Adjusted EBITDA of $1.5M beat the $0.5M EBITDA guide, though boosted by a non-recurring $0.8M tariff refund (with $0.4M bad debt expense). Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $20-22M and an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.5-3.0M, and full-year revenue outlook was cut to $95-97M from the prior $100-110M. Management cited a slower Europe recovery (EMEA -14.8% YoY), a weaker-than-expected GO ESS ramp ($1.3M vs $2.2M in Q2), and a U.S. inverter partner launch pushed to Q4, with U.S. revenue down 51.4% YoY.

SFL reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of ~$202 million, flat versus the prior quarter, adjusted EBITDA of ~$122 million versus $130 million, and net income of $37 million ($0.26/share, up from $0.25), including non-cash mark-to-market gains. Backlog rose to ~$5 billion after adding over $1.6 billion this year, supported by Hapag-Lloyd's seven-year extension on six container vessels (~$750 million) and a two-vessel container acquisition (~$250 million), while the board declared its 91st consecutive $0.22 quarterly dividend. The quarter was weighed down by zero rig revenue on Hercules and a $5 million sequential rise in opex to $85 million, but a $175 million book gain from the sale of seven tankers to Trafigura is set to be recognized over Q4 and Q1. Guidance was qualitative rather than numeric, with management pointing to Hertwo spot Suezmax Suezmax earnings above $200,000/day so far in Q4 and a Hercules campaign starting March 2027.

Ternium reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $785 million, up 10% sequentially, with margin expanding to 16.9% on a 5% sequential shipment increase to 4 million tons driven by Mexico market share gains and higher realized prices. Net income was $368 million, and cash from operations was $613 million, yielding positive free cash flow of $215 million and a net cash position of $22 million versus net debt of $112 million at June-end. Q4 guidance is for EBITDA broadly in line with Q3, as year-end seasonality lowers shipments but a modest margin-per-ton improvement offsets rising raw material and slab costs. Management flagged Brazil as challenging with a temporary partial suspension at MUSA and continued import pressure, while Mexico demand and pricing trends are described as positive into Q1 2027.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 10% YoY to $611 million and Adjusted EBITDA grew 8% to $165 million (27% margin), but customer-friendly sports results pushed sports margin down to 12.1% versus a 13.7% trailing 24-month average, cutting revenue by roughly $40 million and EBITDA by about $25 million. Management revised full-year 2026 guidance downward to $2.525-$2.575 billion revenue and $700-$720 million Adjusted EBITDA, citing the Q3 sports outcomes while maintaining that the underlying business remains strong. iCasino wagers hit records, up 11% YoY (14% ex-U.S.), active customers reached 6 million (+9%), and the board authorized a new $150 million buyback alongside roughly $25 million in quarterly dividends.

TWFG reported Q3 2026 total revenue up 24.6% to $79.9 million and organic revenue growth of 16.6%, with total written premiums up 18.5% to $554.2 million and adjusted EBITDA up 15% to $19.5 million. However, adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 210 bps to 24.4% versus 26.5%, net income fell to $9 million from $9.6 million, and diluted EPS declined to $0.09 from $0.11. Management modestly raised the revenue guidance range to $300-320 million and reaffirmed an adjusted EBITDA margin of 24%-27%, noting nine-month organic growth of 21.5% and margin of 28% track above the high end, while flagging continued normalization of the MGA Florida takeout book and softening market conditions.

Sight Sciences reported record Q3 revenue of $24.9M, up 25% YoY, with IDE revenue of $3.9M (up 45% QoQ) and IG revenue of $21.0M (up 7% YoY). Gross margin held at 86%, net loss narrowed to $6.8M ($0.12/share) from $8.2M ($0.16), and quarterly cash use fell 74% to $2.4M. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $92-93M from $88-92M, with IDE lifted to ~$12M from $9-11M and IG narrowed upward to $80-81M, while adjusted opex guidance of $92-94M was maintained. Management flagged a small sequential decel implied in Q4 TearCare and deferred 2027 guidance to a future call.

QuinStreet reported record fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $416.7 million, up 46% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $42.7 million, up 108% and at a 10.2% margin (300 bps expansion). Adjusted EPS was $0.50. Financial services grew 31% to $271 million on 42% auto insurance growth, and home services grew 86% to $145.7 million. Management guided fiscal Q2 revenue to $360-380 million and adjusted EBITDA to $32-33 million, and raised full-year FY2027 guidance to $1.5-1.6 billion revenue and $155-165 million adjusted EBITDA (20% and 42% growth at midpoints).

CPI reported record quarterly revenue of $158 million (up 15% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $27 million (up 17% YoY), driven by double-digit growth across all segments. Management increased full-year guidance for revenue growth and free cash flow to the low double digits and $50-$55 million respectively, while reaffirming adjusted EBITDA growth guidance. The company ended the quarter with net leverage of 2.6x.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $83.4M, down 12% YoY, but up 21% excluding the prior-year $25.9M China deferred sales; China grew 31% ex-deferred item and ex-China rose 13%. GAAP net income was $5.6M ($0.11/diluted share) versus a $6.3M net loss ($0.13) ex-item a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA of $14.4M ($0.28/share) versus $8.9M ($0.18) ex-item. Gross margin fell to 70.9% from 82.2% (75.5% ex-item), pressured by ERP-related low production volumes, freight, tariffs, and inventory provisions; management expects Q4 gross margin above Q3 and further improvement in 2027. No formal Q4 or FY2027 guidance was given, though management said China would grow versus last year with a seasonal Q4 decline, and the $225M adjusted opex target was reaffirmed; a $50M buyback was authorized in September.

Novo Nordisk reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted sales growth of 4% (DKK 79.2 billion) and adjusted operating profit growth of 27%, driven by GLP-1 volume growth in obesity and a favorable comparison base from prior transformation costs. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted sales growth to -2% to +2% at CER, citing improved expectations for international operations and the impact of the U.S. Bridge program, while acknowledging headwinds from loss of exclusivity in Canada and price dynamics in China.

Continuing-operations revenue rose 35.9% YoY to $12.6 million in Q3 FY2026, with nine-month revenue up ~48% to $30 million and a year-to-date book-to-bill of 1.46 on $43.6 million of bookings. Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to approximately 40% (roughly $45 million) from a prior 25%-30%, and guided FY gross margin to 40%-42% with adjusted EBITDA of $0.5-$1 million. Q3 gross margin fell to 40.6% from 45.6% a year ago on product mix, and GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $0.6 million (-$0.02/share), with adjusted EBITDA of $0.3 million hit by $544K of bad debt and $394K of legal expense (about $1.2 million excluding those items). Cash used in continuing operations was $12.4 million for the nine months, driven by the $6.25 million legal settlement and a $7.8 million inventory build ahead of expected growth.

Navigator reported record reported net income of $78.3 million and EPS of $1.28 driven by a $48 million gain on vessel sales, while underlying adjusted EBITDA was $67.8 million. Utilization recovered to approximately 94% in September from an 87.9% quarterly average, with TCE averaging $30,314 per day. Management maintains full-year guidance for operating expenses and interest but refrained from providing specific fourth-quarter revenue or EPS guidance.

Nuvectis Pharma reported a net loss of $30.1 million for Q3 FY2026, excluding upfront license payments and milestones, with an adjusted net loss of $5.8 million. The company ended the quarter with approximately $140 million in cash, providing a runway into the second half of 2029. Management highlighted significant pipeline progress, including China approval for NXP100 (ciprocopan) in PNH and breakthrough designation for NXP200 in glioma, while outlining plans to file US INDs by year-end.

Nuvation Bio reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $45 million, driven by $27.5 million in U.S. net IBTROZI product revenue (18% sequential growth) and $17.5 million in collaboration/license revenue. Despite a 15% decline in total new patient starts across the ROS1 TKI market, the company maintained its position as the leading ROS1 TKI with over 60% share of first-line new patient starts. Management reiterated that quarterly fluctuations are expected in this ultra-rare disease and provided no specific financial guidance updates.

NETGEAR reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $167.3 million, down 9.3% year-over-year and below the midpoint of its guidance range ($165M-$175M), primarily due to manufacturing constraints at a key partner that limited supply fulfillment despite robust underlying demand. The company delivered non-GAAP EPS of $0.13 and non-GAAP operating income above the high end of its guidance range, reflecting strong enterprise margins (53.2%) but offset by a consumer contribution loss of $1.4 million. Management raised Q4 revenue guidance to $160M-$175M, acknowledging that production delays will persist into Q1 2027.

NRP generated $45 million of free cash flow in Q3 2026, a slight increase over the prior year period driven by higher metallurgical coal pricing and volumes, while soda ash net income decreased $2 million due to oversupply. The partnership raised its quarterly distribution to $2.34 per common unit following the full repayment of its Opco Credit Facility. Management noted that 2027 outlook for coal remains stable barring geopolitical shifts, while the soda ash market is expected to take years to rebalance.

Nomad Foods reported Q3 FY2026 results where management held EBITDA guidance despite negative EBITDA expectations for Q4 driven by inflation on fish and pricing variability. The company reiterated its 2027 outlook with gross inflation assumptions around 7% and savings targets of roughly 3%, maintaining a net inflation expectation of 4%. While the CEO expressed satisfaction in maintaining guidance, the forward range for Q4 implies significant downside risk from cost pressures.

NNN reported Q3 2026 AFFO per share of $0.91 and Core FFO of $0.90, up 5.8% and 5.9% YoY, ahead of internal projections on lower bad debt and higher interest/other income from bankruptcy settlements and land sales. Full-year 2026 AFFO guidance of $3.55-$3.59 (3.8% growth at midpoint) was maintained, with bad debt now expected at ~25 bps of ABR versus 40 bps prior and disposition guidance raised $30M to $160-180M, partly offset by $1M higher G&A from dead deal costs. The key change was a mid-September repricing of the acquisition pipeline, with cap rates up 30-40 bps for Q4 and $50-60 bps on some deals, causing walk-aways and implying a Q4 acquisition slowdown. Occupancy was 99.2%, NOI margin 96.7%, net debt to EBITDAre 5.6x (5.3x pro forma), and the dividend was raised 3.3% to $0.62 for a 37th consecutive annual increase.

Navios reported Q3 2026 revenue of $432 million, up 25% YoY from $347 million, with net income of $185.7 million ($6.42 per unit) and adjusted EBITDA up roughly $78 million to $272 million. Adjusted net income nearly doubled to $164 million versus $84 million, driven by combined TCE rising 26% to $30,371/day, with dry bulk TCE up 43% and tankers up 38% while containers slipped 1%. Contracted revenue backlog hit a record $5 billion, extending past 2030, and management committed roughly $703 million to seven newbuildings plus a $735 million new charter contract, alongside $90 million of accelerated debt repayment that pushed net LTV to 23.1%. No formal numeric guidance was given, but Q4 is 80% fixed at $31,837/day and 2027 is 56% fixed at $29,605/day against a very strong tanker rate environment.

NICE reported Q3 total revenue of $791 million, up 8% YoY, and non-GAAP EPS of $2.84, both above the high end of guidance, helped partly by stronger product revenue in financial crime and compliance. Cloud revenue grew 10.6% (12.2% ex a $10 million atypical customer credit) and CXAI ARR reached $392 million, up 46% YoY, while CXone backlog grew 27% YoY versus 15% for total cloud backlog. Full-year total revenue guidance was reiterated at $3.17-3.19 billion (8% growth at midpoint) and EPS guidance was raised to $11.12-$11.32, but cloud growth guidance now implies roughly 12% ex-credit, with management calling out slower AI ramps, standalone WFM, FCC cloud migration, and weaker Q4 seasonality than last year. Management announced a ~5% workforce reduction with $15-20 million in restructuring charges and lowered its free cash flow margin outlook to 10%-12% reported, while reiterating confidence in reaccelerating cloud growth in 2027-2028.

Navient reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $0.16 and core EPS of $0.03, with a net $0.27 per share drag from significant items including $162 million of gains on legacy loan sales, a $13 million held-for-sale provision benefit, $224 million of provision on previously originated loans, and a $15 million regulatory expense benefit. Originations grew nearly 80% overall, with refinance up 65% and in-school up 84% (graduate up over 170%), while the consumer lending segment swung to $2 million of net income from a $76 million loss a year ago. The quarter included large credit provisions: $211 million on previously originated private loans tied to elevated legacy delinquencies and weaker pre-2025 refi vintages, plus $29 million on $1.4 billion of loans moved to held-for-sale; the allowance increase signals credit performance has lagged prior forecasts. Management maintains full-year operating expenses at $350 million or lower and expects roughly $700 million of Q4 originations, with rising benchmark rates (about 120 bps since September) compressing refi returns toward the high single-digit ROE and potentially pressuring future volumes.

Progyny reported record revenue and profitability for Q3 FY2026, driven by a strong watching season that added 1.3 million new covered lives and over 85 new clients. Management raised the midpoint of full-year 2026 guidance to $1.365 billion-$1.385 billion (5.9%-7.5% growth) and expects Q4 revenue between $344.7 million and $364.7 million. Gross margin expanded 130 bps year-over-year due to reduced stock compensation and operational efficiencies, while the company generated over $56 million in operating cash flow.

Net sales fell 9% reported (7% constant currency) to $116.6M against a record prior-year quarter, with China down 52% constant currency and North America down 6% to $34M. Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $11.1M from $15.2M and operating cash flow fell to $10.8M from $18.5M, though gross margin held at 72.9% versus 73.3%. Full-year 2026 guidance was cut to $460-470M revenue and $44-48M Adjusted EBITDA from the August range of $490-500M and $48-52M, with China expected to remain a headwind into 2027.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $27.2 million, with Tru Niagen down 10% YoY to $23.3 million and net loss of $1.2 million (-$0.01 per diluted share) versus net income of $0.06 per diluted share a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA was positive at $450,000 with $2.6 million operating cash flow and $69.5 million cash, no debt. Gross margin was 62.9% versus 64.5% a year ago (the transcript labels this the second quarter), G&A rose $1.1 million on legal expenses, and S&M was 32% of net sales versus 25.8%. Guidance is qualitative only: Q4 revenue expected to improve sequentially, with 2026 framed as an investment year and ramping S&M, R&D and G&A spend ahead of 2027 launches.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $202.7 million, down 1% year-over-year but up 6% sequentially, with total test volumes down 2% YoY as prenatal volume fell 11%. Gross margin of 67.9% improved 130 bps sequentially but fell 200 bps YoY, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $5 million with adjusted EPS of -$0.11. Management raised the full-year 2026 revenue midpoint to $785 million from $780 million, citing the ~$10 million Q3 outperformance partly offset by ~$5 million of expected prenatal softness tied to the announced $210 million plus inventory divestiture to Labcorp. Cancer Care Continuum revenue rose 1% YoY on 4% volume growth offset by a 3% ASP decline, and the company continues to guide to modest 1%-5% HCT ASP pressure while flagging Ascend cost initiatives with detail deferred to 2027.

Q3 FY2026 revenue of $44.0M came in within the $41.5M-$45.5M guidance range but fell 4.3% YoY and 1.6% QoQ. Gross margin of 14% missed the low end of the 17%-19% guidance, driven by a sharp Korean won appreciation, and non-GAAP diluted loss per share widened to $0.29 from $0.13 in Q2. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $41M-$45M (midpoint down 2.2% sequentially, up 6% YoY) and gross margin of 10%-12%, with management calling Q4 the low point in the gross margin trajectory as Gumi fab operations normalize.

Manitowoc reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $614 million, up 11% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $47 million (up 39%) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 7.7%, up 150 bps. Orders rose 38% to $676 million with a 1.1x book-to-bill, and backlog reached over $1.1 billion, up $444 million YoY. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $160-175 million and adjusted DEPS to $0.90-1.25, but flagged that hitting the free cash flow midpoint requires roughly $90 million in Q4 and noted $30-50 million of inflation and tariff costs still not fully offset. Free cash flow was a use of $42 million in the quarter, driven by a $20 million receivables build.

Materion reported record value-added sales of $313.7 million, up 19% YoY, and record adjusted EPS of $1.93, up 37% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $70.7 million (22.5% of VA sales) expanding 150 bps for a fourth consecutive quarter of YoY margin expansion. All three segments grew double digits, with Electronic Materials VA sales up 30% and its EBITDA up 54% on 500 bps of margin expansion, while aerospace and defense rose more than 40% and telecom/data center more than 70%. The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $7.10-$7.40 from a prior $6.80-$7.20, its third outlook increase of the year, and now expects high-teens 2026 top-line growth. Incoming orders and backlog reached record levels, with order rate up about 25% and backlog up approximately 35% YoY.

Matador's Q3 2026 call carried almost no explicit quarterly financials: no revenue, EPS, or margin figures were stated, though Joe Foran cited production growth of 10% to over 230,000 BOE/day from year-end 2025 reserves of 667 million BOE and a reserve base now above 700 million BOE. The dividend was raised 17% from $1.50 to $1.75, the eighth increase in five years, and management cited a gas realizations swing from paying $0.79 at Waha to receiving $2.99 via Hugh Brinson, moving gas cash flow from negative $38 million in Q2 to $162 million. 2027 guidance was only qualitative (mid-single-digit growth on current prices), with the capital program explicitly deferred to February, and $150 million of the roughly $500-$600 million borrowed has been repaid.

Motorola reported Q3 revenue up 12% to about $3.3B with double-digit growth in both segments and all three technologies, non-GAAP EPS of $4.69 (up 16%) and non-GAAP operating margin of 32.5% (up 200 bps), with revenue and EPS both above guidance. GAAP EPS fell to $3.06 on an $87M non-cash Silvus earnout charge. Backlog hit a record $16.6B (up 14% YoY, $1B sequentially) on record Q3 orders up over 20%, and the company raised FY26 revenue guidance to ~$13.05B from $12.975B, non-GAAP EPS to $17.94-$17.99 from $17.62-$17.72, and operating cash flow to $3.05B. Management also gave preliminary 2027 color of ~$14.25B revenue with organic growth stronger than 2026 and further margin expansion despite memory costs that could double.

Maravai reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $45.9 million, up 10% year-over-year, with TriLink up 12% (mRNA +28%, GMP consumables +30%, discovery mRNA +27%) and Cygnus up 8%. Adjusted gross margin expanded more than 1,700 bps to 57.7%, adjusted EBITDA improved $16.6 million to $5.8 million, and GAAP loss per share narrowed to $0.09 from $0.18. Management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $212-$216 million from $205-$215 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $40-$42 million from $33-$35 million, while noting GMP and CDMO quarterly lumpiness and no high-volume CleanCap COVID revenue in the quarter.

Mosaic reported a difficult fiscal Q3 2026, curtailing phosphate production at Bartow and Louisiana and idling mining at South Fort Meade and Miski Mayo due to high sulfur costs, while potash production fell short of guidance and was cut by roughly 400,000 tons for the year. Q4 sulfur is contracted at $615/ton versus $715 realized in Q3, but cost-of-goods sulfur is guided to $800-$850/ton with ammonia at $590-$610/ton, producing mid-$300s stripping margins. Management guided Q4 phosphate EBITDA to be a trough and expects 2027 SG&A below $500 million and CapEx below $1 billion, while stating phosphate demand is constrained by supply and that curtailed assets will not restart until stripping margins improve sustainably.

Q3 revenue of $80.3M came in well below the $86M-$89M guide and grew 15% YoY; adjusted EBITDA of $19.9M missed the $22M-$25M guide. Q4 guidance was cut to $75M-$78M revenue and $8M-$10M adjusted EBITDA, and FY26 revenue guidance was lowered to $311M-$314M (~10% YoY growth) with EBITDA of $66M-$68M. Management attributed the shortfall to go-to-market execution, citing a redesigned sales compensation plan that drove roughly 40% attrition among experienced quota-carrying sellers; a new CEO (Tony Weisman) was appointed effective November 2nd. Gross margin held at 79% and expansion remained north of 115%, but the disruption is assumed to persist through Q4.

Pre-revenue biopharma with no product revenue; Q3 FY2026 net loss widened to $57.3 million from $36.9 million a year ago on G&A of $37.4 million (vs $9.7M) for launch preparation, partly offset by R&D falling to $22.7 million from $31.5 million. Cash and investments were $624.7 million at September 30, 2026 (from $656.6 million at year-end 2025), with runway into 2028. All forward commentary centers on the December 22, 2026 PDUFA date for lorundrostat and launch readiness; no product guidance, pricing, or launch metrics were provided. The key change versus prior periods is the ramp in commercial spend and headcount ahead of a potential approval.

Martin Marietta reported record Q3 aggregates revenue of $1.7 billion (up 14%) and cash gross profit of $696 million (up 6%), but growth was entirely acquisition-driven, with organic aggregates shipments down 1.1% and organic cash gross profit down $25 million. Organic pricing rose 2.7% excluding mix, while COGS per ton ex-freight rose 5.6% (5.1% organic) on diesel and energy inflation, partly offset by flat organic labor cost per ton. Full-year 2026 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA midpoints were updated to $7.8 billion and $2.48 billion, reflecting stronger acquisition contributions (LNA added $216 million revenue and $115 million cash gross profit since the August 21 close) partially offset by lower heritage expectations, with softer shipments and price-cost pressure persisting through Q4. Preliminary 2027 outlook calls for mid-to-high single-digit mix-adjusted aggregates pricing growth, though reported ASP growth is guided to mid-single digits as lower-priced acquisitions temper the headline.

Group adjusted property EBITDA was approximately $288 million, or about $298 million adjusting for VIP hold, with unfavorable VIP win rates at City of Dreams Macau denting property EBITDA by roughly $14 million. Macau daily OPEX fell to about $3.2 million, below prior guidance, and Melco repurchased roughly 33.1 million ADSs for about $160 million between July 1 and November 3, bringing 2026 buybacks to about 47.1 million ADSs for $236 million. Management flagged a challenging demand backdrop, noting October market GGR was down 10% and citing China consumption weakness, World Cup aftereffects, and overseas tax issues, while saying company performance outpaced the broader market in October. CapEx guidance was lowered to about $375 million for 2026 and $275 million for 2027, and a dividend restart is still targeted potentially toward the end of next year.

MITT reported Q3 2026 GAAP net loss of $15.7 million, or $0.49 per share, and book value fell 7.3% to $9.27 from $10.00, with the entire decline occurring in September; economic return was -4.9% including the $0.24 dividend. EAD of $0.21 per share came in just shy of the $0.24 dividend, with Arc Home break-even after July-August profitability was reversed by September volatility. Management pointed to roughly $0.15-$0.20 of incremental annual EAD in 2027 from resolving $28 million of legacy commercial loans into ~20% ROE home equity, but declined to give a book value update or a Q4 Arc Home outlook, noting the home equity origination ramp is a longer-term driver rather than a next-quarter one.

Magnite reported Q3 revenue of $204 million (+14%) and contribution ex-TAC of $201 million (+20%), beating its guide by over $10 million, with CTV ex-TAC of $105 million (+39%) and DV+ of $95 million (+5%). Adjusted EBITDA rose 46% to $83 million at a 42% margin versus 34% last year, and non-GAAP EPS was $0.33 versus $0.20. Management raised full-year 2026 contribution ex-TAC growth to ~17% from 13%-14%, EBITDA growth to ~30% from >20%, margin to ~38.5% from at least 37%, and free cash flow growth to >60% from the high-40s range. Political spend of ~$12 million in Q3 and >$40 million expected for 2026, versus $15 million previously projected, was the largest single swing, and 2027 top-line growth ex-political is guided to over 15% with no Google Remedies upside included.

MFA reported a Q3 2026 GAAP net loss of $111.7 million, or $1.19 per basic share, as GAAP book value fell to $11.12 and economic book value to $11.44 per share, down 12.5% and 13.3% respectively from June 30, driven by roughly $153 million of mark-to-market declines as the 10-year rose about 85 bps and mortgage spreads widened. Net interest income including TBA dollar roll income rose to $63.4 million from $60.2 million, DE was $0.26 per share versus $0.12 in Q2, and DE prior to realized credit losses was $0.44 per share, or about $0.39 excluding roughly $0.05 of non-recurring items, up 11% quarter over quarter. Management flagged approximately $1.3 billion of 1.4% pay-fixed swaps maturing at year-end and into Q1 2027 that contribute about $0.08 per share per quarter, adding variability to the DE outlook, while noting economic book value has risen about 5% since quarter-end on a rate rally. The 60-plus-day delinquency rate improved to 6.7% from 7.0%, legacy multifamily UPB fell below $300 million, and realized credit losses declined to $18.9 million.

DoorDash used its Q3 FY2026 call almost entirely to discuss the pending acquisition of Instacart, with management citing 'record highs in top-line, bottom line,' accelerating U.S. restaurant marketplace growth (fastest sequential growth in five-plus years), accelerating Wolt and Deliveroo growth, and new verticals nearing gross-profit breakeven by year-end. No specific revenue, EPS, margin, or formal guidance figures were read into the transcript. Management outlined a multi-year path to $500 million or more in annual net synergies, with year one fully reinvested, year three delivering the $500 million to the bottom line, and reaffirmed the tech-stack re-platform on track for completion in the first half of 2027. The key change versus the prior period is the announced Instacart deal, framed as playing offense from a position of strength.

Total revenue was $42.0 million, up 12.5% YoY, with Greenbrook up 20.1% to $26.2 million and NeuroStar up 1.8% to $15.8 million on record capital system sales partly offset by lower session revenue. Gross margin expanded to 52.2% from 45.9%, opex fell 12.6% to $21.3 million, operating income was $0.5 million versus a $7.3 million loss, and adjusted EBITDA was $1.9 million versus -$4.7 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was unchanged at $160-164 million, while opex guidance was lowered to $92.5-95.5 million and cash burn guidance tightened to -$10 to -$12 million. Q3 operating and investing cash flow turned positive at $0.8 million versus -$0.9 million a year ago.

Champion Homes reported Q2 FY2027 net sales up 6.2% YoY, in line with its mid-single-digit expectation, with 6,922 homes sold (+2.2%), U.S. ASP up 4.1% to ~$102,700, adjusted gross margin of 25.5% and adjusted EBITDA of $76 million (10.5% margin). Manufacturing orders rose 17% YoY and backlog reached ~$500 million, up 18.6% sequentially, with lead times extending to ~11 weeks. Q3 guidance calls for revenue growth of 8%-10%, but adjusted gross margin is guided down to 24%-25% as management said material cost inflation accelerated faster than assumed, notably in steel and petroleum-based inputs. Management also completed the Homes Direct acquisition and announced Timberline Homes (~$100 million annualized revenue, nine locations), expected to close in Q4.

Paycom reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $544 million, up 10% year-over-year, with non-GAAP net income rising 37% to $150 million ($3.37 per diluted share). Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue (now $2.213B-$2.218B) and Adjusted EBITDA (now $1.069B-$1.079B), citing strong year-to-date execution and expanding margins of 48.5% at the midpoint. The company highlighted new product launches like Asset Management, a 65% increase in AI usage for IWant, and continued share buybacks.

Third quarter revenue increased year-over-year to $341 million driven by resident fees from the operating portfolio, while net income decreased due to $60 million in transition-related expenses and a prior period gain. Management raised full-year Adjusted FFO guidance to a range of $3.28-$3.30 per share (midpoint $3.29), reflecting strong investment activity including $1.5 billion deployed year-to-date. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with leverage at 3.1x and no revolver borrowings outstanding.

OPENLANE reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $561 million (up 13% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $107 million (up 23% YoY). Management narrowed full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $390-$400 million from the prior range of $385-$400 million, citing a normal seasonal dip in Q4 dealer volumes and increased go-to-market spending. While U.S. dealer and commercial businesses showed strong growth, Canadian results were impacted by macroeconomic headwinds.

Beauty reported Q2 FY2027 net sales growth of 51% (organic ~35%, rhode contributing ~16 points from the pre-anniversary month), with U.S. sales +25% and international +165%; adjusted EBITDA rose 86% to $123 million and adjusted EPS came in at $1.21 versus $0.68 a year ago. Gross margin was 71%, up ~160 bps, of which 30 bps came from tariff refunds. Management raised FY2027 guidance across the board: net sales growth to 22%-24% from 18%-20%, organic growth to 9%-11% from 6%-7%, adjusted EBITDA to $421M-$427M from $401M-$407M, and adjusted EPS to $3.82-$3.86 from $3.50-$3.55. The raised outlook is tempered by planned reinvestment of the $52 million in tariff refunds into pricing and marketing, which pushes second-half adjusted EBITDA margin to the low teens and keeps full-year gross margin roughly flat excluding refunds.

Viavi reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $469.3M, above the $450-460M guide, up 5.9% sequentially and 56.9% YoY, with EPS of $0.47 versus $0.40-0.42 guided. Operating margin of 29% beat the 26.7-27.5% range and expanded 12.7 points YoY, though it included roughly $11M (~110 bps) of tariff refunds. Q2 guidance calls for revenue of $505-515M and EPS of $0.50-0.52, with management expecting sequential growth through the rest of the fiscal year and the $2B revenue run rate now pulled forward to the end of this calendar year from end of next year. NSE grew 74.1% YoY to $376.1M on data center and A&D demand, while wireless remains the lone weak spot.

Ovintiv reported Q3 FY2026 cash flow of $4.51 per share and free cash flow of $680 million, both beating consensus estimates. Total production volumes came in just above the midpoint of guidance at 204,000 barrels per day for oil and condensate, with Permian performance exceeding expectations while Montney volumes were slightly below the low end due to higher Canadian royalties and third-party facility downtime. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged despite reallocating $50 million of capital from the Montney to the Permian.

Wolfspeed reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $155 million, slightly above the midpoint of guidance, with power revenue of $117 million up 10% sequentially and materials roughly $38 million. Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin was negative 12.8%, a 710 bps sequential improvement driven by higher utilization and mix, while operating cash flow was negative $84 million and adjusted EBITDA negative $55 million. Q2 guidance targets revenue of $155-$175 million and gross margin approaching break-even sequentially, with opex of $65-$69 million. The most significant development was the announced conditional 30-year, $1.5 billion U.S. Department of War loan commitment, whose initial $600 million tranche is expected to refinance the 2030 first lien notes, delivering more than $50 million in annual interest savings and roughly $100 million in annual cash interest savings given five years of payment-in-kind interest.

Procore reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $402 million (including DroneDeploy) or $397 million excluding it, beating the high end of guidance by $13 million with growth accelerating to 18.7% YoY and 17.1% organically. Non-GAAP operating margins expanded to 23.5%, significantly exceeding the high end of the prior range. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by approximately $21 million at the high end and increased the non-GAAP operating margin outlook by 50 basis points to a range of 19%-19.5%.

rows.company_name: Arm Holdings plc American Depositary Shares
rows.key_quote: Arm reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.44B, up 27% YoY, with license revenue up 50% to $773M and royalty revenue up 8% to $670M; non-GAAP EPS rose 33% to $0.52 and operating margin expanded 300 bps to 44.2%. Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $1.54B ±$50M (about 24% YoY growth) and EPS of $0.56 ±$0.04, with royalties expected to grow low single digits YoY on edge AI weakness while license revenue grows over 50% YoY. The key change versus prior guidance is increased confidence in the Arm AGI CPU silicon business, now targeting up to $2B in revenue across FY2027–FY2028 (up from more than $1B), with shipments starting in Q4 FY2027. Edge AI royalties were roughly flat as higher memory prices pressured smartphone units, partly offset by higher Armv9/CSS royalty rates.

Eagle Materials reported record Q2 revenue of $653 million, up 2% year over year, driven by record cement volume and higher wallboard and recycled paperboard volume. However, higher diesel-related freight and raw material costs pushed EPS down 14% to $3.63 and operating earnings down 12% in heavy materials and 13% in light materials. Management announced cement and aggregates price increases of $10-$15 per ton effective January 1, 2027, and expects cost headwinds to persist. Wallboard demand remains challenged by high interest rates, and the Mountain Cement plant modernization faces commissioning risk and recent operational disruptions.

Revenue rose 10% YoY to $49.9 million (4% organic), with Recorded Music up 18% to $15.4 million and Music Publishing up 8% to $33.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA and OIBDA both grew 14% to $22.1 million and $20.7 million, net income doubled to $4.6 million, and diluted EPS rose to $0.07 from $0.03. Full-year guidance was narrowed and raised to revenue of $188-192 million (~8% growth at midpoint) and Adjusted EBITDA of $77-80 million (~7% growth), with the CFO citing appropriate conservatism in the EBITDA outlook. Net debt ticked up to $433.8 million from $429.8 million at March 31.

8x8 reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $192.0 million (up 4.3% YoY) and service revenue of $187.8 million (up 4.9% YoY), with platform usage revenue up ~51% YoY. Non-GAAP operating margin was 10.8% ($20.7 million operating income) and EPS was $0.12, with the company stating it exceeded the high end of guidance for service revenue, total revenue, operating margin, EPS, and cash flow from operations ($13.1 million). Full-year FY2027 guidance was raised: service revenue to $732-752 million (+$7 million), total revenue to $750-770 million (+$5 million), EPS to $0.36-0.40 (from $0.33-0.38), and operating cash flow to $49-54 million. Q3 guidance implies platform usage growth moderating to 35-45% YoY from 51%, and gross margin of 58-60%, slightly below Q2's 60.1% on continued usage mix shift.

PacBio reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $40.6 million, a 6% year-over-year increase driven by instrument sales and consumable growth, though gross margin contracted to 36% due to memory costs and manufacturing transition expenses. Management narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $155-$160 million and lowered annual operating expense guidance to $203-$207 million following restructuring savings. The company maintained a year-end cash target of $175-$185 million while acknowledging continued constraints in academic funding and the ongoing transition to new chemistry.

PACs Group reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.5 billion (up 11.5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $175.7 million (up 33.6% YoY), driven by a 6.4% same-store revenue increase and margin expansion to 11.7%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue to $5.95-$6.05 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $685-$695 million, incorporating contributions from recent acquisitions in Florida and Texas. The company highlighted strong same-store occupancy gains of 200 bps and successful remediation of internal control weaknesses.

Revenue of $559.5M came in above the midpoint of guidance, up 22% sequentially but flat year-over-year, with GAAP EPS of $2.23 and non-GAAP EPS of $2.70. Non-GAAP gross margin of 53.8% and operating margin of 28.5% benefited from a temporary wafer cost benefit that management said made this a high point. Q3 guidance of $510-570M implies a sequential decline, which the CFO attributed to timing (December revenue pulled into September) rather than a demand change, while gross margin is guided down to 51-53%. PC headwinds have not eased and OEMs have pushed out new model launches, offsetting content gains in smartphones.

ATS reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of CAD 666 million, down 8.6% YoY and in line with its guide, with adjusted earnings from operations of CAD 57.4 million (down 27.4%) and adjusted margin of 8.6% versus 10.9% last year, as gross margin contracted 131 bps to 28.6% on mix and absorption. Management withdrew its prior full-year goals for modest revenue growth and margin expansion, citing packaging order delays tied to Section 338 tariffs plus cyclical weakness in food and beverage and transportation repositioning; Q3 revenue is guided to CAD 640-680 million. Offsetting the miss, order bookings rose 12.7% to CAD 827 million, life sciences backlog hit a record CAD 1.2 billion, trailing 12-month book-to-bill was 1.05, and operating cash flow improved to CAD 81 million from CAD 28 million. The Fixed Cost Transformation Program remains on track for CAD 65-75 million of net annualized savings (~250 bps) over 15 months, and the company repurchased ~2.2 million shares for CAD 61 million.

Par Pacific reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $10.70 per share and adjusted EBITDA of $646 million, driven by a Hawaii turnaround completion and strong mainland margins averaging $38.45/bbl. The company achieved a historic milestone of becoming a net cash position with $2.4 billion in liquidity after fully repaying ABL borrowings. Management provided specific Q4 throughput guidance for all refineries (e.g., Hawaii 85k-89k bpd) and noted that while the Hawaii crude differential is expected to soften slightly, clean product freight pass-throughs provide meaningful offsets.

Ocugen reported a net loss of $0.01 per share for Q3 FY2026, an improvement from the $0.07 loss in the prior year quarter, with total operating expenses of $19.7 million compared to $19.4 million previously. The company advanced its three late-stage programs into Phase III, dosing the first patient in the OCU410 GA trial and completing enrollment for the OCU400 RP trial. Management confirmed a cash runway extending into 2028 and reiterated on-track progress toward filing three BLAs by 2028.

Consolidated revenue from continuing operations grew 16% to $65.4 million in Q3 FY2026, driven by growth in global products and mazdutide royalties. The company announced a definitive agreement to watch its BioReference assets to Labcorp for approximately $722 million, reclassifying the segment as discontinued operations. Management withdrew full-year guidance due to the pending transaction but provided updated Q4 revenue expectations of $62-$72 million.

Q1 FY2027 revenue fell 15% YoY to $280 million (from $329 million), but the adjusted EBITDA loss of $17 million improved by more than $15 million YoY, and adjusted EBITDA for the trailing 12 months totaled $124 million, up 30%. Healthcare Services revenue dropped 16% on the Inflation Reduction Act, yet segment adjusted EBITDA rose 56% to $11 million, and EBITDA per member reached $108, up over 60%. Senior revenue decreased to $51 million with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $12 million (down from $21 million a year ago), and Life adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to $7 million (17% margin, up more than 500 bps). The $60+ million fiscal 2027 operating cash flow target was reiterated rather than raised, and the smaller agent force underpinning the season will reduce Medicare Advantage policy volumes by roughly 10%-15%, per prior guidance.

Twin Disc reported Q1 FY2027 sales of $88.7 million, up 10.9% YoY (11.8% organic), with gross margin flat at 28.7%, operating income more than doubling to $4.6 million, net income of $3.4 million ($0.24/share) versus a $0.04 loss a year ago, and EBITDA of $7.7 million, up 62.6%. Six-month backlog reached a record $190.6 million, up 7% sequentially and from $163.3 million a year ago, with defense now ~24% of backlog versus ~17% at year-end and defense backlog up ~104% YoY. Free cash flow swung to $5.6 million from negative $11 million and net debt fell to $13.1 million (0.4x leverage), though management guided FY2027 free cash flow conversion to only 20%-40% versus its 60% long-term target and expects gross margins broadly in line with fiscal 2026.

PayPay reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of JPY 118.1 billion, up 27.7% YoY, exceeding the upper end of its guidance range, with adjusted EBITDA of JPY 42.1 billion, up 54.8% YoY, and a 36% margin. Net income fell to JPY 18.4 billion due to the absence of a prior-year one-time tax benefit, though profit would have increased excluding that item. GMV growth slowed to 20% YoY from 23% in Q1, and management expects lower take rate in Q3 and Q4 due to heightened online payment controls and a high base for financial services interest income. The company broadly revised its full-year guidance upward based on strong first-half results, though it flagged a lower adjusted EBITDA margin in Q4 on seasonal expenses and expected policy rate hikes.

Third quarter revenue was $2.5 billion, down $195 million year-over-year due to lower roofing volumes from weak storm activity and softer demand in the Doors segment. The company reported a net loss of $248 million driven by a $476 million non-cash impairment charge in the Doors business, though Adjusted EBITDA was $489 million with a 20% margin. Management lowered Q4 revenue guidance to $2 billion-$2.2 billion and expects enterprise Adjusted EBITDA margins of 10%-12%, citing continued inflationary pressure and destocking.

Envista reported Q3 2026 core sales growth of 2.7% and adjusted EPS growth of 25%, driven by price contributions of $12 million and factory productivity. Management raised full-year guidance for core sales (3.75%-4.25%) and adjusted EPS ($1.54-$1.58), narrowing the ranges from prior expectations. The quarter included a one-time foreign currency gain in GAAP results, while China revenue declined low double-digits due to VBP preparations.

PureCycle reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.3 million (down from $4.5 million in Q2) and an operating loss of $37.5 million, driven by production limitations from reliability issues and a New Jersey regulatory extension that delayed approximately 15 food contact programs. Management noted monthly operations spending came in below the prior range at $7.8 million, but emphasized that the quarter fell short of internal revenue goals due to these specific headwinds rather than a lack of demand. While management expressed confidence in solving reliability issues and securing new branded orders (including L'Oréal and P&G), they explicitly stated they could not provide firm guidance on when Ironton would reach break-even.

Modine reported Q2 FY2027 sales up 35% to a level implying strong data center momentum, with data center revenue +95% (Americas +132%, EMEA -6%) and Commercial HVAC sales +23%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to a 13.7% margin, but gross margin contracted 160 bps to 20.7% on material and tariff inflation, and adjusted EPS was $1.35, up 27%. FY2027 guidance was updated to exclude Performance Technologies post-spin, with total sales of $3.1B-$3.2B (+50-55%), data center growth raised to 80-90% and Commercial HVAC to 10-15%, but management flagged that margins will improve at a lower rate than originally anticipated, with data center EBITDA margin expected around 20%+ only by Q4.

Kyndryl reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $3.65 billion, down 1.9% year-over-year as reported and down 80 bps in constant currency, with adjusted EBITDA of $699 million at a 19.1% margin (up 190 bps) and adjusted pre-tax income of $150 million at a 4.1% margin (up 80 bps). Q2 signings were $4.1 billion and LTM signings $15.5 billion with a 1.04x book-to-bill, and U.S. revenue rose 9% (about six points from Kyndryl Consult growth and roughly three points from resolution of a commercial matter). Full-year FY2027 guidance was reaffirmed: adjusted pre-tax income of $600-700 million, revenue flat to down 2% in constant currency, and free cash flow of $400-500 million; FY2028 targets and the $1 billion free cash flow goal were described as on track. Kyndryl Consult growth decelerated to 6% constant currency in Q2 from 11% in Q1, which management called the low point of the year.

McKesson reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $111 billion, up 8% with growth in all four segments, and adjusted EPS of $11.68, up 18% (24% excluding prior-year Norway divestiture and US Oncology net gains). The company raised FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance to $45.60-$46.40 from $44.20-$45.00, implying 17%-19% growth, with revenue growth of 6%-10% and operating profit growth of 12%-16%. Gross profit rose 10% to $3.9 billion with opex as a percentage of gross profit improving about 141 bps, while North American Pharmaceutical operating profit grew 22% and Oncology & Multispecialty revenue grew 24%. Management also disclosed the roughly $2.25 billion Precision Medicine Group acquisition (closed this week) and a roughly $1.4 billion agreement for a 49% minority stake in Option Care Health, neither of which is fully reflected in segment margins.

Total consolidated revenues increased 10% to $769 million, driven by double-digit growth in digital subscriptions (14.6%) and digital advertising (12%). Adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.68 from $0.59 in the prior year period. While total subscription and ad revenues met guidance, digital advertising revenue came in slightly below the specific guidance range.

PGEN reported Q3 FY2026 net product revenue of $72.9 million, a 37% quarter-over-quarter increase driven by strong demand for its approved therapy PAPZIMEOS. The company achieved profitability in the quarter with net income of $35.8 million and generated positive operating cash flow of $11.9 million, surpassing prior guidance. Management highlighted that launch-to-date revenues reached approximately $151 million with over 500 patients treated.

Harley-Davidson raised full-year 2026 guidance: global retail and wholesale shipments both lifted to 135,500-139,000 units from 133,500-138,500, HDMC operating income to $25-55M from $10-50M, HDFS operating income to $60-70M, and capex cut to $140-165M from $175-200M. Q3 global retail rose 5% to ~35.8k units with North America up 9% (accelerating from 3% in Q2) and 37% U.S. 601+cc share, but wholesale units fell 8% to 33.6k, HDMC revenue fell 10% to $964M, and consolidated EPS fell to $0.40 from $3.10. HDMC gross margin expanded 173 bps to 28.1% and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 9.7% from 8.7%, while GAAP operating margin slipped to 4.6% on $14M restructuring. Full-year gross tariff costs were raised to ~$105-120M from $75-90M, offset by near-equal recoveries, and LiveWire withdrew guidance and disclosed substantial going-concern doubt.

Grab reported record adjusted EBITDA of $237 million, up 73% YoY, with its 19th consecutive quarter of EBITDA expansion, and raised full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance for the second time this year to $790-800 million (from $720-740 million). On-demand GMV grew 22% constant currency, MTUs hit a record 57 million, and all three segments were profitable with financial services at $12 million segment adjusted EBITDA. However, management deliberately guided Q4 EBITDA roughly flat sequentially on festive season driver incentives and fuel cost support, and noted Indonesia's new two-wheeler commission framework and elevated fuel prices as ongoing headwinds.

Match reported Q3 FY2026 with Tinder direct revenue down ~2% FX-neutral (same as Q2), Tinder MAU down ~6% (improved from -7%), and payers down ~4% (improved from -5%); DAU turned positive YoY in September for the first time in 3.5 years. Hinge grew revenue ~19%, E&E remained under pressure from the Azar redesign, and full-year expectations now land slightly above the midpoint of revenue guidance with Adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow both expected to exceed February targets. Tinder 2026 user givebacks came in at $25 million versus $60 million planned, driving ~2 points of the ~3-point revenue improvement versus February expectations. Guidance is largely intact with a new quantified 2027 headwind: IAP fees are expected to be a one-point Adjusted EBITDA margin drag next year from EU Apple fee increases (~$20 million) and Google partnership expiration in Q1 2027.

VYJUVEK Q3 revenue was $127.3 million, up 30% YoY, with $95.3 million U.S. and $32 million international, diluted EPS of $2.05 versus $2.66 a year ago, which included non-recurring tax benefits. Gross margin slipped to 94% from 96% on ex-U.S. mix, net income fell to $63.1 million from $79.4 million, and full-year non-GAAP R&D plus SG&A guidance was cut to $155-165 million from $175-195 million. The board authorized a $400 million buyback, and Germany and Italy pricing are finalized with an early-2027 Italy launch. Several clinical readouts slipped: KB801 NK enrollment and top-line now expected in 2027, KB407 CF interim to H1 2027, and KB803 ocular DEB last-patient-visit to February 2027, while Gorlin pilot data showed regression in all three patients.

Tempus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $411.5 million, up 23% year-over-year, with oncology revenue up 28% on 32% unit growth and data & apps revenue up 33%. Adjusted EBITDA was $25.6 million, and the company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.60-$1.605 billion while maintaining Adjusted EBITDA guidance of approximately $65 million. The quarter included new strategic collaborations with BMS and Pathos worth $192.5 million over five years and a partnership with Moderna and Merck, alongside progress on the pending Personalis acquisition.

Inspire reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $206.7 million, down 7.9% YoY but up 3% sequentially, with U.S. outperformance offsetting international softness; gross margin rose 20 bps to 86% on favorable Inspire V mix. Adjusted operating income fell to $1.9 million from $10.9 million, adjusted diluted EPS was $0.14, and GAAP diluted loss per share was $0.84 including $24.1 million of Project Horizon restructuring charges and a $7 million legal settlement. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $850-860 million with adjusted operating margin of 4.5%-5.5%, and management guided to low single-digit YoY revenue growth for 2027 after an estimated $120 million full-year coding/reimbursement impact (about $30 million in Q3). International declined on German destocking, and the company is redirecting roughly $30 million of annualized savings from Project Horizon into patient-flow initiatives and 40 additional field support roles.

Marriott reported Q3 FY2026 global RevPAR up 6.5% (U.S. & Canada +7.4%, luxury +12%, select service +6%), with gross fee revenues up 14% to $1.52 billion, adjusted EBITDA up 12% to $1.51 billion, and adjusted diluted EPS up 22% to $3.02. Full-year 2026 global RevPAR guidance was raised to 4.5%-5% from an initial 1.5%-2.5% range, gross fees now seen up ~13%, full-year adjusted EBITDA up ~13%, and EPS growth of 20%-21%. Preliminary 2027 RevPAR growth was indicated at 3.5%-4.5%. Offsets include Greater China roughly flat, a 12% Middle East RevPAR decline with a steeper Q4 drop expected, and own/leased revenue net down to $41 million from $70 million.

Pre-revenue nuclear fuel developer reported no product revenue; net loss was $20.4 million ($0.62/share) for the first nine months of 2026 versus $12.4 million ($0.55) a year earlier, with operating expenses up $11.1 million to $25.6 million and cash used in operations of $13.2 million versus $8.1 million. Cash and equivalents stood at approximately $236.7 million with no debt, after $48.9 million of net ATM proceeds year-to-date (only $4.5 million in Q3) with $91.4 million remaining on the $150 million program. Management highlighted the August selection into DOE's Nuclear Energy Launch Pad INL program as the pathway to a pilot manufacturing facility, but disclosed no binding construction commitments as of September 30 and said the Pilot Factory will be a significant multi-year investment requiring additional capital over time. First quantitative post-irradiation examination results are expected in the first half of 2027.

ISG reported Q3 revenue of $65.1 million, up 4.4% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $10 million (+18.7%) and margin expanding nearly 200 bps to 15.4%, a four-year high; GAAP EPS was $0.07 and adjusted EPS $0.10 versus $0.09. AI-related revenue grew 56% to almost $34 million, surpassing 50% of total revenue well ahead of the prior expectation of sometime in 2027, and recurring revenue rose nearly 8% to a record $30.5 million. Q4 guidance targets revenue of $64-65 million and adjusted EBITDA of $9-10 million, implying continued YoY growth and margin expansion but a modest sequential step-down from Q3. Management flagged Americas softness (flat revenue) with some engagements slipping into Q4, offset by Europe +6.2% and APAC +46.8%.

Tower reported record Q3 2026 revenue of $526M, up 33% YoY from $396M and 14% QoQ, with gross profit of $179M (+92% YoY), operating profit of $127M (2.5x YoY), net profit of $120M at a 23% net margin (vs 14% a year ago), and diluted EPS of $1.05 vs $0.47. Q4 mid-range revenue guidance is $600M, implying full-year 2026 revenue of ~$2.0B versus $1.57B in 2025, and management expects Q1 2027 to run above a $2.4B annual run rate with none of the typical first-quarter seasonality. The business model target was raised to $3.6B annual revenue (up $760M, +27%), 45% gross margin (from 39%), and $1.2B net profit (from a prior 26% net margin target), while Q4 SiPho annualized run rate is guided above $1.1B and SiPho start capacity is targeted to 3x Q3 levels by Q3 2027.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $91.9 million, up 7.1% YoY, as lymphedema grew 13.1% to $81.8 million while airway clearance fell 25.1% to $10 million on DME inventory destocking. Gross margin expanded 90 bps to 76.7%, but higher opex pushed operating income down to $9.6 million from $11 million and adjusted EBITDA to $14.3 million (15.6% margin) from $14.4 million. Full-year revenue guidance was maintained at $360-$366 million even as the airway clearance outlook was cut to a mid-to-high single-digit decline from roughly flat; adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $50-$52 million from prior levels. Q4 lymphedema growth is expected to moderate against a 16% prior-year comparison.

Syndax reported Q3 2026 total revenue of $83.3 million, up 82% year-over-year, with Revuforj net revenue of $60.7 million (+90% YoY, +11% QoQ) and Niktimvo collaboration revenue of $22.6 million. Management reaffirmed 2026 R&D plus SG&A guidance of approximately $400 million and raised the Niktimvo margin contribution outlook to the low-to-mid 30% range from 25%-30% previously. Revuforj new patient starts returned to growth at about 300 new patients, up roughly 20% QoQ, and NPM1 accounted for more than 35% of Revuforj revenue versus more than 30% last quarter. The company ended the quarter with $551 million in cash and disclosed a CFO transition, with Aaron Ondrey succeeding Keith Goldan effective November 9.

TAT reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 20.2% YoY to a record $55.6 million and diluted EPS of $0.58 versus $0.37 a year ago, with gross margin at a record 30.9% and adjusted EBITDA up 60.9% to $10.9 million (19.6% of revenue). APU revenue rose 34.4% and trading/leasing/distribution rose 85.5%, while heat exchangers grew 7.3% and landing gear fell below 4% of revenue. Backlog declined to $577 million from $615 million, but $34 million of that was landing-gear contracts removed due to component shortages, leaving backlog essentially unchanged otherwise. Management gave no numeric guidance but said it expects to finish 2026 strong and carry momentum into 2027, with a 15%-19% tax rate beginning in 2027 as Israeli and US tax losses are exhausted.

Jazz reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.24 billion, up 10% YoY, with oncology up 35% and Xywav up 12% to $483 million. Non-GAAP EPS was $7.15 excluding a $754 million ($11.03/share) Actio acquired IPR&D charge that produced a GAAP-equivalent non-GAAP loss of $3.88. Management raised and narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $4.775-4.85 billion (~13% growth at midpoint), with the new low end above the prior high end, and lifted gross margin guidance 50 bps to 90.5-91.5%. Offsets included a 110 bp gross margin decline YoY and management flagging 2027 competitive headwinds for Zepzelca (IMDELLTRA) and a more measured Modeyso pace.

Neurocrine reported record Q3 net product sales topping $1.1 billion, up more than 40% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS above $3. INGREZZA sales reached $801 million (+17% YoY, including a $20 million order-timing benefit), CRENESSITY $211 million, and VYKAT XR $107 million. Full-year INGREZZA guidance was raised again to $2.9-2.925 billion (from $2.7 billion at the start of the year), but VYKAT XR growth is now expected to be delayed due to external safety-related events. Management flagged mid-to-high single-digit INGREZZA net price concessions for 2027, offset by expected double-digit volume growth.

Realty Income reported Q3 FY2026 AFFO per share of $1.12, up 3.7% YoY, and raised full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to $4.45-$4.46 (a $0.01 midpoint increase) while reaffirming the $10 billion investment volume target. The company invested ~$2.6 billion (~$2.2 billion pro rata) at a 6.8% cash yield with a ~170 bps leverage-neutral spread, and raised occupancy guidance above 98.5% while cutting credit loss expectations from 40 to ~30 bps. Management highlighted Europe (42% of pro rata volume at 7.1% yields) and credit investments (~$250 million) as newer return levers, and noted public equity funded only 19% of YTD volume versus a 47% three-year average. Commentary was constructive but acknowledged the U.S. 10-year reaching 5.35% pressured domestic acquisition economics.

Worldwide revenue grew 14.5% to $55.7M with U.S. revenue up 13.9% to $52.8M on 19.5% U.S. procedure volume growth, partly offset by lower ASP from site-of-care and procedure mix. Adjusted EBITDA rose 32.4% to $3.0M (5.5% margin) and net loss narrowed to $3.6M ($0.08/share) from $4.6M ($0.11). Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $231-233M (implying >20% Q4 growth) with gross margin at 79%, while opex growth guidance was trimmed to 10.5% from 12%. Management cited the Onyx alpha launch tracking ahead of Granite's early launch and new Granite DRGs effective October 1, but deferred 2027 guidance to late February and flagged modest 2027 gross margin pressure from Onyx capacity depreciation.

SBA reported Q3 FY2026 AFFO per share of $3.19 with Tower Cash Flow margins of 80% and Adjusted EBITDA margin of 69%; results were described as in line with expectations. Domestic new lease and amendment billings were about $8 million (international ~$5 million), with Sprint churn of $16 million ($55-56 million for the full year) and EchoStar churn of $14 million ($36 million for the full year). Guidance midpoints for 2026 AFFO and AFFO per share were raised $2 million and $0.08 respectively, but site leasing revenue, Tower Cash Flow and Adjusted EBITDA outlook was roughly unchanged after FX and the Chile/Ecuador divestitures cut about $10 million/$6 million/$4 million. The company repurchased 1.7 million shares for $300 million at an average of $179.68, returned about $430 million total, and declared a $1.25 quarterly dividend up ~13% year over year.

Palantir reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.313 billion, up 96% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, its highest-ever reported growth rates as a public company, with GAAP EPS of $0.44 and adjusted EPS of $0.44. U.S. commercial revenue grew 148% year-over-year to $984 million and surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time, while adjusted operating margin was 62% and adjusted free cash flow was $1.216 billion (53% margin). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $8.530-$8.534 billion (91% growth, a nine-point increase over last quarter's guide), U.S. commercial guidance to at least $3.559 billion, adjusted operating income to $5.245-$5.249 billion, and adjusted free cash flow to $4.8-$5.0 billion. Net dollar retention rose 800 bps sequentially to 165%, though total TCV bookings grew only 6% to $2.918 billion and international commercial grew just 21%.

IDEXX reported Q3 FY2026 organic revenue growth of 10%, with CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue up 11% organically and EPS of $4.01, up 18% as reported and 22% comparable. Operating margin expanded about 60 bps comparable to 33.1% reported, and gross margin rose 110 bps to 62.9%. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $4.741-$4.767 billion (up $32M at midpoint) and EPS to $14.96-$15.16 (up $0.25 at midpoint), while absorbing ~$0.13 of CoVet dilution. U.S. same-store clinical visits declined an estimated 1.8%, but the diagnostics growth premium remained ~1,100 bps, the fourth consecutive quarter above 1,000 bps.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $235M, up 151% YoY and 45% above the midpoint of guidance issued August 3; adjusted EBITDA was $35M, also 45% above the guidance midpoint, with a Rule of 40 score of 166. Both channels accelerated: direct revenue rose 112% to $119M and third-party revenue rose 209% to $116M, the latter marking three sequential quarters of acceleration. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $838-842M (117% growth at the midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA to $134-136M; Q4 guidance implies $220-224M revenue (102% growth at the midpoint) and $30-32M adjusted EBITDA. Contribution margin compressed to 28% (contribution profit +81% to $66M) on a 10-point heavier third-party revenue mix and higher top-of-funnel brand spend that modestly reduced YoY return on ad spend; ARPU declined sequentially to $1,655 on whole-life mix, and no shares were repurchased under the $100M program.

Q3 revenue of $1.72B came in $22M above the guidance midpoint, up 7% sequentially and 11% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin expanding 190 bps sequentially to 41.2% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.90. AI data center revenue grew 39% sequentially to $180M and is now expected to reach ~$620M in 2026 (up 140% YoY), while automotive fell 1% and is guided down high single digits in Q4 due to deliberate supply reallocation. Q4 guidance is $1.715-1.815B (2.5% sequential at midpoint), gross margin 41.5-43.5%, and EPS $0.95-1.07, with management also announcing the $600M Ferric acquisition plus $175M earnouts and raising the 2030 AI data center target by $500M to over $3B.

Kosmos reported Q3 FY2026 with production up 14% year-on-year for the first nine months, absolute operating costs down about 26% (roughly $150 million) and OpEx per barrel down about 37% ($12/bbl). EBITDAX nearly doubled to almost $800 million for the nine months, with roughly $300 million of free cash flow expected for 2026 and net debt down about 17% year-to-date against a 20% target. Jubilee gross production rose about 17% quarter-on-quarter to 84,500 bbl/d, and GTA remains on track for the upper end of 32-36 gross LNG cargo guidance. Management guided Q4 net production lower quarter-on-quarter on Gulf maintenance and Hurricane Isaias downtime plus Jubilee decline, with about $20 million of RBL extension financing costs, while reiterating the year-end 2027 net debt target of around $2 billion.

POSCO Holdings reported Q3 2026 revenue of KRW 19.1 trillion and operating profit of KRW 945 billion (4.9% margin), with OP up 15% QoQ and 48% YoY and rising for a third consecutive quarter. Steel drove the improvement as POSCO's standalone OP reached KRW 455.1 billion (margin 4.6% vs 2.9% in Q2) on a KRW 20,000/ton price increase to KRW 962,000-982,000 and cost savings, while the rechargeable battery materials segment swung to an operating loss of KRW 17 billion on falling lithium prices, Argentine weather disruptions and PPLS feedstock costs. Net debt fell KRW 4.3 trillion QoQ to an 18.4% debt-to-equity ratio, helped by KRW 2.5 trillion in stake sales plus roughly KRW 700 billion from the Woori Financial stake. Guidance is qualitative: a Q4 blast furnace relining is expected to cut crude steel output by about 430,000 tons into Q1 2027, and lithium profitability (Argentina plant 2, PPLS) is pushed toward 2027-2028.

Paymentus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $372.2 million, up 19.8% YoY, with contribution profit of $118.5 million (+20.6%) and adjusted EBITDA of $49.7 million (+38.6%), exceeding the top end of guidance on all three metrics. Adjusted EBITDA margin reached a record 41.9%, up 540 bps, with incremental margin of 68.4%, and non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.25 from $0.17. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue ($1.464-1.469B), contribution profit ($466-468M), and adjusted EBITDA ($186-191M), and set Q4 revenue guidance of $373-378M. The CEO outlined a path to roughly $2 billion in combined revenue and backlog within 18-24 months, flagged a first sizable interchange monetization agreement, and noted BillWallet users doubled to over 200,000.

PSEG reported Q3 2026 net income of $0.76 per share versus $1.24 a year ago, while non-GAAP operating earnings were $1.15 per share versus $1.13, bringing year-to-date operating EPS to $3.56. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 non-GAAP operating earnings guidance of $4.28-$4.40 and the 6%-8% five-year growth outlook through 2030, calling results in line with expectations. Utility margin growth from energy efficiency and transmission was offset by higher depreciation, interest and tax timing, while PSEG Power benefited from the absence of the prior-year Hope Creek refueling outage, higher realized prices and 95.5% nuclear capacity factor. Management flagged a widened PECO-to-Western Hub basis discount (about 30% versus 20% historically) and continued to withhold detail on the upcoming New Jersey base rate filing.

Travere reported Q3 FY2026 total U.S. net product sales of $220.2 million, with FILSPARI net product sales up approximately 120% year-over-year to $200.2 million and THIOLA contributing $20 million; total revenue was $224.6 million including $4.4 million of licensing collaboration revenue. Management did not raise formal numeric guidance and explicitly declined to guide on patient start forms, but reiterated confidence in achieving or exceeding $3 billion in FILSPARI annual sales by 2033. The quarter included roughly $8 million of FILSPARI sales from specialty pharmacy inventory build that management expects to reverse in Q4, and a $113.1 million IPR&D charge tied to the $112.5 million Everest upfront payment. CEO Eric Dube is stepping down in December, with incoming leadership communicated as a transition from a position of strength.

Q3 revenue of $235M rose 52% YoY versus guidance of $223-225M, with gross margin of 88% (up 480 bps), operating income of $77M (33% margin, up ~1,300 bps), and diluted EPS of $0.71. Free cash flow was $120M (51% margin) excluding $7M of acquisition payments, and the company repurchased 296,000 shares for $26M. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $879-881M from $856-860M, with operating income raised to $266-268M; Q4 is guided to $249-251M revenue at 46% growth. Full-year yield expectations rose to 4.6% from 4.45% and LTM eligible lives to ~25.5 million; President Jim Pursley is stepping down at year-end, with Aaryn Pure leading go-to-market and Pursley joining the board.

Q3 revenue was $328.7M, up 12% sequentially and 37% year-over-year, within 0.4% of the guidance midpoint. Gross margin hit 16%, above the high end and up 190 bps sequentially, operating margin rose to 8.6% from 5.5%, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.63 came in well above the high end of guidance. Q4 guidance of $345-365M implies ~8% sequential growth to a 30% full-year 2026, with gross margin stepping to 16.5% and EPS of $0.65-$0.75. Management cut expected second-half growth to 24% from the 'at least 25%' cited a quarter ago, citing supply constraints and about $10M of Q4 revenue pushouts (roughly half from commercial space launch schedules).

Q3 revenue of $142M grew 3% (Pain Treatments +6% to $71M, Surgical Solutions +1% to $51M, international +16% to $18M, Restorative Therapies -3% to $21M), adjusted EBITDA of $28M at 20% margin expanded 70 bps, and adjusted EPS of $0.17 rose 13%.
