LTL was flat at $678 million with a 91.3% adjusted OR, and management described U.S. LTL as broken, with the OR there closer to 97% versus a sub-75% Canadian operation. Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of $1.30-$1.40 was set alongside OR expectations of 400-500 bps truckload improvement, 100-200 bps logistics improvement, and a 0-100 bps LTL deterioration.

The Bancorp reported Q3 2026 core EPS of $1.47, up 25% YoY, with core ROA of 2.42% and core ROE of 34.7%; average loans grew 18.2% YoY and GDV growth was 23% with fintech fee growth of 19%. The company maintained its 2026 core EPS guidance of $5.95-$6.04 but issued a 2027 baseline of $7-$7.20, reduced from prior expectations due to the Chime/Stride Bank acquisition impact, updated pipeline phasing, and rate environment, partly offset by buybacks and a lower tax rate. It initiated 2028 guidance of $8-$8.20. Management also announced a restructuring with an $4.3M charge, 80 position reductions, and $14M annual savings, along with a tax credit strategy lowering the core tax rate to ~24%.

Weyerhaeuser reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP earnings of $61 million, or $0.08 per diluted share, on net sales of $1.9 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of $248 million, up 14% YoY. Wood Products adjusted EBITDA fell $38 million sequentially to $91 million on lower pricing across most products and record-high diesel/transportation costs, including an $18 million OSB loss, while Timberlands EBITDA rose 8% QoQ to $133 million and Strategic Land Solutions fell $43 million to $86 million on real estate timing. Q4 guidance calls for Wood Products EBITDA moderately lower, Timberlands comparable, and SLS down roughly $45 million, with housing expected to remain subdued through year-end as mortgage rates move back over 7%. Management flagged increased Q4 share repurchase, an $146 million / ~81,000-acre Arkansas timberland divestiture, and full-year SLS guidance of ~$450 million; 2026 Monticello capex was lowered to ~$250 million from a $300 million prior estimate.

Sanofi reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of EUR 14.4bn, up 14.3% at constant rates, with business EPS up 19.6% and BOI up 19.7% as gross margin expanded 2.1 points on favorable mix and gross-to-net pricing. Dupixent surpassed EUR 5bn for a second straight quarter at EUR 5.7bn, new launches grew 19.2% to about EUR 2.2bn, and vaccines fell 7%, better than the low-to-mid-teens decline flagged in Q2. Management upgraded 2026 guidance to low-teens sales growth (13-15%) and mid-teens business EPS growth (15-17%), but flagged that 2027 pricing returns to a slightly negative contribution and that Cheplapharm and Medley divestments cut sales by about EUR 1.3bn. The quarter also carried a real negative: amlitelimab and itepekimab were discontinued and the pipeline was described as lagging peers.

ExxonMobil reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP earnings of $15.4 billion and cash flow from operations of $25.7 billion, with global fuels utilization at a record excluding Middle East impacts and diesel yield up 3.5% versus 2019, which management said represented another $1.5 billion of quarterly margins. The company raised the dividend 4% (44th consecutive annual increase) and said it plans to maintain $20 billion of buybacks in 2027, while net debt fell more than $9 billion and net debt to capital remained the strongest in the industry. Middle East disruptions, concentrated in Qatar LNG train damage and deferred UAE sales, are expected to keep the 350 KBD volume impact unchanged in Q4, and management did not host a December corporate plan update, deferring 2027 metrics to a press release and the January call.

Strattec reported Q1 FY2027 sales of $147.2 million, down 3.4% year-over-year from $152.4 million, as lower customer production volumes reduced sales by $6.2 million, partly offset by $1 million in net pricing. GAAP EPS fell to $1.19 from $2.07 and adjusted EPS to $1.85 from $2.22, while gross margin contracted 80 bps to 16.5% and adjusted EBITDA declined to $13.5 million (9.2% of sales) from $15.6 million. Management guided full-year gross margin to 15%-16%, below the 16.5% just reported, citing lower volumes, and expects adjusted SAE of $16.5-$17 million per quarter, with North American production forecast down about 2% for the fiscal year. The company generated $10.8 million in operating cash flow, repurchased roughly 68,000 shares for $5 million, and ended with $111.8 million in cash and no debt.

Q3 FY2026 adjusted sales rose 2.8% with adjusted EBITDA of $67M (13% of net sales, $4.9M above last year) and non-GAAP diluted EPS up 13.2% to $1.54. Vehicle Control grew 6% to $209.5M, Nissens rose 7.6% on Europe's hot summer, Temperature Control fell 4.1% to $138.7M against a record prior-year quarter, and Engineered Solutions grew 4.9%. Full-year guidance was unchanged: low-to-mid-single-digit sales growth and an 11%-12% adjusted EBITDA margin, with tariff pass-through and warehouse ramp costs cited as drags. Leverage reached 1.8x EBITDA, ahead of the 2x target by a quarter, while CFO Nathan Iles departed and former CFO/COO Jim Burke returned as interim CFO.

Standex reported record Q1 FY27 sales of $232.6 million, up 7% total and 12.4% organically, with adjusted EPS of $2.41 (+21.1%), record electronics organic growth of 29.5% and a company book-to-bill of 1.17 on record $273 million order intake. Adjusted gross margin rose 240 bps to 44.4% and adjusted operating margin rose 110 bps to 20.2%, with margin expansion in every segment. Management raised FY27 total sales growth to high single digits from mid-to-high single digits and reiterated high-teens adjusted EPS growth, and announced a new $100 million share repurchase authorization. Offsetting the strength, engraving and hydraulics revenue fell 14.9% on North American auto softness and corporate expense rose about $3 million year-on-year.

Vale reported Q3 2026 proforma EBITDA of $3.5 billion, down 20% year-on-year, as realized iron ore prices fell 10% and C1 cash cost rose 12% YoY to $23.1/t, with all-in cost up 21% to $60.4/t. Iron ore production fell 6% YoY on Serra Norte depletion, cave-related restrictions and fleet ramp-up issues, though sales held at 86.3 Mt; management now guides to the low end of iron ore production guidance for the year. Vale Base Metals grew EBITDA more than 60% YoY to $1.1 billion, and management is confident on the upper half of copper and nickel production guidance, with 2026 cost guidance reiterated. Free cash flow was $2.2 billion after $1.25 billion of capex, and expanded net debt fell about $200 million to $16.4 billion even after $1.7 billion of dividend and interest-on-capital payments.

Silvercrest reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $32.7 million, up $1.4 million YoY, with GAAP net income of $1.2 million ($0.08 per Class A share) and adjusted EPS of $0.16. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.4 million, or 13.5% of revenue, while the compensation ratio stayed elevated at 66.3% for the nine-month period amid the firm's investment program. Discretionary AUM fell $939.2 million to $23.8 billion on weaker markets ($753 million revenue effect), though net flows were roughly flat at $58.3 million and organic new client accounts of $182.2 million were the best quarter of 2026. No formal guidance was issued; management said the compensation ratio should stay elevated as investments mature and pointed to 2027 for revenue contribution, with a dividend of $0.21 per share declared.

Q1 FY2027 net sales fell 5.7% YoY to $127.9M, but gross profit jumped to $12.5M from $3.4M and gross margin expanded to 9.8% from 2.5%. The net loss narrowed more than $9M to $2M and adjusted EBITDA was $6.1M, an $8.6M YoY improvement, with $2.5M of free cash flow. Brazil sales rose 14.4% while Americas sales fell $8.2M and Asia fell $3.7M on pricing pressure. Full-year fiscal 2027 outlook is unchanged, with sales and profitability expected to improve YoY and H2 better than H1; the $55.5M term loan was repaid from a real estate sale.

Oxford Square reported Q3 2026 net investment income of ~$4.9M, or $0.04/share, down from $5.1M, or $0.05/share, in the prior quarter, while total investment income rose to ~$9.9M from ~$9.4M. NAV per share fell to $1.21 from $1.29, and combined net unrealized and realized losses widened to ~$3.3M ($0.03/share) from ~$1.1M ($0.01/share). The board declared monthly distributions of $0.015 for January, February, and March 2027, a step down referenced on the call as in line with current and prospective near-term earnings power, alongside a stated intent to moderately delever (debt-to-equity fell from 1.26x at Q1 to 1.07x at Q3, and lower intra-quarter).

Cavco reported Q2 FY2027 net revenue of $656.4 million, up 18% YoY from $556.5 million, with record shipments of 5,972 homes and diluted EPS of $7.17 versus $6.55. Factory-built gross margin was 21.1%, down from 22.9% a year ago on higher input costs but up roughly 30-40 bps sequentially as pricing offset materials inflation. Backlog rose 63% YoY with 8-10 week coverage, aided by newly disclosed data-center workforce housing orders, though management declined to quantify that pipeline or give margin guidance. Buybacks totaled $30 million with $272 million unrestricted cash; no formal guidance was provided beyond commentary that material inflation remains a risk to margins.

RBC reported Q2 FY2027 net sales up 15.2% YoY to $524.6M, adjusted EPS up 29.9% to $3.74, and adjusted EBITDA up 20.4% to $175M (33.4% of sales). Gross margin expanded to 45.6% from 44.1% reported / 44.9% adjusted, with A&D segment margin up to 42.2% from 38.7%. Q3 guidance is $520-525M (12.7%-13.7% growth), with nine-month sales of $1.564-1.569B (15.6%-16%), and management reiterated full-year gross margin expansion of ~100 bps. The quarter was led by Aerospace & Defense (+15.8%) and Industrial (+14.8%), though marine production remains behind plan and is expected to catch up in Q4.

Q3 results far exceeded the high end of outlook for a third consecutive quarter: same-property hotel EBITDA rose 15.1% to $115.2M ($10.7M above the high end), adjusted EBITDA was $107.9M ($11.4M above the high end), and adjusted FFO per share was $0.63 ($0.11 above the top end), with same-property RevPAR up 8.3% on 7% ADR growth and hotel EBITDA margins expanding 205 bps to 28.8%. Full-year guidance was raised by more than the Q3 beat: same-property RevPAR growth to 7.6%-8% (midpoint up 280 bps), same-property hotel EBITDA growth of 12.9%-14.1% (midpoint up 420 bps), and adjusted FFO to $1.88-$1.92 per share (midpoint up $0.17). Q4 guidance calls for same-property RevPAR growth of 4%-6% and adjusted FFO per share of $0.26-$0.30. Management flagged Q1 2027 revenue pace as currently negative on convention timing and Super Bowl shifts, but up 8% or more in each of Q2-Q4 2027.

Piper Sandler reported Q3 2026 adjusted net revenues of $456 million (up modestly YoY), a 19.8% operating margin, and adjusted EPS of $0.87; advisory revenues rose 18% YoY to $250 million, while corporate financing fell YoY (though up 50% sequentially) and municipal financing dropped 36% YoY on higher rates. Management guided Q4 advisory to be the strongest quarter of the year but below the prior-year record fourth quarter, expected corporate financing to slow, and flagged a full-year non-compensation expense ratio above last year. The quarter was mixed: record corporate IB/advisory and strong fixed income were offset by sharp public finance weakness and a softer financing and brokerage outlook into year-end.

Capri reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $809 million, down 5.5% reported (4.9% constant currency), but operating income rose 55% to $31 million (3.8% margin, up 150 bps) and EPS came in at $0.42 versus a $0.03 loss last year, with results above management's expectations on revenue, operating income and EPS. Michael Kors revenue fell 8.6% to $663 million, weighed by ~$50 million of inventory delays, a ~40% cut in markdown inventory and ~50% fewer promotional days, while Jimmy Choo grew 11.5% to $146 million and expanded operating margin 830 bps to 1.4%. Guidance was raised: FY2027 revenue now ~$3.42 billion, operating income ~$175 million (+50%) and EPS $2.20 (+45%), with weighted shares cut to ~108 million on $300 million of planned buybacks; Q3 revenue guided to just over $1 billion and EPS $0.95. Gross margin expanded 230 bps to 63.3%, and net debt fell to $336 million from $1.6 billion last year after $150 million of repurchases (10.3 million shares, a ~9% share count reduction).

Q3 total sales grew 7.5% year-over-year with 5.1% core growth, led by Water Quality at 6.4% and PQI at 3.2%; adjusted EPS rose 19.2% and free cash flow was $304 million. Both segments accelerated core growth sequentially, and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.49-$4.52 (15%-16% growth), with Q4 core growth guided to 5.5%-6.5% and total sales growth of ~10%-11%. Q4 margins are modeled roughly flat to up ~30 bps year-over-year, with Cost Optimization Program savings and Cleanwater1 dilution offsetting, and 2027 detail deferred to the February guide.

Baxter reported Q3 FY2026 sales of approximately $3.0 billion, up 5% on both a reported and organic basis, with every division contributing; adjusted EPS was $0.58, down 16% YoY due to prior-year discrete tax benefits. Full-year organic growth guidance was raised to 3%-4% from 2%-3%, and adjusted EPS guidance narrowed and raised at the low end to $2.05-$2.15 from $1.95-$2.15. Free cash flow was strong at $448 million, bringing YTD to $705 million, and management reiterated confidence in reaching ~3x net leverage by year-end. Offsets include a 110 bps gross margin decline to 38.3%, a 40 bps operating margin decline to 14.5%, and the decision to discontinue cephalosporin production at Round Lake (~$50 million sales, $30 million operating income in 2026) tied to FDA warning letter remediation.

BBVA reported Q3 2026 net attributable profit of just over EUR 3 billion, up 19.1% YoY, with EPS up 23.9% and nine-month profit of EUR 9.66 billion (+13.6% YoY). NII grew 16.5% YoY and 5.7% QoQ in constant terms, gross income rose 15.7% YoY, and ROTE reached 22% with an efficiency ratio of 37.9%. Management raised group ROTE guidance to above 21% (from above 20% previously) and said it has full confidence in beating 2025-2028 plan targets, while reiterating regional guidance with Mexico lending likely to beat its ~10% target and Turkey/South America cost of risk running slightly above guidance. CET1 fell 20 bps QoQ to 12.21% on RWA growth (-44 bps) and market impacts, partly offset by 71 bps of earnings; a record EUR 0.37 interim dividend was paid and the second EUR 1 billion buyback tranche is underway.

Brunswick reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.5 billion, up 7% YoY, with adjusted operating earnings up 38%, adjusted operating margin of 10.1% (up 230 bps), and adjusted EPS of $1.58, up 63% and significantly ahead of expectations; all segments grew sales and expanded margins. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to approximately $4.65 from $4.55, the third raise this year (initial $4.10), while revenue guidance of $5.7-$5.8 billion and ~8% adjusted operating margin were maintained. The $0.10 EPS increase reflects roughly half of the Q3 beat passed through, with the remainder offset by unanticipated material inflation (aluminum, copper, memory) and channel stocking caution heading into Q4. Management also disclosed a CEO transition, with Navico President Áine Denari succeeding David Foulkes on January 1.

Bandwidth reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of $234 million, up 22% YoY, with cloud communications revenue of $158 million (+12%) and record adjusted EBITDA of $35 million (+43%, 22% margin). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.50 and free cash flow was $33 million (up over 150% YoY). Full-year 2026 guidance was narrowed and the midpoint raised: total revenue $905-910 million (~20% growth), cloud communications $624-626 million (~11%), adjusted EBITDA $124-125 million, and non-GAAP EPS $1.73-1.79, with commercial cloud revenue raised $4 million while political campaign revenue was trimmed $3 million to $10 million. Management expressed growing confidence in double-digit cloud communications growth for 2027, citing 11 deals over $1 million ACV (~$19 million) signed year to date and a Salesforce international BYOC expansion.

Textron reported Q3 FY2026 revenues of $3.8 billion (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.76 (up from $1.55), driven by strong performance in Textron Aviation ($1.7B revenue, +14%) and Textron Systems (+16%). Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EPS to $6.55-$6.65 and manufacturing cash flow to $800M-$900M, citing lower CapEx and strong Q3 order activity at Aviation. The Industrial segment separation remains on track with a 12-18 month timeline.

AXT reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $73.4 million, up 54% sequentially from $47.6 million and 162% from $28.0 million a year ago, with non-GAAP gross margin of 56.1% versus 45.0% in Q2 and 22.4% in Q3 FY2025. Non-GAAP net income was $26.8 million, or $0.41 per diluted share, and Q4 guidance calls for roughly $90 million of recognizable revenue with non-GAAP EPS of $0.57-$0.59. Backlog surpassed $500 million from more than $100 million a quarter ago, and management said indium phosphide revenue opportunity more than quadrupled in 2026 with capacity targeted to roughly double again in 2027.

Net sales rose 2% YoY to $1.311B with volume growth in three of four end markets, but adjusted EBITDA fell 4% to $282M (21.5% margin) and adjusted EPS declined 6% YoY to $0.63, both below internal expectations on softer Europe Refinish volumes. Management cut full-year guidance: Q4 sales now seen roughly flat vs prior +3%, full-year adjusted EBITDA to $1.10-1.11B and EPS to ~$2.45, with Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $254-264M and EPS ~$0.55, citing macro caution and accelerated MSO conversion investment (~$8M in Q4). Europe Refinish volumes fell double-digit YoY and total Refinish volumes were down mid-single digits, partly offset by Commercial Vehicle net sales up 24% to a record $119M and Mobility EBITDA margin expanding 100 bps to 19%. Free cash flow rose 3% to $92M and net leverage hit a record-low 2.1x ahead of the expected early-2027 AkzoNobel close.

Tyler Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 results with 11% recurring revenue growth and SaaS revenue growth of 21.2%. Operating margins expanded by 150 basis points to record quarterly free cash flow of $277 million. Management noted that full-year SaaS guidance was lowered slightly due to timing shifts in large deals, though the total sales number remains consistent with prior expectations.

Attruby U.S. net product revenue was $253.2M, up ~134% YoY and ~14% QoQ, driving total Q3 revenue of $353.2M versus $120.7M a year ago, which included a $75M one-time Bayer milestone for Beyonttra. The operating loss narrowed to $11.6M from $145.2M, though the company flagged that the strong operating line benefited from launch-expense timing and that OpEx will catch up in Q4. Management reaffirmed its $4B Attruby peak sales assumption and cited three prioritized launches in the next seven months (BBP-418 Nov 27, 2026; infigratinib Feb 4, 2027; encaleret May 8, 2027), while noting EU filing for BBP-418 shifted to 1H 2028 pending 36-month data.

BCB reported a quarter dominated by a balance-sheet restructuring: a successful capital raise, a sale of over $200 million of mostly criticized/classified loans plus a ~$100 million fair-value write-down, and a $60 million deferred tax asset valuation allowance taken against the DTA. Net interest margin came in at 3.03%, above the previously previewed 2.90-3.00% range despite roughly $1 million of interest accrual reversals, with deposit costs trending lower. Classified loans fell from $207 million to $153 million (Jawad cited a 70% reduction in one measure) and reserve coverage rose, while NPLs sit at $22 million against a $70 million ACL (over 3% of loans). Management guided to a full cannabis loan/deposit sale in Q4 (~$70-80 million deposits, ~$70 million loans) and expects $2.5-3 million of elevated transaction expenses to largely fall away, with no formal 2027 expense guidance and DTA recapture only around end-2027.

Adjusted EPS of $2.00 beat prior-year $1.89 and nine-month EPS came in at $4.63 versus $4.40, with management calling results in line with expectations. Full-year 2026 EPS guidance was narrowed to $6.07-$6.12, with management now pointing to the top half of the original range, and standalone 2027 guidance was initiated at $6.53-$6.63 (about 8% growth). The 7%-9% long-term EPS and dividend growth targets were reaffirmed, and the Essential Utilities merger remains on track to close by end of Q1 2027 with settlements reached in Pennsylvania, Texas and North Carolina. Capital plan was raised to more than $20 billion through 2030, and California desalination cost estimate was updated to $825 million plus AFUDC.

PHINIA reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $912 million (up 0.4% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $135 million (margin 14.8%). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $3.625-$3.675 billion and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $500-$520 million, citing organic strength in commercial vehicles and the stoba acquisition. The company returned $76 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends.

Reported sales rose 5% to $2.3 billion with organic growth of 4%, and adjusted EPS of $2.42 came in above expectations, up 2% year-over-year. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to $10.10-$10.24 with the midpoint slightly raised, but the company still frames underlying performance as better than reported, with destocking a ~2-point sales and ~$0.15 EPS headwind in Q3. Materials organic sales grew 5% with segment EBITDA margin down ~1 point to 16.4%, while Solutions organic sales grew 1% and margins expanded 80 bps to 17.8%. Intelligent Labels grew only low single digits as logistics declined double digits, and the large retailer fresh rollout slipped into a 2027 ramp.

Atomera reported zero revenue in Q3 FY2026 versus $11,000 a year ago and $158,000 in Q2, with no wafer shipments for revenue falling in the quarter. GAAP net loss was $6.0 million ($0.15/share) versus $5.6 million ($0.17/share) a year ago, and non-GAAP net loss widened to $4.6 million from $4.4 million. Non-GAAP OpEx guidance for 2026 was reaffirmed at the high end of ~$18.5 million ±$250,000, with Q4 revenue from wafer deliveries guided to approximately $50,000 and a ~$1.4 million one-time 200-mm tool lease prepayment flagged. Operationally management reported reaching three of four Gate-All-Around customers, extending memory work into DRAM 4F-squared and NAND, and a GaN-on-silicon JDA with IQE.

Q3 revenue rose 2.2% (price +$78M, surcharges +$23M, M&A +$77M, volume -$69M), net income +3.3% to $558M, adjusted EBITDA roughly flat at $1.1B, and EPS +4.1% to $1.02. Building Materials revenue rose 1.8% to $2.8B with 30 bps margin expansion and EBITDA +2.7% to $938M, while Building Envelope revenue grew 3.6% to $929M but EBITDA fell 14.6% on raw material and freight inflation. Guidance was cut, with FY2026 revenue now $12.2B-$12.4B and EBITDA $2.95B-$3.05B, and the company pushed expected price-over-cost positivity in Building Envelope out to 2027. Management cited a $36M prior-year Q4 insurance benefit that will not repeat and expected Q4 shingle de-stocking as pressures.

AMERISAFE reported Q3 2026 net income of $7.2M ($0.39/diluted share) and operating net income of $7.4M ($0.40/share), down sharply from $13.8M ($0.72) and $10.6M ($0.55) in Q3 2025. Net premiums earned rose 3% to $73.3M, but gross written premiums fell 4.5% to $76.7M on unfavorable audit adjustments (-$1.6M vs a +$2.5M prior-year swing), and the expense ratio widened to 32.5% from 31.1%. Management reiterated its mid-single-digit growth target for the year but flagged intensifying competition, 'irrational' pricing/commission structures, and loss cost declines of 5-6% heading into 2027; no formal numeric EPS or premium guidance was provided.

Silicom reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $26.7 million, a 71% year-over-year increase that beat the $25M-$26M guidance range. The company returned to non-GAAP profitability with positive operating income of $20,000 and EPS of 4 cents, significantly improving on the prior quarter's loss. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $96M-$98M (57% YoY growth) and provided Q4 guidance of $27M-$28M.

Ryerson reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $2.2 billion (up 8.6% sequentially) and diluted EPS of $0.61, exceeding guidance across the board despite a one-time $4 million inventory purchase accounting adjustment that compressed gross margin to 17.2%. Management raised fourth-quarter revenue guidance to $1.96-$2.04 billion and adjusted EBITDA (ex-LIFO) to $100-$104 million, citing strong start-of-quarter momentum in data center and commercial transportation sectors. The company surpassed its first-year synergy target of $40 million with $13 million realized in Q3, bringing the annualized run rate above $60 million.

Amazon reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $201.9B, up 12% YoY (13% ex-FX), with operating income of $28.1B, up 61%, and a record 13.9% operating margin. AWS grew 39.3% YoY to $46B (a $184B run rate) with a 38.7% operating margin, marking a sixth consecutive quarter of acceleration and a $578B backlog. Q4 guidance was set at $240-247B net sales and $28.5-33.5B operating income; management stated AWS could grow north of 40% in each of 2027 and 2028 and reach $1T in revenue in 5-10 years, with 2026 capex of ~$220B and meaningfully more in 2027. Segment growth was dampened by the Prime Day shift into Q2 (roughly 400 bps of retail headwind and 850 bps on ad growth), and Leo cost capitalization slipped, keeping expenses in Q4.

Shell reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted earnings of $10.8 billion and cash flow from operations of $21 billion, driven by strong operational performance and trading capabilities in a volatile environment. The company completed the ARC Resources acquisition and announced FID on LNG Canada phase II, while reducing net debt by $6 billion to 17% gearing. Management maintained its distribution policy of 40%-50% of CFFO through the cycle, announcing a $5 billion share buyback program.

Q3 sales were $941 million, essentially flat YoY, with EPS of $0.93; North America grew 3% (1% organic) but segment margin fell 60 bps to 23.6% as double-digit steel and freight cost increases cut earnings by $18 million, partly offset by $16 million of IEEPA tariff refunds and cost savings. Rest of World sales fell 7% to $193 million, with China local-currency sales down 17% and segment margin at 5.4%. Full-year guidance was reset to exclude China, with sales up approximately 4% and adjusted EPS of $3.42-$3.52, and management said the ex-China outlook sits within the ranges implied by July guidance; boiler growth guidance was raised to 10%-12% from 6%-8%, while water treatment was cut to 3%-4% from 5%-6% and Leonard Valve to about $65 million from about $70 million. The company announced a definitive agreement to watch 81% of its China business to CPE at an approximately $400 million enterprise value, retaining a 19% stake and a brand licensing agreement, with after-tax proceeds prioritized for buybacks.

Sonic Automotive reported record quarterly total revenues of $4 billion and gross profit of $617.5 million for Q3 FY2026, with GAAP EPS of $1.28 and adjusted EPS of $1.30. Franchised dealership revenues decreased 3% year-over-year due to EV pull-forward effects in the prior period, while EchoPark revenues surged 14% and Powersports revenues hit an all-time record high of $113.7 million. Management maintained full-year guidance ranges for SG&A as a percentage of gross profit despite higher-than-expected costs from AI investments and travel.

APi reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $2.55 billion, up 22.5% YoY with 15.7% organic growth, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50, up 22%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 24.6% to a 13.7% margin, up 20 bps, though adjusted gross margin fell 120 bps to 30.3% on project/business mix and rising material and fuel costs. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $9.20-9.25 billion from $8.875-9.025 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $1.235-1.255 billion from $1.205-1.245 billion, the third raise this year; 2027 guidance is deferred to February. Backlog exceeded $5 billion for the first time, and M&A closed 13 transactions YTD toward a $250 million bolt-on target.

Third quarter revenue increased 17% to a record $982 million, supported by 8.9% tonnage growth and a 5.8% increase in revenue per shipment excluding fuel surcharge. Operating income rose 17.5% to $122.3 million with an operating ratio of 87.6%, which remained consistent with the prior year adjusted result despite seasonal headwinds. The company authorized a new share repurchase program of up to $250 million and appointed Todd Fowler as an independent director.

Antero reported record production of 4.2 Bcfe/d, up 23% year-over-year, with total cash costs down 16% to a company-record low and the unhedged EBITDAX margin up 27% ($0.27/Mcfe) even as natural gas prices fell 4%. Free cash flow per share rose 139% year-over-year, and the company repurchased 1.6 million shares in the quarter, bringing the five-quarter total to about 15.5 million. Guidance calls for Q4 volumes of roughly 4.3 Bcfe/d with 15-20 Bcf of curtailments, cash costs of $2.10-$2.20/Mcfe, and low-single-digit organic growth from a steady three-rig, two-crew program in 2027. Management expects the $300 million margin-enhancement target to be reached, with a path to roughly doubling it beyond 2028, while fourth-quarter C3+ NGL prices are running about 50% above third-quarter levels.

Management fees rose 10% YoY to nearly $1.1 billion, FRE came in at $524 million with a 42.5% margin versus 41.4% a year ago, and after-tax realized income per share was $1.26 ($3.79 YTD, up 15%). AUM reached $691 billion (+16% YoY) and fee-paying AUM $416 billion (+13%), with $31 billion+ gross fundraising and $35 billion deployed in the quarter. Full-year FRE growth is guided within the 16%-20% target and FRE margin expansion slightly above the midpoint of the 0-150 bp range, but full-year net realized performance income guidance was trimmed to $300-325 million due to European waterfall payment delays. The dividend was raised over 20% YoY to $1.35 per share.

Q3 revenue was $564M, up 36% YoY (29% organic), and adjusted EBITDA was $256M, up 67%, with margin expanding 840 bps to 45.4%. Free cash flow rose 117% to $150M and net leverage fell to 1.6x. ARXS raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.05-2.07B (up $90M at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA to $855-865M (up $65M at midpoint, ~41.7% margin), and introduced FY2027 revenue of $2.4-2.5B (10-15% organic) and adjusted EBITDA of $1.01-1.06B (42.1-42.4% margin). Management described the outsized growth as 'ramp capture' from simultaneous platform ramps, expecting it to moderate toward a more normalized 10-15% organic rate in 2027.

Algoma reported Q3 FY2026 shipments of ~144,500 tons (in line with its October 1 guidance of ~145,000 tons) and revenue of $249.4M, down from $523.9M a year earlier as the EAF-only transition and a Lake Superior Power turbine outage cut volumes. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $13.9M (negative 5.6% margin), within guidance, but underlying EBITDA improved ~$19M sequentially to roughly -$67M excluding the capacity utilization adjustment. Average realization rose 11% sequentially to $1,510/ton and direct tariff costs fell to $18.1M from $89.7M. Q4 shipments are guided 25%-35% higher sequentially with substantially improved underlying EBITDA, and management targets ~1.2M tons for 2027 with an exit rate of 1.5-1.6M tons.

Q3 revenue was $40.0M, up 10% YoY, with organic growth of 9% (vs 4% a year ago) and organic recurring revenue growth of 14%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to $10.5M at a 26% margin (up ~400 bps), non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 75% from 70%, and net loss narrowed to $0.6M from $5.4M. Management introduced preliminary 2027 guidance of $183-187M revenue and 26-28% adjusted EBITDA margin, incorporating an October acquisition (~$10M run-rate) for $26.5M, and set Q4 2026 revenue at $42-44M and adjusted EBITDA at $10-12M. Q4 EBITDA guidance midpoint implies only ~10% revenue growth with integration and sales ramp costs weighing on the quarter.

ASE reported record Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of TWD 244.2 billion, up 28% QoQ and 45% YoY, with operating margin expanding 2.5 pts QoQ and 5.8 pts YoY to 13.6% and net income of TWD 27 billion (up 148% YoY). ATM revenue hit a record TWD 151.5 billion (+20% QoQ, +51% YoY) with gross margin of 30.6%, up 8 pts YoY and above the historical structural ceiling; diluted EPS was TWD 5.84. Q4 guidance calls for consolidated revenue +6-8% QoQ, gross margin 23-24%, ATM revenue +11-13% QoQ, and 2026 LEAP revenue was raised to over $4 billion from $3.7 billion previously, with CapEx lifted to $11.5 billion from $10.5 billion. Full-process revenue was guided to over $1 billion in 2027 versus $300 million in 2026, and CPO revenue of over $0.5 billion is expected next year.

Titan reported Q3 revenue of $454 million and adjusted EBITDA of $28 million, both consistent with guidance despite a cyclical downturn in end markets. Management highlighted the sale of the ITM Undercarriage business to reduce debt and focus on core wheel and tire growth, while noting that agricultural segment sales declined 12% due to elevated costs and sluggish activity in Brazil. Full-year 2026 guidance was revised to revenue of $1.85 billion-$1.87 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $91 million-$101 million inclusive of ITM.

Twilio reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.56 billion (up 20% reported, 16% organic) and record non-GAAP income from operations of $326 million. Management raised full-year 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 15% and full-year 2026 non-GAAP income from operations to $1.19-$1.2 billion. The company also provided a preliminary outlook for FY2027, projecting at least 10% organic revenue growth and non-GAAP income from operations of at least $1.35 billion.

Q3 FY2026 sales were $220.5 million, up 23.2% YoY, with gross margin of 40.9% (up 120 bps) and adjusted EBITDA of $52.5 million (23.8% margin, up from 21.9%). ITDS revenue rose 37.8% to $113.9 million on data solutions up ~61%, while ADRS grew 10.7% to $106.6 million with segment gross margin down to 39.6% on mix and FX. Q4 guidance is $220-240 million in sales with 40-42% gross margin, bucking normal Q4 seasonality on record all-time-high bookings that exceeded quarterly sales. The quarter showed broad growth with margin expansion, tempered by raw material, FX, and logistics cost inflation and elevated inventory to support demand.

ATEC reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $221 million (up 13% YoY), with surgical revenue of $202 million (up 14%) and surgical hardware up 17%, but revenue fell short of the company's expectations, driven by a $1 million YoY decline in biologics and softer thoracolumbar procedure volumes. Gross margin expanded nearly 200 bps to 72% and adjusted EBITDA reached $38 million (17% margin, up over 400 bps), while free cash flow was approximately $6 million. Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $862 million (from a prior implied level) and reduced adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow expectations, citing lower biologics attachment, lower overall procedure volumes, and a temporary international supply constraint.

ATI reported Q3 revenue of $1.4B, up 26% YoY and 13% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $328M (up 46% YoY) beating the high end of guidance by $13M. Adjusted EPS rose 72% to $1.46, adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 300 bps to 23%, and AA&S posted a record 25.8% margin (up 850 bps YoY). Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by $35M to $1.19-1.20B (midpoint $1.195B, 39% growth) and guided Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $345-355M and EPS of $1.51-1.57. HPMC margin was pressured ~200 bps by a new alloy ramp, expected to be fully behind by year-end.

Belden reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $966 million, up 38% YoY with 11% organic growth, and adjusted EPS of $2.26, up 15%, both within guidance ranges ($950-970M and $2.15-2.30) and including RUCKUS from July 1. Adjusted gross margin expanded 330 bps to 41.5% and adjusted EBITDA rose 44% to $171 million (17.7% margin). Orders exceeded $1 billion for the first time, up 46% YoY and 16% organically, with book-to-bill of 1.05x. Q4 guidance of $960-980M revenue and $2.20-2.35 adjusted EPS implies 6-13% EPS growth, below the 15% delivered this quarter, reflecting RUCKUS component shortages that cut about $10-15 million of revenue; management called the supply issue transitory and expects phased improvement into 2027.

Total Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 7% YoY to approximately $13.1B, with the growth portfolio up 12% to $7.7B and legacy portfolio up 1% on ELIQUIS strength (+26% to ~$4.7B). Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.35, including a $0.58 per-share hit from acquired IPR&D and licensing; excluding that charge the full-year EPS guidance midpoint would have risen ~$0.15. Full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance is now $6.35-$6.55 on raised revenue guidance, with legacy portfolio decline narrowed to 3%-5% and ELIQUIS growth held at 20%-25%. OPDIVO fell 6% to ~$2.4B on QVANTIG conversion, while QVANTIG reached $334M (+28% QoQ) and BREYANZI grew 48%.

UFP Industries reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.73 billion, an 11% year-over-year increase driven by volume growth and pricing, though Adjusted EBITDA declined to $119 million due to elevated transportation costs and losses from new operations. Management maintained its full-year guidance unchanged despite macro headwinds in residential construction and soft demand in certain segments. The company highlighted strong performance in Deckorators and Packaging but noted continued challenges with freight rates and material costs.

Colony Bankcorp reported Q3 FY2026 operating net income of $11.6 million and operating pre-provision net revenue of ~$16.3 million, with net interest margin up 7 bps to 3.59% and operating non-interest income up $702K to $12.3 million. Operating non-interest expense rose $950K and the operating NIE/avg assets ratio ticked up to 1.53% from 1.51%. Management guided Q4 and FY2027 loan growth to ~5%, well below its 8%-12% long-term target, and said ROA (~1.25%+ this quarter) will pull back 10-15 bps post-First Reliance close before reaching a 1.35% target in 2027. A sale-leaseback (~$15M gain, offset by ~$100M securities sale at ~2% yield) and the pending November 1 First Reliance legal close were the main strategic items.

Consolidated sales of $2.8 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.41 missed expectations due to fire truck production challenges in the vocational segment. Management revised full-year guidance for adjusted EPS to a range of $8.50-$9.50, citing potential timing delays on the next NGDV order. While access equipment demand remains strong with a $2.7 billion backlog, the company is resetting near-term expectations for fire truck throughput and margin recovery.

Q3 2026 diluted EPS was $0.91, flat versus Q2 2026 and bringing record nine-month EPS to $2.69, up 31.2% versus adjusted $2.05 for the prior-year period. Fully tax-equivalent NIM held at 3.89% (core, ex-accretion, rose to 3.75%), originated loans grew $76 million (4.7% annualized), and total deposits fell $32.6 million only because of a $76.1 million exit of higher-cost corporate deposits at 3.69%. No formal guidance was issued; management expects a stable margin into Q4 and 2027, an interest-bearing deposit beta around 40%, and a modest Q4 expense uptick from incentive comp plus technology investment in 2027. Prior-year comparatives were recast under ASU 2025-08 with no impact on 2026 results or full-year 2025.

CareDx reported Q3 2026 revenue of $139M, up 39% YoY and 6% sequentially, with testing services revenue of $119M (+65%) including $15M of out-of-period revenue versus a prior $8M estimate. Non-GAAP gross margin rose to 74% from 71%, adjusted EBITDA doubled to $30M (22% of revenue), and the company generated $13M in operating cash flow with $250M cash and no debt. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $30M to $520M-$530M (38% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA guidance by $23M to $90M-$100M. Transplant testing volume grew 21% YoY, Specialty Oncology grew 37% YoY on a comparable basis, and AlloHeme remains on track for a Q1 2027 launch with coverage anticipated in 2028.

Cullen/Frost earned $178.5 million in Q3 2026, up 3.4% year-over-year, with EPS of $2.84, up 6.4% from $2.67. Average loans grew 9% to $23.4 billion and average deposits rose 3.6% to $43.6 billion, while the net interest margin expanded 3 bps sequentially to 3.78%. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised on net interest income (5%-5.5% from 4.75%-5.25%), loan growth (8%-8.5% from 7%-8%) and non-interest income (8.5%-9% from 7.5%-8.5%), while NIM, deposit and net charge-off guidance were unchanged and expense growth moved to the upper end of the 4.5%-5% range. Non-performing assets fell to $67 million from $114 million last quarter on the payoff of a large multifamily CRE loan, and net charge-offs were 14 bps of average loans.

Churchill Downs reported record Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $696 million and record Adjusted EBITDA of $264 million, with Kentucky HRM Adjusted EBITDA up 10% and gaming segment Adjusted EBITDA up 4%. Virginia Adjusted EBITDA fell $6 million ex-insurance, hit by Petersburg casino competition and a roughly $5 million new live-racing-day tax, though The Rose in Northern Virginia grew sequentially. Free cash flow through nine months was $603 million ($8.59/share); the board authorized a new $750 million buyback and a 7% dividend increase, with bank leverage of 3.8x expected to fall below 3.0x after the nine-property regional gaming sale, which management expects to sign by year-end. No formal revenue or EBITDA guidance was given; Derby 153 ticket sales are up about 25% YoY with roughly 40% of inventory sold.

Q3 revenue of $132.1M rose 6% sequentially but fell 2% year-over-year; EPS ex-items of $0.16 improved from $0.11 in Q2 but dropped from $0.22 a year ago. EBIT ex-items of $12.6M lifted margin 200 bps sequentially to about 10%, helped by Reservoir Description margins of 10% (up from 5%) and product sales up 19% QoQ, partly offset by Production Enhancement margins sliding to 9% from 12%. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $128.5M-$134.5M (roughly flat sequentially) and EPS of $0.12-$0.20, with management citing continued Middle East disruptions and project delays and withholding a specific 2027 outlook while saying client conversations point to a global capex increase.

O'Reilly reported Q3 FY2026 comparable store sales growth of 7.2% and diluted EPS growth of 14%, significantly surpassing expectations. Management raised full-year comparable store sales guidance from a range of 4%-6% to 5.5%-6.5% and updated full-year EPS guidance to $3.25-$3.35, reflecting strong execution despite some margin pressures in petroleum categories offset by tariff refunds. The company also announced an acceleration in new store growth with a 2027 target of 265-275 net new stores.

Omnicell reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $308 million and non-GAAP EBITDA of $45 million, both exceeding the high end of previously shared guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP EBITDA and EPS guidance while narrowing total revenue and product/service revenue ranges due to increased visibility. The company highlighted strong operational execution, favorable customer mix, and cost efficiency driving outperformance.

Climb reported record Q3 FY2026 results: gross billings up 40% to $706.4M, net sales up 37% to $220.3M, gross profit up 28% to $33M, net income up 69% to $7.9M ($0.43/diluted share), and adjusted EBITDA up 35% to $14.7M (44.6% effective margin, +230 bps). Management did not issue quantitative guidance but said Q4 is tracking on the same trajectory and reiterated expectations for another record year. The main change versus prior periods was broader-based organic growth (19 of top 20 vendors grew) and the post-quarter NeoVAD acquisition expanding European presence; SG&A as a percentage of gross profit improved to 63.2% from 68.5% in Q2.

The call was Q&A-only, with results deferred to the separately posted earnings release and prepared remarks, so no revenue, EPS, margin or cash flow figures were stated in the transcript. Management said it expects to stay in maintenance production mode into 2027, supported by hedges, and is not giving forward guidance. The Q3 in-basin differential came in wider than expected with two-thirds of the portfolio exposed in-basin, though curtailments totaled less than 1 Bcf for the quarter. Cost inflation from diesel and steel affects less than 1% of capital, and share repurchases remain the capital-allocation benchmark against which M&A is tested.

Coinbase delivered flat quarter-over-quarter revenue as total crypto spot trading volume fell 10% QoQ, offset by Prediction Markets crossing a $200M annualized run-rate; predictions plus derivatives reached roughly 25% of transaction revenue and subscription services were about 49% of total net revenue. Management did not provide explicit forward guidance figures, instead framing the quarter as a mix-shift story where diversification cushioned a spot decline. The most-cited forward driver is the agentic and 'everything exchange' build-out, with agentic trading volume growing roughly 20% week-over-week off a small base, while tokenized equities have done $3B in volume on Base since launch for non-U.S. customers.

Q3 FY2026 net sales rose 2% to $963 million, exceeding the revenue guidance, with international up 9% (China low-teens, Korea high-teens, EMEA up 7%) offsetting a 1% U.S. decline; reported EPS was $1.66 versus $0.95 a year ago. Operating margin was 11.4%, up 120 bps on an underlying basis, though reported gross margin slipped 20 bps to 49.8% including a 50 bp factory accommodation headwind. Q4 revenue is guided up 3.5%-7% and EPS $1.85-$2.10, bringing full-year sales to up 2%-3% and EPS to $4.65-$4.90, with full-year gross margin of 52.1%-52.3% and operating margin of 8.7%-9.1%. Management flagged a weak Mountain Hardwear (down 17%) and a challenging China macro, but cited a strengthening spring 2027 order book and mid-single-digit first-half 2027 wholesale growth as key positive signals.

Vulcan Materials reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $707 million, representing a 5% year-over-year growth in underlying business excluding approximately $40 million in energy headwinds and prior divestitures. Management maintained full-year guidance near the midpoint despite these headwinds, citing resilient execution and disciplined cost control. The company closed on two bolt-on acquisitions during the quarter and expects to complete several more before year-end.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $377M, up 94% as reported on the Udemy acquisition but down about 3% on a normalized basis; adjusted EBITDA was nearly $62M (16.3% margin, up over 800 bps YoY) and net income was $57M. Enterprise grew 2% normalized with NRR of 93% and customers down 4%, while consumer fell 9% normalized on softer funnel and transactional pressure. Q4 revenue is guided to $358-366M with enterprise roughly flat and consumer decelerating further; the full-year outlook was narrowed within the prior range and the ~14% adjusted EBITDA margin target maintained, but a directional 2027 baseline frames enterprise flat-to-down and consumer down low double digits. Management declined to give 2027 EBITDA margin guidance or Helix pricing, and said no Helix revenue is assumed for 2027, while integration savings accelerated to more than $150M in annualized gross savings by year-end against a $115M net synergy target.

CRH reported Q3 2026 revenue of $11.4 billion, up 3% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $2.7 billion essentially flat versus the prior year as the margin contracted 80 basis points to approximately 24%. Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was updated to a range of $7.8 billion to $8.0 billion, reflecting softer residential activity, elevated energy and haulage cost inflation, and a partial Arcosa contribution. Management pointed to cost recovery actions, a $6 billion buyback through 2030, a 5% dividend increase to $0.39 per share, and expects positive price-cost spread with margin expansion in 2027.

Coastal returned to profitability in Q3 FY2026 with net income of $13.8 million ($0.89 per diluted share), versus a $42.1 million net loss ($2.76) in Q2 and $13.6 million ($0.88) a year ago. BaaS program fee income rose 17.6% QoQ and 79.6% YoY to $14.1 million, but net interest income fell 1.2% QoQ to $88.3 million and NIM compressed to 6.59% from 7.27% on loan mix. The prior quarter's single-partner credit issue drove a $46 million provision (largely offset by $41.8 million of credit enhancement income), and management disclosed over $20 million of potential annualized non-interest expense savings targeted over four to six quarters without formal guidance. Bluevine's pending acquisition by Valley National adds a deposit transition, with $452.4 million on-balance-sheet and $1.85 billion swept deposits, which management said will not materially affect liquidity.

Caterpillar reported Q3 FY2026 sales and revenues of $20.7 billion, up 17% YoY and in line with expectations, with adjusted EPS of $7.20 up 45% and adjusted operating margin of 20.6%, up 310 bps. Backlog hit a record $78 billion, up about 96% YoY, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of sequential growth across all three primary segments. Full-year guidance was maintained: sales growth in the mid-to-high teens, adjusted operating margin near the bottom of the target range excluding IEEPA recoveries, and MP&E free cash flow in the top half of the $6-15 billion range; Q4 is guided to only moderate sales growth against a tough comp with a roughly $1 billion Construction Industries dealer destock headwind. Resource Industries sales to users rose just 4%, below expectations on mining shipping and commissioning delays, and Power & Energy capacity expansion remains the pacing factor for growth.

Q3 revenue grew 5% to $841M with adjusted EPS up 15% to $1.80, and Back-Up Care rose 13% to $286M, but Full Service grew only 1.3% to $522M on a 50 bps enrollment decline (ex-Australia) and ~100 bps Australia headwind. Guidance was cut, with total revenue now ~$3.07B and adjusted EPS $4.98-$5.03 versus the prior outlook, and Q4 revenue guided to $730-740M with EPS of $1.14-$1.19. The company booked a $290M non-cash goodwill impairment plus $4M intangible impairment tied to the international full-service unit (Australia), and management flagged softer-than-expected fall new-family starts, largely in the U.K. where a regulator notice extended a review period.

Carrier reported 12% reported and 15% organic sales growth, adjusted operating margin expansion of 260 bps, and adjusted EPS up 30% (or ~15% excluding IEEPA refunds), with ~$700M free cash flow in Q3 and $1.5B year-to-date. Full-year organic growth guidance was raised to ~10% on sales of nearly $24B (from a little over $23B), with adjusted EPS of $2.85-$2.90 and no change to adjusted operating profit, free cash flow, or buyback outlook. However, the CSA segment operating margin outlook was cut to ~19% on lower-than-expected price realization (low-single-digit vs. mid-single-digit expected) plus higher input costs and supply chain challenges, and an impairment was booked on Climate Solutions Europe. Data center demand is the standout: orders up 300%, year-to-date orders over $3B, record backlog above $8.5B, and a new >$3B hyperscaler agreement with minimum volume commitments.

Q3 FY2026 revenue of $32.6 million rose 52% year over year and beat the top end of guidance by 9%, driven by Embedded revenue of $11.1 million (up over 1,000% on the Midjourney, Merge Labs, and Bridge Neurotech partnerships). Adjusted gross margin reached a record 73% versus 64% a year ago (a 913 bp increase), and the Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 85% to $1.2 million. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to $123-126 million in revenue (from a prior range $4 million higher at the bottom and $3 million higher at the top) and to an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $12-15 million, an $8 million improvement at the bottom. The main soft spot was international revenue, down 5% to $5.1 million, with management attributing it to deal timing shifts and partner inventory work-through; Core POCUS grew 5%.

Bunge reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.56 versus $2.27 a year ago and adjusted segment EBIT of $997 million versus $924 million, with GAAP EPS of $1.64 versus $0.86. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was maintained at $9.25-$9.75, with soybean processing and refining plus tropical oils and specialty ingredients now forecast slightly lower and grain merchandising and milling higher. Net interest expense guidance rose to $640-$670 million from $620-$660 million and CapEx is now expected toward the high end of $1.5-$1.7 billion. Management flagged no meaningful 2026 contribution from the four major projects and pointed to roughly $0.50 per share each in 2027 from project ramp and incremental cost synergies, with cost savings tracking just above $200 million for 2026 versus the prior $190 million target.

Third quarter revenue was $1.15 billion at the high end of guidance, while Adjusted EBITDA of $123 million and non-GAAP EPS of $1.01 both exceeded the top end of guidance. Management raised full-year outlooks for Brigit revenue growth to approximately 35% and narrowed ranges across all consolidated metrics including EPS. The company generated $121 million in free cash flow, more than double the prior year, while reducing net leverage to 2.4 times.

Univest reported Q3 net income of $21.6 million ($0.78/share), which was negatively impacted by a $14.4 million charge-off on a commercial lending relationship. Excluding this one-off, core operations remained solid with fee income up 6.3% and NII growing 10.5% YoY, though the company maintained its full-year loan growth guidance of 2%-3% despite a shift in lending philosophy that reduced mortgage and CRE holdings.

Net sales fell ~2% to $3.9 billion as core organic single-family sales declined 6%, outweighing acquisition growth; gross margin contracted 260 bps to 27.8% and adjusted EBITDA fell 28% to $311 million (8.1% margin, down 290 bps), with adjusted EPS down 25% to $1.51. Management maintained the midpoints of its 2026 net sales ($14.2-14.6B) and adjusted EBITDA ($1.075-1.125B) outlook while narrowing the ranges, and kept gross margin at 27.5-28.5% and free cash flow near $400-450 million. Cash flow weakened sharply — operating cash flow of $147 million versus $548 million a year prior and $76 million of free cash flow — net debt/EBITDA stood at ~4.1x, and no shares were repurchased in the quarter. Management flagged weak fall demand, noted some builders may slow starts further, and repeatedly stressed that its 2027 sensitivity scenarios are not guidance, with Q4 gross margin expected down slightly from Q3.

Total revenue grew 4.7% to $790 million driven by organic growth of 4%, while Adjusted EBITDAC margin declined 30 bps to 30.9%. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDAC margin guidance from a projected decline of 50-100 bps to a modest decline, citing disciplined cost management and talent investment absorption. Forward outlook remains cautious with expectations for continued property pricing deterioration in Q4 and into 2027, alongside intensified competition in casualty and binding authority.

VICI reported Q3 FY2026 AFFO per share of $0.62, a 4.3% increase year-over-year, driven by a 5.8% revenue growth and successful refinancing that reduced the all-in interest rate by nearly 15 basis points. Management raised full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to between $2.47 and $2.48 per share, citing strong underlying demand in Las Vegas and continued portfolio diversification with four new tenants added in 2026. The company also announced a new $2 billion stock buyback authorization as a capital allocation tool.

AFFO of $0.39/share rose 5.4% YoY and full-year 2026 AFFO guidance of $1.55-$1.57 was reaffirmed (midpoint $1.56, ~5% growth), with the investment range raised to $700-800M and dispositions to $150-200M. Same-store rental revenue grew only 0.7% YoY, or ~1.9% excluding two industrial properties now under redevelopment. The $456M build-to-suit pipeline (~$306M remaining) is expected to add ~$36M of annualized base rent by end-2027, while management flagged a ~25-50 bp rise in cap rate expectations, tenants taking longer to commit, and ~10-15% higher construction costs. Leverage fell to 5.4x from 5.9x on a $409M unsettled forward equity raise, and the dividend was raised 1% to $0.295.

OneSpan reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $63.9 million, a 12% year-over-year increase driven by double-digit growth in both Cybersecurity (11%) and Digital Agreements (14%). The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue to $254-$258 million from the prior range of $248-$252 million, citing strong Q3 results and updated expectations. Gross margin expanded to 76.3%, and management highlighted a shift in mix toward higher-margin software and services.

BUD reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 4.9% with revenue per hectoliter +4.2%, volumes +0.4%, EBITDA +3.9% at flattish margins, EBIT +6%, and underlying EPS +22% to $1.21 ($1.21 dollar EPS, +13.9% at constant currency). Management said it remains confident in delivering the 2026 outlook and repeated a balanced first-half/second-half shape, but gave no 2027 guidance beyond the mid-term EBIT 5-9% framework. The quarter was two-sided: Middle Americas and other markets grew strongly (Mexico mid-single-digit volume, Colombia double-digit, non-alcohol revenue +35%, BEES GMV $15.9bn +12%), while China revenue and volumes fell 16.8% against an industry down low-to-high-teens in its footprint, with inventory adjustment adding to the decline. Interim dividend was raised to EUR 0.40 from EUR 0.15, and $2.6bn of the $6bn buyback has been executed.

BorgWarner reported Q3 sales just under $3.5B, down from $3.6B a year ago, with organic sales down 1.6% roughly in line with market production but including a $54M battery-segment headwind. Adjusted operating margin expanded 20 bps to 10.9% on $381M adjusted operating income, and adjusted EPS rose 12% ($0.15) to a level supported by lower taxes and ~$725M of trailing buybacks; free cash flow was $195M. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed at the top end to $14.0-14.2B from $14.0-14.3B, the 10.7-10.9% margin range was maintained, and adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.20-5.35 from $5.05-5.30, driven by buybacks and a lower tax rate rather than operations. Light vehicle eProduct sales grew 33% to $630M on European strength, while the data center turbine generator remains on track for year-end production trials and $300M of 2027 revenue.

Bankwell reported record GAAP net income of $12.7 million, or $1.58 per share, versus $12.4 million and $1.52 in Q2, despite $3 million of pre-tax core conversion costs; operating net income was $15 million, or $1.86 per share. NIM expanded 13 bps to 3.71% for a third consecutive quarter, non-interest income rose 21% to $4 million on record $2.8 million SBA gain-on-sale, and NPAs fell 26 bps to 20 bps of assets after watching the largest legacy problem credit. Management raised full-year net interest income guidance to $119-121 million from $115-117 million and non-interest income guidance to $14-15 million from $12-13 million, while keeping loan growth at 5-7% and operating expense at $65-67 million.

BXMT reported a Q3 GAAP net loss of $1.95/share with DE of $0.38/share and DE prior to realized gains/losses of $0.42/share, down $0.06 QoQ (including a $0.04 tax benefit). Book value fell 12% to $17.06/share, driven by a $1.59/share increase in CECL reserves tied mostly to impairments of roughly $800 million of legacy office and one hotel loan among six watchlist loans. The board cut the quarterly dividend to $0.30 from $0.47 and management guided to near-term earnings pressure, though it expects the new dividend to be covered in Q4 and full year 2027. The company sold nearly $1 billion of loans at ~$0.93 on the dollar and cut its watchlist ~60% QoQ, while deploying only ~$500 million of new investments.

Originations accelerated sharply: consumer loan assignment unit volume rose 38% YoY to over 110,000 loans and dollar volume rose 51% to $1.4 billion, the first YoY growth since Q4 2024, with a record 12,093 active dealers (up 19%) and volume per dealer up 15%. But the company recorded a GAAP net loss of $56.6 million (-$5.43 per diluted share) versus $108.2 million of net income ($9.43) a year ago, driven by a $291 million (2.5%) reduction in forecasted net cash flows for 2022-2026 vintages, more than four times the $59 million prior-year adjustment. Adjusted net income was $135.5 million ($13.01 per share), up 15% and 27% respectively, and economic profit rose 18% to $50.7 million ($4.87 per share, up 30%). Management guided that the revised collection rate for 2025-2026 vintages is about 65% and that the impact will be realized over the life of the loans; operating expenses fell 10% ($14.2 million) with headcount cut about 6%, $161.6 million of buybacks retired 2.6% of shares, and the New York and multi-state matters were settled with no material expected effect on growth strategy.

Vista reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.23 billion (up 75% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $841 million (up 78% YoY), driven by record production of 169,000 BOE/d (up 33% YoY). Management raised its 2027 production guidance to 185,000 barrels per day and reiterated a full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $3.3 billion at $80 Brent. The company strengthened its balance sheet with net leverage at 1.12x adjusted EBITDA and executed $55 million in share buybacks.

Silicon Motion reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $560 million, beating the high end of its guidance range of $519-$541 million, with gross margins expanding to 53.7%. The company delivered record earnings per ADS and raised full-year 2026 guidance, projecting sequential revenue growth of 5%-10% for Q4 and top-line doubling for the year. Management highlighted strong momentum in automotive, enterprise boot drives, and MonTitan enterprise SSDs, while noting headwinds in consumer markets.

Rivian reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.155 billion, a 38% year-over-year increase driven by record R2 deliveries which became the best-watching vehicle volume-wise. Consolidated gross margin was 8%, with automotive gross profit improving to a loss of $80 million from a prior quarter's $130 million loss due to higher volumes and regulatory credits. Management raised full-year delivery guidance to 67,000-70,000 units and lowered 2026 CapEx guidance by $300 million at the midpoint.

Sirius XM reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of approximately $2.2 billion (essentially unchanged YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $694 million, a 3% increase with margin expansion to 32%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($8.55B), adjusted EBITDA ($2.65B), and free cash flow ($1.4B) by $25 million, citing improved subscriber performance and operating efficiencies despite headwinds from elevated memory costs in equipment revenue.

Sterling Infrastructure reported exceptional Q3 FY2026 results with revenue surging 127% YoY to $4.63 billion and adjusted diluted EPS reaching $7.58, an 118% increase. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($4.63B-$4.73B), adjusted diluted EPS ($21.70-$21.96), and EBITDA ($970M-$981M). The company highlighted a total scoped work of nearly $8 billion, up 90% YoY, driven by strong demand in data centers, semiconductors, and energy infrastructure.

Teck reported strong Q3 FY2026 results with adjusted EBITDA doubling to CAD 2.3 billion and cash flow from operations reaching CAD 1.6 billion, driven by record copper prices averaging $6.40/lb and an impairment reversal of CAD 888 million at Trail Operations. Management lowered 2026 net cash unit cost guidance for both copper and zinc segments due to strong performance but maintained unchanged annual production guidance despite severe weather disruptions at Quebrada Blanca (QB) and a labor strike at Highland Valley. The company reiterated its merger timeline with Anglo American, expecting completion within 12-18 months of the September 2025 announcement.

Trane Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 enterprise organic revenue growth of 16% and adjusted EPS growth of 25% (excluding a $0.10 tax benefit). Management raised its full-year organic revenue guidance to approximately 11% while reaffirming the EPS range of $15.20-$15.30, citing robust backlog and strong pipeline. The quarter was driven by exceptional performance in Americas Commercial HVAC and Applied Solutions, though price realization faced some headwinds from timing and mix.

Pitney Bowes delivered strong Q3 FY2026 results with year-over-year improvements in EPS, adjusted EBIT, and adjusted free cash flow despite increased investment. Management raised the midpoints of revenue and adjusted free cash flow guidance based on these results and the volume tailwind from PCI's exit. The company is pivoting to a growth phase with increased CapEx and investment, acknowledging short-term transition costs.

Hippo reported Q3 FY2026 gross written premium of $498 million, up 60% year-over-year, with net written premium up 26% to $149 million, revenue up 29% to $156 million, and adjusted net income up 9% to $20 million ($0.74 per diluted share). The combined ratio improved 1 point to 98.4%, and net income was $9 million ($0.33 per diluted share), down $89 million year-over-year due to a $91 million prior-year gain on sale. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across the board: GWP to $1.7-$1.75 billion, revenue to $585-$590 million, adjusted net income to $77-$80 million, and lowered the combined ratio range to 97%-98% (from 99%-101%). The company also announced a partnership with Greenlight Re to act as a preferred program carrier for emerging MGAs.

PBF Energy reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $12.78 per share and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $2.3 billion, driven by strong product markets and full system availability following turnarounds. The company reduced net debt by more than $1.2 billion during the quarter and raised its quarterly dividend by 18%. Management provided Q4 throughput guidance of 925,000-985,000 bbl per day and maintained 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $825 million to $875 million.

Stryker reported Q3 FY2026 organic sales growth of 7.7%, with Adjusted EPS of $3.52 (up 10.3% YoY) and Adjusted Gross Margin expanding 40 bps to 65.4%. Management acknowledged that overall results fell short of expectations due to a market slowdown in hip and knee procedures, supply disruptions in peripheral vascular, and operational distractions from a cyber incident and SAP implementation. Consequently, the company revised its full-year guidance downward to expect organic net sales growth of 6.5%-7% and Adjusted EPS of $14.80-$14.90.

TotalEnergies reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with adjusted net income of $9.1 billion and cash flow of $12.3 billion, driven by record refining margins averaging $33/barrel and high commodity prices. Management raised full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance to a range of $42-$43 billion and confirmed the interim dividend at EUR 0.90/share while reiterating a commitment to return 40% of cash flow to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.

Supernus reported record Q3 2026 total revenue of $226.8 million, an 18% increase year-over-year, driven by growth products like Qelbree (net sales $91M) and ZURZUVAE ($42M collaboration revenue). The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue to $875-$900 million (from $860-$890 million) and non-GAAP operating earnings to $160-$180 million (from $150-$180 million). Management highlighted strong demand across the portfolio, including a 43% growth in combined revenues for key products, and confirmed the merger with Indivior is expected to close on November 2nd.

Patrick Industries reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated net sales of $975 million, essentially flat year-over-year, driven by strong growth in Marine (+14%) and Powersports (+30%) that offset a significant decline in RV revenue (-37%). Adjusted EPS was $1.03, slightly beating the prior year's $1.01, while reported EPS missed at $0.64 due to accounting dilution. Management maintained a cautious outlook for 2026, forecasting flat-to-down retail shipments in RV and Marine, with full-year adjusted operating margin expected to be flat versus 2025.

Ranpak reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated net revenue growth of 3.4% on a constant currency basis (up 3.8% excluding warrants), driven by strong automation sales which grew 26.9% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA increased $1.1 million to $22.5 million reported, or 6.1% in constant currency terms. Management noted that while Europe and APAC volumes were softer due to channel inventory normalization and macro volatility, North America performance remained robust with a 6.9% revenue increase.

LENZ reported Q3 FY2026 total product revenue of $2.6 million plus $0.8 million in license revenue from Arrotex, with over 38,000 paid scripts, representing roughly 50-51% sequential growth over Q2 and a gross-to-net of about 93%. SG&A fell 10% sequentially to $35.8 million, R&D was zero, net loss was $31 million ($0.99 per share), and the company ended the quarter with $197.3 million in cash. Management announced a consumer-marketing-led reorganization cutting headcount to about 40 employees and reducing 2027 operating expenses to $70-75 million (over 50% lower), alongside the CEO's departure effective December 1, 2026, with the CFO becoming interim CEO. No revenue or cash runway guidance was provided, and profitability timing was not addressed.

Blue Owl reported fee-related earnings (FRE) of $0.27 per share and distributable earnings (DE) of $0.24 per share for Q3 FY2026, representing 15% and 14% growth over the last 12 months respectively. The company raised a record $12.6 billion in total capital during the quarter, bringing the last 12-month total to $49 billion, with institutional and insurance investors driving nearly three-quarters of equity raises. Management reaffirmed confidence in beating full-year guidance of $1.02 FRE and $0.89 DE per share, citing strong fundraising momentum and a robust pipeline.

WEC Energy Group reported Q3 FY2026 earnings of $1.18 per share, a beat driven by warmer weather and rate-based growth. Management raised and narrowed full-year 2026 EPS guidance to a range of $5.60-$5.64, assuming normal weather for the remainder of the year. The company unveiled an updated five-year capital plan increasing total investment to $47.5 billion (2027-2031), primarily driven by new demand from very large customers like Microsoft and Oracle.

Tradeweb reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $585 million, a 14.9% year-over-year increase, marking the second-highest quarterly revenue in company history. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded by 57 basis points to 54.5%, driven by strong growth across rates (18%), credit, and equities despite higher interest rate volatility. Management raised adjusted expense guidance for FY2026 to $1.155-$1.175 billion while maintaining a positive outlook on margin expansion.

Acadian reported Q3 FY2026 ENI revenue of $189 million (up 39% YoY), management fees of $188 million (up 38%), ENI diluted EPS of $1.36 (up 79%, a record), and ENI operating margin of 42.6% (up ~9pp from 33.2%). AUM reached a record $239.6 billion (up 44% YoY), though net inflows slowed to $2.6 billion (4% annualized organic growth) versus $28.3 billion YTD (21% annualized). Guidance was limited to a variable comp ratio of 34%-38% and reaffirmation of the 38%-40% near-term operating margin aspiration, with management indicating it may land a bit early on that target.

Telesat reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of CAD 81 million and adjusted EBITDA of CAD 12 million, with results described as in-line with expectations. Management reiterated full-year GEO guidance but lowered the LEO CapEx forecast to CAD 1.1-1.3 billion from the prior range of CAD 1.3-1.5 billion due to a three-month delay in global service launch timing. The company maintains compliance with financial covenants while navigating debt refinancing discussions and structural declines in its GEO segment.

TriMas reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $178.7 million (up 7.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.50 (up from $0.17), driven by strong Packaging growth while Specialty Products faced temporary throughput constraints at Norris Cylinder. Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $1.60-$1.70 but modestly raised the sales outlook to 4%-6% YoY, acknowledging that margin expansion will be slower in Q4 due to ongoing operational challenges and a less favorable product mix.

Provident Financial Services reported Q3 FY2026 core net income of $84 million ($0.65 diluted EPS) and record total operating revenues of $238 million, driven by a 7% year-over-year increase in net interest income. The bank successfully completed its core conversion project and maintained strong deposit growth with non-interest-bearing balances expanding 5% annualized. Management reiterated full-year loan and deposit growth guidance of 5%-6% and expects fourth-quarter non-interest income of approximately $29 million.

TPG reported GAAP net income of $100 million and after-tax distributable earnings of $265 million ($0.65 per share) for Q3 FY2026. Management raised full-year 2026 FRE margin guidance to approximately 48%, citing strong capital formation of $42 billion year-to-date and a robust realization pipeline. The company expects to raise more than $55 billion in total fundraising for the year, driven by broad-based momentum across private equity, credit, and real estate strategies.

Pinterest reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.174 billion, representing a 12% year-over-year increase but missing the company's internal guidance range due to headwinds from European regulatory changes and cross-border seller pullbacks. Adjusted EBITDA of $339 million came in within the expected range, while Q4 revenue guidance was widened to reflect continued pressure from international factors. Management highlighted strong user growth (10% to 661M MAUs) and re-acceleration in the UCAN region despite the sequential deceleration.

PMT reported a Q3 net loss of $36 million ($0.41 EPS) driven by market-driven value declines from mortgage spread widening and rate volatility, though adjusted EPS improved to $0.35 due to lower prepayment speeds on MSRs. Management indicated the upcoming fourth quarter dividend will be reduced to maximize book value accretion while maintaining a sustainable run rate of approximately $0.30 per share. The company executed significant MSR sales totaling roughly $35 billion in UPB at fair value and increased share repurchase authorization by $130 million.

Phathom reported Q3 FY2026 net revenues of $84.7 million, representing a 71% year-over-year increase and a 14% sequential increase. The company delivered its second consecutive quarter of positive operating profit ($5.8 million excluding stock-based compensation) and generated $2.1 million in cash from operations. Management maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $310 million-$325 million, noting that gross-to-net discounts came in slightly below the guided range due to lower wholesale inventory levels.

The Hanover Insurance Group reported Q3 FY2026 operating EPS of $5.15 and net written premium growth of 3.1%. The company achieved a combined ratio of 92.3% (85.5% excluding catastrophes), with all segments delivering favorable loss ratios and strong pricing power, particularly in Personal Lines where growth decelerated to 1.7% due to deliberate mix shifts toward higher-value accounts. Management raised full-year expectations, stating that outperformance on the combined ratio will cause the full-year result to clearly beat original guidance.

Pagaya reported record GAAP net income of $50 million and network volume growth of 29% year-over-year to $3.6 billion in Q3 FY2026. Management raised full-year 2026 net income guidance for the third time this year, projecting a range of $162-$182 million despite higher rates compressing FRLPC margins to the lower end of their 4%-5% range. The company highlighted strong funding diversification with $3 billion in ABS raised and robust bank pipeline growth.

Total revenues declined 5% year-over-year to $1.2 billion in Q3, driven by lower WSE volumes despite pricing improvements. Insurance cost ratio improved to 89%, and adjusted EPS of $0.94 beat internal expectations, though full-year guidance remains unchanged with revenue trending toward the bottom end of the range.

Trinity Industries reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 18% YoY and EPS of $0.27, though operating profit declined 19% due to lower gains on lease sales and higher SG&A. Management raised full-year secondary market gain expectations by roughly $20 million to a range of $180-$200 million while holding full-year EPS guidance at $2.20-$2.40. The company reaffirmed its view that 2026 is the cyclical low for industry deliveries, with projected annual deliveries below 25,000 units.

For Q3 FY2026, Pilgrim's Pride reported net revenues of $4.65 billion, a 5.5% year-over-year decline driven by lower commodity pricing and internal supply allocation to prepared foods. Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted significantly to 6.8% from 13.3% in the prior year quarter, with U.S. adjusted EBITDA falling to $185.2 million from $479.1 million. Management noted that while volume remained steady and prepared foods grew double-digits, rising costs and competitive pressures on margins resulted in a miss relative to the strong profitability of the previous year.

PennyMac reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $29 million ($0.54 EPS) and adjusted net income of $56 million ($1.05 EPS), representing a decline from the prior quarter due to lower origination volumes in a high-rate environment. The production segment recorded a pre-tax loss of $7 million, while servicing pre-tax income was $99 million excluding MSR fair value changes. Management highlighted aggressive expense reduction initiatives targeting $160 million in annualized savings and an upcoming sale of $29 billion UPB of low-coupon MSRs to pay down debt.

AXIS reported Q3 FY2026 gross written premiums of $2.4 billion, up 11% YoY, with net income of $202 million ($2.75 per diluted share) and operating income of $229 million ($3.12 per share), producing a 15.7% annualized operating ROE. The combined ratio deteriorated to 94.0% from 89.4%, driven by higher catastrophe and war losses ($75 million, 4.6 points) and a 1.9-point rise in the insurance attritional loss ratio to 54.2%. Management guided full-year reinsurance premiums down low double digits, a Q4 acquisition expense ratio proxy of 22%, and net investment income around $200 million, while declining to provide 2027 growth guidance amid softening property and casualty markets.

Third quarter adjusted EPS of $1.06 missed the guidance range of $1.20-$1.32 due to historically mild weather reducing residential and commercial load. Consequently, management revised full-year adjusted earnings guidance down from $3.33-$3.53 to $3.18-$3.28 per diluted share.
