Despite the miss, management raised long-term capacity growth expectations for large customers to 12% annually through 2030 and reaffirmed long-term EPS/dividend growth of 5%-7%.

Tenet reported Q3 FY2026 net operating revenues of $5.6 billion and consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $1.355 billion, representing a 10% increase in adjusted EBITDA over the prior year. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $5.05-$5.2 billion, citing fundamental outperformance alongside one-time transition items from the Conifer transaction. The company highlighted strong same-store growth in total joint replacements and disciplined cost controls driving margin strength.

Bel Fuse reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $220.5 million, up 23.2% year-over-year, with gross margin of 40.9% (up 120 bps) and adjusted EBITDA of $52.5 million, up ~34% to a 23.8% margin. ITDS revenue rose 37.8% to $113.9 million on data solutions growth of ~61%, while ADRS grew 10.7% to $106.6 million, though ADRS gross margin fell to 39.6% from 41.1% on mix and FX. Q4 guidance is for net sales of $220-240 million and gross margin of 40-42%, with management citing record all-time-high bookings exceeding sales and expecting Q4 to buck normal seasonality. The company ended with $333.1 million in cash and securities, up from $57.8 million at year-end largely on the Q2 equity raise.

T. Rowe Price reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS of $2.86 and adjusted net revenue of $2 billion, representing a sequential increase but following significant net outflows of $28.3 billion driven by equity strategies and target date redemptions. Management anticipates sequential improvement in net flows for the fourth quarter as outflows moderate from Q3 levels, though they remain elevated relative to historical norms. The company highlighted strong performance in fixed income, alternatives, and its expanding ETF/SMA franchises while noting structural headwinds in active equity.

Third quarter revenue reached a record $154.3 million, representing a 14.2% year-over-year increase in constant currencies. Adjusted EPS of $0.63 beat expectations and marked the highest level since Q3 2020, driven by strong factory growth despite a sequential gross margin contraction of 230 bps due to machine upgrades and contract labor. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance from an 8%-10% range to 10%-11%, citing double-digit organic growth for the first time since 2018.

Stoke Therapeutics reported Q3 FY2026 financial results with a net loss of $73.6 million and cash equivalents plus marketable securities of $358.8 million. The company reiterated its timeline for an EMPEROR data readout in Q3 2027 and a planned NDA submission in the second half of 2027 following FDA discussions that accepted a multicomponent Vineland-3 assessment. Management expressed confidence in advancing the pipeline, including dosing the third cohort of the ADOA phase I study underway.

SkyWest reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $120 million ($3.08 EPS) and revenue of $1.1 billion, which beat consensus expectations but was impacted by a significant $13 million headwind from higher prorate fuel costs ($4.56/gallon). Management maintained full-year 2026 GAAP EPS guidance in the $10.60 area despite the quarter's miss and noted that Q4 depreciation expenses will increase due to a fleet life extension. Forward outlook for 2027 remains flat on EPS compared to 2026, assuming similar fuel costs and recognizing less deferred revenue.

STM reported Q3 FY2026 net revenues of $3.76 billion, beating the midpoint of guidance and driven by strong growth in communication equipment (64% YoY) and industrial segments. Gross margin expanded to 37.3%, up 410 bps YoY, while Non-U.S. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.37. Management raised revenue expectations for AI data centers to well above $2 billion in 2027 and reiterated a path toward intermediate financial model margins of 44%-46% by late 2027/early 2028.

Roblox reported Q3 FY2026 results with bookings coming in above the high end of guidance, driven by strong retention and engagement despite continued monetization headwinds in younger U.S. cohorts. Management raised full-year CapEx expectations to $468 million due to a shift of approximately $140 million from Q3 to Q4 for AI initiatives like Build and Roblox Reality. For Q4, bookings are expected to decline 10%-15% year-over-year, with guidance explicitly building in modest headwinds from the release of GTA.

Q3 total product revenue was ~$1.29B, up 52% YoY and 10% QoQ, with TTR franchise revenue of $1.15B up 59% YoY; however, management disclosed that expanded customer-facing teams have not yet translated into faster demand growth. The 2026 TTR guide of $4.2B-$4.5B is reiterated but now expected to land at the low end, and Q4 faces headwinds from inventory and price (Q3 had a $17M inventory benefit and $10M one-time Medicaid gross-to-net adjustment) plus potential 340B-driven ordering volatility and UnitedHealth Medicare Advantage access restrictions. Management deferred 2027 guidance from JPMorgan to the February Q4 call, citing uncertainty from the pending 340B rule. GAAP net income of $2.2B was inflated by a $1.9B non-cash tax valuation allowance release; non-GAAP operating income fell 11% YoY to $425M on lower Roche collaboration revenue.

Reddit reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $895 million, up 53% year-over-year, with advertising revenue reaching $847 million. GAAP EPS was $1.47 and adjusted EBITDA grew over 70% year-over-year to $480-$510 million for the quarter. Management noted a meaningful decline in search referral traffic due to Google's AI Overviews but emphasized strong growth in logged-in and app users, which drive over 80% of monetization.

Schneider National reported Q3 FY2026 enterprise revenue of $1.35 billion (excluding fuel surcharge), up 3% year-over-year, with adjusted income from operations rising 66% to $63.8 million and adjusted EPS reaching $0.29 versus $0.12 in the prior year. The company updated its full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to a range of $1-$1.10, raising the low end from prior expectations while maintaining the high end. Management highlighted strong pricing execution and productivity gains, though noted sequential earnings moderation due to seasonality, the loss of a large Dedicated customer, and a one-time favorable settlement impact.

SCI reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.97, an 11% increase YoY, though revenues and earnings missed internal expectations due to lower Funeral volumes, higher fixed costs (healthcare, fuel), and a shift in product mix affecting commissions. Management lowered full-year 2026 EPS guidance from a midpoint of $4.20 to approximately $3.99, citing unfavorable expense trends and volume misses that will impact Q4. Despite the miss, adjusted operating cash flow grew 11% YoY to $297 million, and pre-need Cemetery sales production grew 5%, providing some earnings resilience.

The RealReal reported Q3 FY2026 results with record GMV of $642 million (up 23% YoY) and revenue of $206 million (up 19% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 290 bps to 8.3%, beating the top end of prior guidance. Management raised full-year GMV, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA guidance, citing strong momentum entering Q4.

Third quarter revenues increased 1% sequentially to $468 million, driven by Technical Services growth but offset by an 8% decline in Wireline and a $74.5 million non-cash impairment charge related to Pintail. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to 15.3%, while management noted persistent pricing weakness and increased cost pressures reducing long-term earnings expectations for the Wireline business. Management remains cautious regarding year-end seasonality and industry improvement pace, stating they will not aggressively reactivate spare capacity until pricing improves.

Republic Airways reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $40 million ($0.85 per diluted share) and adjusted EBITDAR of $107 million. Management outperformed internal forecasts due to improved completion factors in August and September, leading to a full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDAR guidance raise to $410-$420 million (from $395-$405 million) and an expected full-year adjusted earnings above $3.30 per share.

Rocket Companies reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $2.6 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.15, landing near the midpoint of guidance in a challenging high-rate environment. The company expanded Adjusted EBITDA margins to 29%, its highest level in nearly five years, driven by synergies from the Mr. Cooper transaction and technology efficiencies. Management provided Q4 guidance for adjusted revenue between $2.1 billion and $2.3 billion, acknowledging that market activity is expected to decline significantly due to elevated mortgage rates.

Alerus reported Q3 revenue of $81 million (highest in company history) with diluted EPS of $0.76 and adjusted EPS of $0.71, up 17% and 8% YoY respectively; adjusted PPNR rose 17% YoY and ROTCE was 17.35%. Net interest income of $46.7 million fell 2.1% linked quarter (reported NIM 3.84%, down 13 bps) largely on a prior-quarter one-time recovery, while core margin improved ~3 bps to 3.55%, and commercial loans surged with ~$100 million of C&I growth. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed (mid-single-digit loan growth, NIM 3.75%-3.85%, adjusted ROA above 1.25%), though the NIM guide implies Q4 contraction from 3.86% YTD as purchase accounting diminishes and funding costs rise. Credit stayed strong with 10 bps net recoveries, NPAs at 30 bps of assets, and criticized loans down to 1.96% from 4.66%, alongside $8.2 million of buybacks and a dividend.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 3% YoY to $291 million with gathering volumes up 19% and compression up 17%, though throughput was reduced by roughly 10 BCF of curtailments in the quarter. Capital invested was $51 million and free cash flow after dividends reached $449 million, including $377 million of Clearwater litigation proceeds, which funded over $400 million of debt reduction and accelerated buybacks. Leverage fell to 2.8x, below the 3x target. Management guided to high single-digit Q4 EBITDA growth quarter-over-quarter, an all-time high EBITDA in Q4, and double-digit EBITDA growth in 2027, alongside a step-up of over $100 million in incremental capital for East Side Express and regional gas demand projects.

Rimini Street reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $112.1 million, an 8.3% year-over-year increase, with adjusted recurring revenue growing 9.8% to $410.4 million and gross margin expanding 50 bps sequentially to 61.4%. The company delivered a strong quarter driven by record SAP sales and double-digit growth in international revenue, while reiterating its fiscal 2026 Rule of 20 guidance for the full year.

Silgan reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of approximately $2 billion (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.31 (up 7% YoY), beating the high end of the estimated range. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $3.83-$3.93, representing a 4% increase at the midpoint versus the prior year's $3.72. The company expects Q4 volumes to be comparable to the prior year and anticipates organic EBIT growth in the Dispensing and Specialty Closures segment.

Adjusted operating revenue excluding unlocking rose 10% to $5.1 billion and EPS rose 22%, with ROE at 56% versus 52.8% a year ago. AUM/A reached $1.8 trillion, up 8%; Wealth Management revenue grew 13% to $3.4 billion at a 29% margin, and asset management earnings rose 18% to $308 million at a 46% margin. Management kept full-year G&A guidance (mid-single-digit growth in Wealth, flat in asset management ex-Seligman) and trimmed its share count 7%. The main negatives were a $74 million after-tax unfavorable unlocking impact, $8.4 billion of asset management outflows driven by institutional reallocations, and heavy analyst pushback on press reports of a broad advisor retention program, which management repeatedly denied exists.

Republic Services reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 8.2% and adjusted EPS of $1.94, driven by disciplined pricing and volume improvements in small and large container businesses. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance to a revenue range of $17.425-$17.475 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $5.5-$5.575 billion, citing higher fuel recovery fees as the primary driver for the increase. The Environmental Solutions segment delivered strong organic growth of 9% excluding one-time emergency response jobs.

Alignment Healthcare reported Q3 2026 revenue of ~$1.4B (+37% YoY) and health plan membership of 301,200 (+31% YoY), with adjusted gross profit of $142M and adjusted MBR of 89.5%, 240 bps worse YoY and ~100 bps above the implied midpoint of Q3 guidance. Adjusted EBITDA of $22M was within the prior range, but the company lowered full-year guidance to at least $575M adjusted gross profit and $100M adjusted EBITDA, citing provider appeals/disputes, SNF, and catastrophic-case cost pressure; Q4 adjusted EBITDA is guided to at least negative $28M. Management called the outlook prudent, noted some cost stabilization in September and October, and reiterated a 2027 top-line growth target of at least 20%, while flagging a 3.5-star California HMO rating as a 2028 headwind.

Quad reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $587 million, which was flat year-over-year at $588 million in the prior period. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $51 million from $53 million a year ago, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA margin decrease from 8.9% to 8.7%. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance, narrowing the net sales decline expectation to 1%-3% and tightening the adjusted EBITDA range to $185-$195 million.

Combined brokerage and risk management revenue grew 18% (17% adjusted) with organic growth of 5% in brokerage and 10% at Gallagher Bassett; adjusted EBITDAC grew 25% and adjusted EPS grew 26% (37% levelizing for prior-year interest income). Brokerage adjusted EBITDA margin was 35.3%, up 200 bps headline (60 bps underlying plus AP contribution and 90 bps synergies), and risk management margin rose 90 bps to 22.8%. Guidance was maintained: ~6% full-year 2026 combined organic, ~5% Q4 brokerage organic, and an early 2027 view of legacy brokerage organic similar to 2026 with AP roll-in a modest 40-50 bp drag. Benefits came in below the September forecast on deferred consulting projects and a contingent commission true-up, offset by a strong quarter in reinsurance (7%) and U.K./EMEIA.

Patterson-UTI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.314 billion, a 9% sequential increase driven by strong performance in drilling services ($417M), completion services ($808M), and drilling products ($110M). Adjusted EBITDA was $264 million, with net income of $28 million including an $18 million one-time gain on rig sales. Management raised full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to less than $600 million (net of asset sales) and maintained a strong balance sheet with $339 million in cash.

Ambev reported Q3 FY2026 total volume growth of 0.8%, net revenue growth of 7.6%, normalized EBITDA growth of 8.9% to BRL 7.3 billion with 40 bps of margin expansion, and normalized EPS growth of 15.4% to BRL 0.28. Stated net income fell 10.2% on one-off items in the prior-year quarter, while normalized net income rose 14.3% and cash flow from operations increased 39% year-to-date to BRL 15.6 billion. Guidance for Brazil Beer cash COGS per hectoliter was unchanged at a 4.5%-7.5% increase, and the board approved a new buyback of up to roughly BRL 3 billion. Brazil Beer volume grew just 0.5% in Q3 after 5% in Q2, with market share gains and inventory described as at the right level for high season.

Stagwell reported record third quarter results with revenue of $816 million (up 10%) and adjusted EBITDA of $145 million (up 25%), driven by strong growth in Digital Transformation (+23%) and The Marketing Cloud (+108%). Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA to $490-540 million and adjusted EPS to $1.07-1.21, citing a successful pivot to higher-margin AI-based transformation software.

PTC Therapeutics reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $358 million and product revenue of $276 million, representing over 100% year-over-year growth driven by record Sephience sales of $182 million. Management raised full-year 2026 product revenue guidance to $960-$990 million and total revenue to $1.29-$1.32 billion, citing strong U.S. demand and international expansion in Japan. The company also announced the acquisition of ST-920 for Fabry disease and maintained a cash balance of $2.13 billion.

SPX Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 21% YoY and adjusted EPS growth of 20%, driven by record HVAC segment performance. However, management lowered the top end of full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.50 (midpoint $8.35) due to growth-related inefficiencies from rapid capacity ramping and elevated input costs impacting HVAC margins. Management expects these headwinds to persist into Q4 but anticipates improved productivity and pricing power in 2027.

ACIC reported Q3 2026 net income of $19.4 million and core income of $20.4 million, down $10.1 million year over year on softening commercial property market conditions. The underlying combined ratio deteriorated to 68.4% from 57.8% a year ago, while gross premiums written rose 3.2% and account retention held near 90%; adjusting for $8.6 million of E&S premium, the legacy book was down roughly 9%. Management declined to give 2027 guidance until the January investor call, but expects revenue growth next year even under a double-digit rate decline and floated a potential special dividend if no significant Q4 catastrophe losses occur. The quarter reflects a clearly weaker underwriting result, partially offset by new E&S initiatives (ACES Specialty licensing, Skyway MGA pipeline) and a 12% increase in stockholders' equity to $355.7 million.

Adamas Trust reported a Q3 FY2026 GAAP net loss of $159.1 million ($1.89/share) and a 19.6% decline in adjusted book value per share to $8.88, driven by Agency RMBS mark-to-market losses as the 10-year Treasury rose 82 bps to ~5.29% and Agency current-coupon spreads widened from 107 to 125 bps. EAD held at $0.30/share, covering an 11% dividend increase to $0.30 quarterly, and adjusted net interest income rose to $51.5 million from $50.3 million, though net interest spread narrowed to 140 bps from 148 bps. Management said adjusted book value has rebounded about 4% in Q4 through October 26 as it cut its $2.9 billion TBA short by ~76% to $680 million; no formal guidance was provided. The quarter's key change versus prior periods was a severe unrealized Agency book-value hit that management characterizes as valuation rather than credit-driven.

Agnico Eagle reported Q3 FY2026 gold production of 814,000 ounces, at the midpoint of adjusted guidance, with total cash costs of $1,133/oz coming in 1% above the top end of cost guidance and AISC of $1,648/oz. Free cash flow was $852 million, adjusted net income about $1.3 billion or $2.62 per share, and adjusted EBITDA about $2.5 billion. Full-year production guidance is now expected at the low end and costs at the high end of prior ranges, with elevated diesel adding more than $30/oz versus budget. Shareholder returns reached $478 million in the quarter (56% of FCF), and full-year 2026 returns are now expected above 50% of free cash flow versus an initial 40% target.

Albany reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $349.5 million, up 34% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $100.1 million (28.6% margin) and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.68, above the high end of its revised outlook. Results were heavily aided by the renegotiated CH-53K settlement, worth roughly $12 million to revenue and $44 million to adjusted EBITDA, plus a $33.4 million gross profit benefit; underlying AEC EBITDA margin was about 12.5% excluding those items. Q4 guidance was reiterated at $325-335 million revenue and $0.65-0.75 adjusted EPS, and full-year Machine Clothing revenue is still expected slightly down versus 2025. Free cash flow was $36.5 million versus $25.7 million a year ago, and net debt stood at roughly $343 million.

AGCO reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of ~$2.3 billion, down 8.6% YoY (8.7% ex-FX), with adjusted EPS of $1.05 versus $1.35 and GAAP EPS of $0.75 versus $4.09. Adjusted operating income fell ~26% to $137 million and adjusted operating margin contracted 140 bps to 6.1%. Management cut its 2026 industry outlook for Western Europe, Latin America, and North American small AG, and now guides full-year net sales of $9.8-$10.0 billion and adjusted EPS of approximately $5.50. Free cash flow was a use of ~$381 million through September versus positive ~$65 million prior year.

Alamos produced 119,000 oz in Q3 at $1,956/oz AISC, with revenue of $510 million, net earnings of $166 million ($0.40/sh) and adjusted EPS of $0.44; free cash flow was $76 million and the company ended with $397 million net cash. Production was in line with quarterly guidance, but the company is now on 'revised' annual guidance after the June seismic event at Young-Davidson. Island Gold shaft commissioning slipped about one quarter to mid-2027 due to a dike and additional ground support, pushing the 2,400 tpd ramp to 2H27 and lifting Phase 3+ capital 5% above the $835 million budget; PDA underground development also ran slower than planned, trimming expected 2H27 production. These delays are partly offset by record Island Gold District output of 68,700 oz, record underground rates of 1,790 tpd and Magino Mill throughput of 10,300 tpd, plus a 26% Q4 production increase expected to drive costs lower.

Third quarter revenues reached $251 million, representing a 53% year-over-year increase and a 61% sequential gain, driven by M&A activity that nearly doubled from the prior year. Management reiterated full-year adjusted compensation margin guidance at 67%, citing strong backlog growth of nearly three times last year's level and broad-based strength across consumer, industrials, energy, and financial institutions sectors.

Quanta Services reported a record Q3 FY2026 with revenue of $12 billion (up 57% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of $1.4 billion (up 69%), and adjusted EPS of $6.06 (up 82%). Management significantly raised full-year 2026 guidance, increasing the revenue midpoint by approximately $1.9 billion to a range of $41.3-$41.6 billion, while also raising adjusted EBITDA and EPS expectations. The company ended with a record backlog of $64 billion and strengthened its balance sheet with $5.2 billion in total liquidity.

Q3 FY2026 results showed 3.8% same-store sales growth and 3% net restaurant growth, driving 6.2% system-wide sales growth and 6.7% organic adjusted operating income (AOI) growth. Adjusted EPS increased 6.9% year-over-year to $1.10, supported by Burger King's strong U.S. performance and international expansion, though Popeyes same-store sales declined -1.8%. Management maintained full-year guidance for segment G&A, interest expense, and CapEx, while noting a slight reduction in expected Restaurant Holdings AOI.

SPS Commerce reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $197.6 million (4% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $70.9 million (36% margin), beating expectations despite a 500 bps headwind from the divestiture of the 3P Revenue Recovery business and lower-than-anticipated Amazon take rate revenue due to new policy changes. Management raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $267.4M-$269.4M (midpoint margin 34%) and maintained Q4 revenue guidance, stating that without the specific headwinds they would have raised guidance on the year. The company deployed $48.8 million in share buybacks.

Wesco reported record Q3 FY2026 results with organic sales increasing 17% to $7.2 billion and adjusted EPS rising 47% to a record $5.77 per share. Management significantly raised the full-year 2026 outlook, projecting organic sales growth of 13%-14%, adjusted EBITDA margins of approximately 7.2%, and adjusted EPS between $18-$18.50. The company highlighted strong momentum across all business units, with data center sales up 55% year-over-year and backlog surging over 80%.

Incyte reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $1.56 billion, up 14% YoY, with total net sales of $1.32 billion also up 14%. Jakafi franchise sales were $827 million, up 4% (demand up 12%), while core business ex-Jakafi rose 30% to $490 million and OPZELURA net sales grew 36% to $255 million (21% pro forma). Management raised full-year 2026 total net sales guidance to $5.210-$5.300 billion, along with raises for OPZELURA ($1.1-$1.12 billion) and hematology/oncology ($890-$910 million), while maintaining opex guidance. GAAP expenses rose 146% to $2.27 billion on a $1.23 billion IPR&D charge from the ~$1.27 billion Vega Therapeutics acquisition, and pipeline news included deprioritizing CDK2 667 in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (halting MAESTRA-2 enrollment).

OMA reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of MXN 2.9 billion (up 8.7% YoY) with a margin expansion to 75%, driven by an 8.3% increase in total aeronautical and non-aeronautical revenues. Management raised full-year traffic guidance expectations, anticipating low single-digit growth for 2027 with recovery starting mid-year, while confirming plans to reach 100% tariff compliance by the third year of the five-year plan.

MAA reported Q3 2026 core FFO of $2.10 per diluted share, in line with guidance, but same-store revenue came in about $0.02 light on weaker new lease pricing and modestly lower average occupancy, partly offset by $0.02 of favorable expenses. Full-year core FFO guidance midpoint was cut $0.04 to $8.49 (range $8.43-$8.55), with same-store revenue growth midpoint lowered 35 bps to -0.25%, effective rent growth midpoint cut 20 bps to -0.1%, average occupancy midpoint down 10 bps to 95.4%, and same-store NOI growth midpoint reduced 35 bps to -1.25%. Blended lease-over-lease was up only 10 bps versus Q3 2025, with new lease pricing around -6% for the quarter, though management cited improving October trends and positive November/December pre-leasing as recovery now developing roughly one quarter later than originally expected. Q4 core FFO guidance was set at $2.12-$2.24 ($2.18 midpoint).

Sandisk reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $11 billion, beating the guidance range of $10.3-$10.8 billion, with non-GAAP EPS of $49.51 exceeding the $44-$46 guidance. Gross margin expanded to 85.1% driven by volume and pricing, while data center revenue surged 61% sequentially. Management raised Q2 revenue guidance to $12.2-$12.6 billion and maintained a strong outlook for fiscal year 2027.

Allegro reported Q2 FY2027 sales of $277 million, beating the high end of guidance by $277 million (implied prior range ~$15M-$28M based on context or a typo in transcript where '277' likely refers to absolute beat amount over a much lower base, but text explicitly says '$277 million above the high end'). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.26, doubling YoY. The company raised its Q3 sales guidance range to $278-$288 million (midpoint +23% YoY) and expects gross margins between 51.5% and 52.5%. Key drivers included record design wins (+40% YoY), strong automotive growth (+11% YoY), and data center sales hitting a record $46 million.

CSW Industrials reported record Q2 FY2027 results with consolidated revenue of $361 million (up 31% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $97 million (up 33% YoY). The company raised its synergy target for the MARS acquisition to $15 million, having already realized that amount. Management noted a slight decline in consolidated gross margin to 42.1% due to freight and raw material costs, but emphasized strong organic growth across segments and a resilient repair/replace demand mix.

Pre-revenue developer with no revenue or EPS to report; Q3 balance-sheet and execution update. Cash ended Q3 at $22 million, with total liquidity of $40.5 million including $18.3 million undrawn on the Taurus bridge, available until November 29 conditional on the joint financial model and framework agreement amendment. Nine-month operating cash outflow was $7.8 million (a ~$1.3 million improvement), investing outflows $24 million and financing inflows $34 million, with no financing in Q3; E&E assets rose from $104 million to $272 million, reflecting capitalized Kabanga spend and bridge-loan interest. Management gave no numeric guidance but said it is in advanced negotiations with the Orion Critical Mineral Consortium on a just-over-$500 million equity raise into KNL, with debt project financing upwards of $800 million, commercial terms concluded and final legal processes remaining.

Lloyds reported Q3 FY2026 statutory profit after tax of GBP 4.8bn YTD on net income of GBP 14.8bn, up 9% YoY, with Q3 net income up 2% QoQ and NII up 3% YoY. NIM was 325bps, up 3bps QoQ, and the year-to-date cost/income ratio was 49.3% (Q3 47.2%) on costs of GBP 7.2bn, up 1%. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated (NII >GBP 14.9bn, costs <GBP 9.9bn, AQR ~25bps, ROTE >16%, capital generation >200bps, CET1 ~13%), with NII now expected modestly above GBP 14.9bn, though management flagged 2027 NII growth lower than 2026 amid competitive deposit and asset markets.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 55% to $62 million in Q3 2026 from $40 million a year ago, on higher watching prices and lower costs that more than offset lower volumes from the completed turnaround; TTM adjusted EBITDA now exceeds $220 million. Free cash flow through nine months was roughly $74 million after $58 million of sustaining capital, with $200 million+ of cash and ~1.1x net leverage. Management guided to another strong Q4 citing Tampa ammonia at $545/ton, NOLA UAN around $390/ton, and gas near $3/MMBtu, and said it expects to add ~$15 million of run-rate EBITDA improvement by end-2026 toward a $55 million target, plus $25-30 million annually from CCS once operational. No formal guidance range was issued.
